sundar.41.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa spoke words of right counsel, in agreement with the wise, the Purāṇas and the Vedas. On hearing them, Rāvaṇa rose in fury and said: Wretch, your death is now close at hand. ॥1॥
sundar.41.cau2: Fool, you have always lived because I let you live, and yet, simpleton, you favour the enemy's side. Tell me, wretch: who is there in the world whom I have not conquered by the strength of my arms? ॥2॥
sundar.41.cau3: You live in my city and love those ascetics. Fool, go and join them, and preach your counsel to them. With these words he kicked him, and his younger brother clasped his feet again and again. ॥3॥
sundar.41.cau4: Umā, this is the greatness of a saint: he does good even to one who does him harm. Vibhīṣaṇa said: You stand in a father's place for me; you were right to strike me. But it is in worshipping Śrī Rāma that your good lies, my lord. ॥4॥
sundar.41.cau5: With his ministers, Vibhīṣaṇa rose into the sky and went off, saying this for all to hear: ॥5॥
sundar.41.do41: Śrī Rāma is the Lord whose resolve always comes true, and your court is in the grip of death. I go now to take refuge with Śrī Rāma; do not lay the blame on me. ॥41॥
sundar.42.cau1: As soon as Vibhīṣaṇa set off, saying this, all of them were doomed to die. Pārvatī, scorn shown to a holy man at once destroys every good. ॥1॥
sundar.42.cau2: The moment Rāvaṇa cast Vibhīṣaṇa off, the luckless king lost all his splendour. Vibhīṣaṇa set out joyfully for Śrī Rāma, cherishing many hopes in his heart. ॥2॥
sundar.42.cau3: I shall go and see those lotus feet, rosy and soft, that bring joy to his servants: the feet whose touch saved the sage's wife, Ahalyā, and which made the Daṇḍaka forest holy. ॥3॥
sundar.42.cau4: The feet that Sītā, Janaka's daughter, holds to her heart, that ran over the ground after the deceitful deer, that bloom as lotuses in the lake that is Śiva's heart: what good fortune! I shall see those very feet. ॥4॥
sundar.42.do42: The feet on whose sandals Bharata has set his mind: today I shall go and behold those feet with these eyes of mine. ॥42॥
sundar.43.cau1: Thinking such loving thoughts, Vibhīṣaṇa soon reached this shore of the ocean. The monkeys saw him approaching and thought he must be an important envoy of the enemy. ॥1॥
sundar.43.cau2: Keeping him there, they went to the king of the monkeys and reported everything to him. Sugrīva said: O Lord of the Raghus, hear this: Rāvaṇa's brother is here to meet you. ॥2॥
sundar.43.cau3: The Lord said: Friend, what do you make of it? The king of the monkeys said: Listen, O king of men: no one can see through the wiles of the demons. Who knows why this shape-changer has come? ॥3॥
sundar.43.cau4: The wretch has come to learn our secrets; I think we should keep him in bonds. The Lord said: Friend, you have weighed the policy well, but I am pledged to remove the fear of whoever comes to me for refuge. ॥4॥
sundar.43.cau5: Hanumān rejoiced at the Lord's words: the Lord is loving to those who seek his refuge. ॥5॥
sundar.43.do43: Those who abandon one who has come to them for refuge, judging that he may do them harm, they are base and full of sin; there is harm in even looking at them. ॥43॥
sundar.44.cau1: Even one who bears the guilt of killing millions of brāhmaṇas I do not abandon once he comes to me for refuge. The moment a soul turns to face me, the sins of millions of births are destroyed. ॥1॥
sundar.44.cau2: It is the very nature of a sinner that worship of me never pleases him. If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me? ॥2॥
sundar.44.cau3: Only one whose mind is pure finds me; deceit, cunning and fault-finding do not please me. Should Rāvaṇa have sent him here to learn our secrets, still, king of the monkeys, we have nothing to fear and nothing to lose. ॥3॥
sundar.44.cau4: Friend, Lakṣmaṇa can kill in the blink of an eye every demon there is in the world. And if he has come to me for refuge out of fear, I will guard him as I guard my own life. ॥4॥
sundar.44.do44: The abode of mercy said with a smile: Bring him in either case. Crying victory to the compassionate Lord, Sugrīva set off, taking Aṅgada and Hanumān with him. ॥44॥
sundar.45.cau1: Respectfully placing him in front, the monkeys went to where Śrī Rāma, the mine of compassion, was. From far off Vibhīṣaṇa saw the two brothers, who give the gift of joy to the eyes. ॥1॥
sundar.45.cau2: Then, as he looked upon Śrī Rāma, abode of all beauty, he stood rooted, gazing unblinking, his eyelids held still. The Lord's arms were long, his eyes like red lotuses, his body dark, freeing from fear those who bow to him. ॥2॥
sundar.45.cau3: His shoulders were like a lion's and his broad chest shone; his face would charm the hearts of countless gods of love. Vibhīṣaṇa's eyes filled with tears and his whole body thrilled; steadying his mind, he spoke gently: ॥3॥
sundar.45.cau4: My Lord, I am the brother of Rāvaṇa, and was born in the race of demons, O protector of the gods. By nature I am fond of sin, and my body is of the dark quality (tamas), as the owl loves the darkness. ॥4॥
sundar.45.do45: I have come, Lord, having heard with my ears your fair fame, that you destroy the distress of worldly existence. Save me, save me, remover of suffering, giver of joy to those who seek refuge, O hero of the Raghus. ॥45॥
sundar.46.cau1: Seeing him prostrate himself after these words, the Lord rose at once, full of joy. The humble words pleased the Lord's heart; he gathered him in his mighty arms and held him to his heart. ॥1॥
sundar.46.cau2: Meeting him together with his younger brother, he seated him close by, and the Lord, who takes away his devotees' fear, said: Tell me, Lord of Laṅkā, how you and your family are; you live in an evil place. ॥2॥
sundar.46.cau3: You dwell day and night among a company of the wicked; how do you keep to dharma, friend? Your ways are all known to me: you are deeply versed in right conduct, and wrong does not please you. ॥3॥
sundar.46.cau4: Even a dwelling in hell is better, dear one; may the Creator never grant the company of the wicked. Vibhīṣaṇa said: O Lord of the Raghus, now that I have seen your feet I am well, for you have shown me mercy, knowing me as your servant. ॥4॥
sundar.46.do46: A soul knows no well-being, and its mind no rest even in a dream, until it gives up desire, the home of sorrow, and worships Śrī Rāma. ॥46॥
sundar.47.cau1: Many wicked ones, greed, delusion, envy, pride and vanity, dwell in the heart for as long as Śrī Rāma, holding his bow and arrows, with a quiver at his waist, does not dwell there. ॥1॥
sundar.47.cau2: Attachment is a pitch-dark night at its height, which delights the owls of craving and aversion. It lives in a soul's mind only until the Lord's majesty rises there like the sun. ॥2॥
sundar.47.cau3: Now I am well and my great fears are gone, O Rāma, for my eyes have seen your lotus feet. O compassionate Lord, the one to whom you are gracious is never touched by the three kinds of worldly pain. ॥3॥
sundar.47.cau4: I am a demon of very base nature and have never done a good deed. Yet the Lord, whose form does not come even into the meditation of sages, has joyfully clasped me to his heart. ॥4॥
sundar.47.do47: What good fortune is mine, boundless beyond measure, O Rāma, mass of grace and joy: with my own eyes I have seen the pair of lotus feet that Brahmā and Śiva serve. ॥47॥
sundar.48.cau1: Listen, friend: I tell you my own nature, which Kākabhuśuṇḍi, Śiva and Pārvatī know. If a man who is the enemy of all creation, moving and unmoving, comes in fear, looking to me for refuge, ॥1॥
sundar.48.cau2: and leaves behind pride, delusion, deceit and guile of every kind, I make him at once like a saint. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, house, friends and family: ॥2॥
sundar.48.cau3: one who gathers up the threads of attachment to all of these, twists them into a cord and with it ties his mind to my feet; who sees all with an equal eye, wants nothing at all, and whose mind holds no joy, grief or fear — ॥3॥
sundar.48.cau4: such a good man lives in my heart just as wealth lives in the heart of the greedy. Saints like you are dear to me; it is for no one else's sake that I take on a body. ॥4॥
sundar.48.do48: Those who worship God with form and attributes, who are intent on the good of others and firm in right conduct and in their observances: such men, who love the feet of brāhmaṇas, are as dear to me as my own life. ॥48॥
sundar.49.cau1: Listen, lord of Laṅkā: all these virtues are yours, and so you are exceedingly dear to me. Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, all the troops of monkeys cry: Glory to the sum of all mercy! ॥1॥
sundar.49.cau2: As Vibhīṣaṇa listens to the Lord's words he cannot have enough of them, knowing them to be nectar to the ears. Again and again he clasps the Lord's lotus feet; the boundless love in his heart cannot be held within it. ॥2॥
sundar.49.cau3: Listen, my Lord, master of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow before you, you who know every heart from within: at first there was some desire in my heart, but it has been carried away by the river of love for the Lord's feet. ॥3॥
sundar.49.cau4: Now, compassionate Lord, give me devotion to you, which makes one pure and is ever dear to Śiva's mind. The Lord, unshaken in battle, said: So be it, and at once called for water from the ocean. ॥4॥
sundar.49.cau5: Friend, though you have no desire, the sight of me never fails to bear fruit in this world. With these words Śrī Rāma anointed him with the tilaka, and a boundless shower of flowers fell from the sky. ॥5॥
sundar.49.do49क: Vibhīṣaṇa was burning in the fire of Rāvaṇa's anger, which the fierce wind of his own breath had fanned; Śrī Rāma saved him and gave him a kingdom that would never be broken. ॥49 (क)॥
sundar.49.do49ख: The wealth that Śiva gave Rāvaṇa when he offered up his ten heads, that same wealth Śrī Rāma gave to Vibhīṣaṇa, and gave it with diffidence. ॥49 (ख)॥
sundar.50.cau1: Those who leave such a Lord and worship another are beasts without tail or horns. Knowing Vibhīṣaṇa for his own devotee, the Lord took him as his own; and the Lord's nature delighted the whole monkey race. ॥1॥
sundar.50.cau2: Then the Lord, who knows all and dwells in every heart, who is every form and yet free of all and detached, the upholder of right counsel, who for a purpose became a man and destroys the race of demons, spoke these words: ॥2॥
sundar.50.cau3: Listen, heroes, king of the monkeys and lord of Laṅkā: how is this deep ocean to be crossed? It teems with crocodiles, serpents and fish of every kind; it is fathomless, and hard to cross in every way. ॥3॥
sundar.50.cau4: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: O Lord of the Raghus, listen. Your arrow could dry up ten million oceans. Even so, policy teaches that one should go to the Ocean and make a humble request. ॥4॥
sundar.50.do50: My Lord, the Ocean is a revered elder of your line. He will think it over and tell you a way, and the entire army of bears and monkeys will get across the ocean without effort. ॥50॥
sundar.51.cau1: Friend, the way you have told me is a good one; let it be tried, if fate is on our side. This counsel did not please Lakṣmaṇa; hearing Śrī Rāma's words, he was deeply troubled. ॥1॥
sundar.51.cau2: My Lord, what reliance can be placed on fate? Dry up the ocean; let your mind be roused to anger. Fate is the one prop of a coward's mind; it is the idle who keep crying out, Fate, fate. ॥2॥
sundar.51.cau3: On hearing this Śrī Rāma laughed and said: That is just what I shall do; keep your mind steady. With these words the Lord reassured his younger brother and went down to the ocean. ॥3॥
sundar.51.cau4: First he bowed his head in salutation; then he spread kuśa grass on the shore and sat down. When Vibhīṣaṇa came to the Lord, Rāvaṇa had sent spies after him. ॥4॥
sundar.51.do51: Disguised in the bodies of monkeys, they watched all that took place, and in their hearts they praised the virtues of the Lord and the love he bears for one who comes to him for refuge. ॥51॥
sundar.52.cau1: They began to praise Śrī Rāma's nature openly, and in their great love they forgot to keep up their disguise. Then the monkeys knew them for the enemy's spies, tied them all up and took them before Sugrīva, king of the monkeys. ॥1॥
sundar.52.cau2: Sugrīva said: Listen, all you monkeys: mutilate these demons and send them back. At Sugrīva's words the monkeys rushed at them, bound them and led them round the whole camp. ॥2॥
sundar.52.cau3: The monkeys began to beat them in many ways; though they cried out piteously, still the monkeys would not release them. Then they cried: Whoever cuts off our noses and ears, we charge him by the Lord of Kosala. ॥3॥
sundar.52.cau4: Hearing this, Lakṣmaṇa called them all to him. He was moved to pity, and with a laugh had them set free at once, and said: Put this letter into Rāvaṇa's hand and tell him: Read Lakṣmaṇa's words, you destroyer of your own race. ॥4॥
sundar.52.do52: And give that fool my generous message by word of mouth: Hand Sītā back and come and meet Śrī Rāma, or else your death has come. ॥52॥
sundar.53.cau1: At once the spies bowed their heads at Lakṣmaṇa's feet and set out, recounting a tale of virtues. Telling of Śrī Rāma's glory all the way, they came to Laṅkā and bowed their heads at Rāvaṇa's feet. ॥1॥
sundar.53.cau2: Rāvaṇa laughed and asked: Śuka, why don't you tell me how you are? Then give me news of Vibhīṣaṇa, whose death has drawn very near. ॥2॥
sundar.53.cau3: The fool gave up Laṅkā, where he lived in royal state; now the wretch will be crushed like a weevil in the barley. Then tell me about the army of bears and monkeys: cruel death has impelled it to march here. ॥3॥
sundar.53.cau4: That poor soft-hearted Ocean has become the guardian of their lives. And then tell me about those ascetics, whose hearts are full of dread of me. ॥4॥
sundar.53.do53: Have you met them, or did they turn back as soon as my fair fame reached their ears? Why don't you tell me of the might and splendour of the enemy's army? Your mind seems utterly dazed. ॥53॥
sundar.54.cau1: My lord, as graciously as you have asked, so accept what I tell you, setting your anger aside. When your younger brother went over to them, Rāma anointed him with the tilaka the moment he arrived. ॥1॥
sundar.54.cau2: As soon as the monkeys heard we were spies sent by Rāvaṇa, they tied us up and made us suffer in many ways. They started cutting off our ears and noses, and only when we bound them by an oath in Rāma's name did they let us go. ॥2॥
sundar.54.cau3: You asked about Rāma's army, my lord: a thousand million mouths could not describe it. Its bears and monkeys are of many colours, with fearsome faces, huge and terrifying. ॥3॥
sundar.54.cau4: He who burned the city and killed your son has the least strength of all those monkeys. There are warriors of countless names, tough and terrible, huge and mighty, with the strength of countless elephants. ॥4॥
sundar.54.do54: Among them are Dvivida and Mainda, Nīla and Nala, Aṅgada and Gada, Vikaṭāsya and Dadhimukha, Kesarī, Niśaṭha and Śaṭha, and Jāmbavān — every one of them a mountain of strength. ॥54॥
sundar.55.cau1: All these monkeys are equal to Sugrīva, and there are millions like them; who could count so many? By Rāma's grace their strength is beyond compare; they think of the three worlds as no more than a blade of grass. ॥1॥
sundar.55.cau2: This I have heard with my own ears, Rāvaṇa: the monkey troop-leaders number eighteen padmas (a padma being an immense number). In that army, my lord, there is no monkey who would not defeat you in battle. ॥2॥
sundar.55.cau3: In utter fury they all wring their hands, but Rāma gives them no order. They will dry up the ocean, fish, serpents and all, or else fill it in with great mountains, ॥3॥
sundar.55.cau4: and crush Rāvaṇa and grind him into the dust: such are the words all the monkeys speak. Fearless by nature, they roar and threaten, as though they longed to swallow Laṅkā whole. ॥4॥
sundar.55.do55: The monkeys and bears are all heroes by nature, and over their heads besides is the Lord Rāma. Rāvaṇa, they could conquer ten million Deaths in battle. ॥55॥
sundar.56.cau1: The splendour, strength and wisdom of Rāma are so vast that a hundred thousand Śeṣas (the thousand-headed serpent) could not sing of them. He can dry up a hundred oceans with a single arrow, yet, skilled in policy as he is, he asked your brother's counsel. ॥1॥
sundar.56.cau2: On his advice he is asking the Ocean for a way across, with mercy in his heart. Hearing this, Rāvaṇa laughed: With wits like these, no wonder he has made monkeys his allies. ॥2॥
sundar.56.cau3: Relying on the word of a born coward, he has taken to sulking and pestering the Ocean like a spoilt child. Fool, why do you sing false praises? I have taken the measure of my enemy's strength and wit. ॥3॥
sundar.56.cau4: Where in the world can victory and glory be found for one whose counsellor is the timid Vibhīṣaṇa? At these words of the wicked one the spy grew angrier, and judging the moment right, he drew out the letter. ॥4॥
sundar.56.cau5: Rāma's younger brother gave me this letter. My lord, have it read out and let it cool your breast. Rāvaṇa laughed and took it in his left hand, and the fool called his minister and had him begin to read it. ॥5॥
sundar.56.do56क: Fool, do not humour your mind with mere talk and so bring your race to ruin. Opposing Śrī Rāma, you will find no escape, even if you take refuge with Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva. ॥56 (क)॥
sundar.56.do56ख: Either give up your pride and, like your younger brother, become a bee at the Lord's lotus feet, or else, wicked one, become a moth with all your race in the flame of Śrī Rāma's arrows. ॥56 (ख)॥
sundar.57.cau1: Hearing the letter, Rāvaṇa was afraid at heart, but with a smile on his face he said for all to hear: Like someone lying flat on the ground reaching up to seize the sky: such is the big talk of the younger ascetic. ॥1॥
sundar.57.cau2: Śuka said: My lord, every word of it is true; set aside your proud nature and understand it. Put away your anger and hear what I say: my lord, give up your enmity with Śrī Rāma. ॥2॥
sundar.57.cau3: Śrī Rāma's nature is very gentle, though he is king of all the worlds. The moment you meet him the Lord will show you grace; he will not keep a single offence of yours in his heart. ॥3॥
sundar.57.cau4: Hand Sītā over to Śrī Rāma; my lord, do this much that I ask. When Śuka spoke of giving Sītā back, the wicked Rāvaṇa kicked him. ॥4॥
sundar.57.cau5: Śuka bowed his head to Rāvaṇa's feet and went to where Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, was. He bowed to him and told his story, and by Śrī Rāma's grace he regained his own true state. ॥5॥
sundar.57.cau6: Pārvatī, by the curse of the sage Agastya he had become a demon; before that he had been a wise sage. Bowing again and again at Śrī Rāma's feet, the sage went back to his hermitage. ॥6॥
sundar.57.do57: The dull Ocean would not heed the entreaty, and three days went by. Then Śrī Rāma said in anger: Without fear there is no love. ॥57॥
sundar.58.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa, bring the bow and arrows; let me dry up the ocean with the fire of an arrow. Entreaty to the wicked, love for the crooked, fine counsel to one who is a miser by nature, ॥1॥
sundar.58.cau2: talk of wisdom to one wrapped up in attachment, praise of dispassion to the very greedy, talk of calm to the wrathful and the story of Śrī Hari to the lustful: all these bear the same fruit as seed sown in barren ground. ॥2॥
sundar.58.cau3: With these words Śrī Rāma strung his bow, and this view pleased Lakṣmaṇa. The Lord fitted a terrible arrow, and flames rose within the ocean's heart. ॥3॥
sundar.58.cau4: Crocodiles, serpents and shoals of fish were thrown into distress. When the Ocean knew that the creatures were burning, he filled a golden platter with gems of many kinds and, setting aside his pride, came in the form of a brāhmaṇa. ॥4॥
sundar.58.do58: However much one waters it, with endless care, a banana plant bears fruit only when it is cut. Listen, Garuḍa: the base do not heed a humble request; they bend only when rebuked. ॥58॥
sundar.59.cau1: The Ocean, afraid, took hold of the Lord's feet: Forgive all my faults, my Lord. Sky, wind, fire, water and earth, my Lord, are by their very nature dull in what they do. ॥1॥
sundar.59.cau2: Impelled by you, māyā brought them forth for the work of creation; so all the scriptures sing. Whatever the Lord has commanded for each, each finds happiness in keeping to it. ॥2॥
sundar.59.cau3: My Lord, you did well to teach me a lesson; yet the bounds were set by you as well. A drum, the unlettered, a śūdra, an animal and a woman: all of these are meant to receive instruction. ॥3॥
sundar.59.cau4: Through the Lord's might I shall dry up, and the army will get across, but there is no glory for me in that. The Lord's command cannot be set aside, the Vedas sing; whatever pleases you, I will do it at once. ॥4॥
sundar.59.do59: Hearing these most humble words, the compassionate Lord smiled and said: Dear one, tell me the way by which the monkey army may cross. ॥59॥
sundar.60.cau1: My Lord, the monkeys Nīla and Nala are two brothers who received a sage's blessing in childhood. At their touch, even massive mountains will float upon the ocean through your glory. ॥1॥
sundar.60.cau2: I too, holding the Lord's greatness in my heart, will help as far as my strength allows. Have the ocean bridged in this manner, my Lord, so that the three worlds may sing this fair renown. ॥2॥
sundar.60.cau3: With this arrow, my Lord, slay the wicked men who live on my northern shore, heaps of sin that they are. Hearing of the pain in the Ocean's heart, the compassionate Śrī Rāma, steadfast in battle, took it away at once. ॥3॥
sundar.60.cau4: Seeing Śrī Rāma's mighty strength and valour, the Ocean rejoiced and was at ease. He told the Lord all the deeds of those wicked men, bowed at his feet and departed. ॥4॥
sundar.60.cha1: The Ocean went to his own home, and this counsel pleased Śrī Rāma. This story washes away the impurity of the Kali age; the servant Tulasīdāsa has sung it as far as his understanding allows. The virtues of Śrī Rāma are a home of happiness; they put doubt to rest and destroy sorrow. Foolish mind, let go of every hope and every reliance, and sing and hear them always. ॥1॥
sundar.60.do60: Singing the praises of Śrī Rāma brings every blessing. Whoever listens to them with reverence crosses the ocean of worldly existence without a boat. ॥60॥
lanka.0.shloka1: I bow to Śrī Rāma, whom Śiva, the foe of Kāma, worships, who takes away the fear of worldly existence and is a lion to the maddened elephant of Death; the lord of yogīs, reached through knowledge, the treasury of virtues, unconquered, beyond attributes and changeless; beyond māyā (the Lord's power of illusion), lord of the gods, intent on slaying the wicked, the one God of the assembled brāhmaṇas; fair as a rain-laden cloud, lotus-eyed, God in the form of a king of the earth. ॥1॥
lanka.0.shloka2: I praise Śaṅkara, whose most beautiful body gleams like a conch and the moon, who wears a tiger's skin, who is adorned with serpents dreadful as Death, and to whom the Gaṅgā and the moon are dear; the lord of Kāśī, who quells the flood of the sins of the Kali age, the wish-fulfilling tree of all that is good; worthy of praise, the husband of Girijā, the treasury of virtues, the destroyer of Kāma. ॥2॥
lanka.0.shloka3: Śambhu, who grants the good even liberation, so hard to attain, and who punishes the wicked: may that Śaṅkara spread blessing upon me. ॥3॥
lanka.0.dou1: The instant, the twinkling of an eye, the atom of time, the age, the year and the aeon are his fierce arrows, and Time is his bow: why, my mind, do you not worship that Śrī Rāma?
lanka.0.sou1: Hearing the Ocean's words, the Lord Śrī Rāma called his ministers and said: What use is delay now? Make a bridge for the army to cross by.
lanka.0.sou2: Jāmbavān, with joined palms, said: Listen, O banner of the solar race. My Lord, your name is a bridge; mounting it, people cross the ocean of worldly existence.
lanka.1.cau1: How long can it take to cross this little ocean? Hearing this, Hanumān, son of the Wind, said: The Lord's glory is a mighty submarine fire; long ago it drank up the ocean's water. ॥1॥
lanka.1.cau2: Then it was filled again by the streams of tears wept by your enemies' wives, and that made it salt. Hearing this hyperbole of Hanumān's, the monkeys looked towards Śrī Rāma and were delighted. ॥2॥
lanka.1.cau3: Jāmbavān summoned the brothers Nala and Nīla, told them all that had passed, and said: Remember Śrī Rāma's glory in your minds and build the bridge; it will cost you no labour. ॥3॥
lanka.1.cau4: Then he called together the hosts of monkeys and said: Listen, all of you, to a small request of mine. Hold Śrī Rāma's lotus feet in your hearts, bears and monkeys, and play a game. ॥4॥
lanka.1.cau5: Run, you formidable troops of monkeys, and bring trees and mountains by the heap. Hearing this, the monkeys and bears set off with a roar, crying: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, the treasure-house of might! ॥5॥
lanka.1.do1: Mountains and trees of great height they lift as if in play, and bring and give them to Nala and Nīla, who shape them well and build the bridge. ॥1॥
lanka.2.cau1: The monkeys bring huge mountains, and Nala and Nīla catch them like balls. Seeing the bridge so beautifully built, the Lord, the treasury of mercy, smiled and said: ॥1॥
lanka.2.cau2: This land is supremely lovely and excellent; its boundless glory cannot be described. I will install Śiva here; that is the dearest wish of my heart. ॥2॥
lanka.2.cau3: Hearing this, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, sent out many messengers, who summoned all the great sages and brought them. Śrī Rāma installed the liṅga, worshipped it with due rites, and said: No one is as dear to me as Śiva. ॥3॥
lanka.2.cau4: One who is hostile to Śiva and calls himself my devotee will not reach me even in a dream. One who turns away from Śaṅkara and yet wants devotion to me is bound for hell, a fool of little understanding. ॥4॥
lanka.2.do2: Those to whom Śaṅkara is dear but who are hostile to me, and those hostile to Śiva who are my servants, dwell in a terrible hell for a whole aeon. ॥2॥
lanka.3.cau1: Those who behold Rāmeśvara will leave the body and go to my realm. And one who brings Gaṅgā water and offers it to him will attain sāyujya, the liberation of union with me. ॥1॥
lanka.3.cau2: One who serves him free of desire and without guile will be given devotion to me by Śaṅkara. Whoever looks upon the bridge I have built will cross the ocean of worldly existence without effort. ॥2॥
lanka.3.cau3: Śrī Rāma's words pleased everyone at heart, and the great sages went back each to his own hermitage. Pārvatī, this is the way of Śrī Rāma: he always loves those who bow before him. ॥3॥
lanka.3.cau4: The skilful Nīla and Nala built the bridge, and by Śrī Rāma's grace their fame shone bright. Stones that sink and drag others down became like ships. ॥4॥
lanka.3.cau5: This wonder is not set down to the ocean's credit; nor is it the stones' own property, nor the monkeys' doing. ॥5॥
lanka.3.do3: By the glory of Śrī Rāma, stones floated on the ocean. Dull of mind are those who forsake Śrī Rāma and go to worship some other lord. ॥3॥
lanka.4.cau1: The bridge was built and made very strong, and the sight of it pleased the Lord, the treasury of mercy. The army set out, beyond all description, and the hosts of monkey warriors roared. ॥1॥
lanka.4.cau2: Climbing up beside the bridgehead, the compassionate Śrī Rāma gazed at the vastness of the ocean. To see the Lord, the source of compassion, all the hosts of sea creatures rose into view. ॥2॥
lanka.4.cau3: There were sea monsters, crocodiles, fish of many kinds and serpents, with huge bodies a hundred yojanas long. Some were such as could swallow even these, and even they lived in fear of yet others. ॥3॥
lanka.4.cau4: They gazed at the Lord and would not move even when driven off; their hearts were glad and all were happy. They hid the water from sight, lost in wonder as they beheld the form of Śrī Hari. ॥4॥
lanka.4.cau5: On the Lord's command the army moved off; who could tell how vast the monkey host was? ॥5॥
lanka.4.do4: The bridge grew so crowded that some monkeys flew by the path of the sky; others climbed onto the sea creatures and crossed over on them. ॥4॥
lanka.5.cau1: Seeing this sport, the two brothers, the compassionate Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, set out smiling. Śrī Rāma crossed over with the army; the throng of monkey chiefs was past all telling. ॥1॥
lanka.5.cau2: Across the ocean the Lord made camp and gave all the monkeys his command: Go and eat the good fruit and roots. At this the bears and monkeys rushed off in every direction. ॥2॥
lanka.5.cau3: For Śrī Rāma's sake every tree bore fruit, in season or out, setting aside the course of time. They ate the sweet fruit, shook the trees and hurled mountain peaks towards Laṅkā. ॥3॥
lanka.5.cau4: Wherever they found a demon wandering about, they would all surround him and lead him a merry dance; then they bit off his nose and ears, told him of the Lord's fair fame, and only then let him go. ॥4॥
lanka.5.cau5: Those whose noses and ears had been cut off told Rāvaṇa all that had happened. As soon as he heard that the ocean had been bridged, Rāvaṇa cried out in alarm with all ten mouths: ॥5॥
lanka.5.do5: Has he bound Vananidhi, Nīranidhi, Jaladhi, Sindhu and Vārīśa? Has he truly bound Toyanidhi, Kampati, Udadhi, Payodhi and Nadīśa (all names of the ocean)? ॥5॥
lanka.6.cau1: Then, aware of his own agitation, he laughed it off, made light of his fear, and went home. Mandodarī heard that the Lord had come and had had the ocean bridged as if in sport. ॥1॥
lanka.6.cau2: Taking her husband by the hand, she brought him to her own palace and spoke in the sweetest words. With her head bowed at his feet she spread out the end of her sari and said: My love, set your anger aside and hear what I have to say. ॥2॥
lanka.6.cau3: My lord, enmity should be made only with one who can be beaten by wit or strength. And what is the difference between you and Śrī Rāma? Truly, that between a firefly and the sun. ॥3॥
lanka.6.cau4: He who slew the mighty Madhu and Kaiṭabha and destroyed the great heroes, the sons of Diti; who bound Bali and killed the thousand-armed Sahasrabāhu: he it is who has come down to take away the burden of the earth. ॥4॥
lanka.6.cau5: My lord, do not set yourself against him in whose hands lie time, karma and every living being. ॥5॥
lanka.6.do6: Bow your head at Śrī Rāma's lotus feet and give Sītā back to him. Hand the kingdom over to your son, go to the forest and worship Śrī Rāma. ॥6॥
lanka.7.cau1: My lord, Śrī Rāma is merciful to the lowly; even a tiger will not eat one who comes before it. All that you ought to do you have done; you have conquered gods, demons and all that moves and does not move. ॥1॥
lanka.7.cau2: Rāvaṇa, the saints teach this rule: in the fourth stage of life a king should go to the forest. There, my husband, worship him who creates, sustains and destroys. ॥2॥
lanka.7.cau3: That same Śrī Rāma loves those who bow before him; worship him, my lord, giving up all attachment. He for whom the great sages labour, and for whom kings renounce their thrones and become ascetics, ॥3॥
lanka.7.cau4: that same Lord of Kosala, Śrī Rāma, has come to show you mercy. If you take my advice, my love, your fair fame will be supremely holy in all three worlds. ॥4॥
lanka.7.do7: So saying, her eyes brimming with tears, clasping his feet and trembling all over, she said: My lord, worship Śrī Rāma, so that my good fortune as a wife may never fail. ॥7॥
lanka.8.cau1: Then Rāvaṇa raised Maya's daughter to her feet, and the wicked one began to boast of his power: Listen, my dear, you are afraid for nothing. Who in all the world is a warrior to match me? ॥1॥
lanka.8.cau2: Varuṇa, Kubera, the Wind, Yama, Death and all the guardians of the quarters I have conquered by the strength of my arms. Gods, demons and men are all in my power; what cause is there for you to be afraid? ॥2॥
lanka.8.cau3: He reassured her in many ways, then went back and took his seat in the council. Mandodarī understood in her heart: he is in the grip of Death, and so this pride has risen in him. ॥3॥
lanka.8.cau4: Coming into the council, he asked his ministers: How shall we fight the enemy? The ministers said: Listen, king of the demons. Why do you keep asking this, my lord? ॥4॥
lanka.8.cau5: Tell us, what is there to fear that needs any thought? Men, monkeys and bears are our food. ॥5॥
lanka.8.do8: Hearing what they all said, Prahasta spoke with joined palms: My lord, do nothing against sound policy; your ministers have very little sense. ॥8॥
lanka.9.cau1: These foolish ministers say only what pleases their master; my lord, going on like this will not carry us through. A single monkey leapt the ocean and came here, and everyone sang of his deeds in their hearts. ॥1॥
lanka.9.cau2: Was none of you hungry then? When he was setting the city ablaze, why did none of you catch him and eat him? Pleasant to hear but bringing sorrow later: such is the counsel these ministers have given their master. ॥2॥
lanka.9.cau3: He who in sport had the ocean bridged and has come down with his army on Mount Suvela — tell me, brothers, is he a man, that we shall eat him? They all talk with puffed-out cheeks. ॥3॥
lanka.9.cau4: Father, hear what I say with full respect, and do not take me in your mind for a coward. People who hear and speak pleasing words are found in crowds in this world. ॥4॥
lanka.9.cau5: But those who hear and speak words that are harsh to the ear yet supremely for one's good are few, my lord. Listen to sound policy: first send an envoy, then give back Sītā and make friends. ॥5॥
lanka.9.do9: If they get the woman back and go home, do not prolong the quarrel; if not, father, meet them face to face on the field of battle and strike them down without yielding. ॥9॥
lanka.10.cau1: My lord, if you accept this advice of mine, you will win good fame in the world either way. Rāvaṇa said angrily to his son: Fool, who put such notions into your head? ॥1॥
lanka.10.cau2: Is doubt rising in your heart already? My son, you have turned out a blight at the root of the bamboo. Hearing his father's harsh and terrible words, Prahasta set off for home, saying bitter words as he went: ॥2॥
lanka.10.cau3: How should good counsel take hold of you, any more than medicine of one in the grip of Death? Seeing that it was evening, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa set off for his palace, gazing at his twenty arms. ॥3॥
lanka.10.cau4: On a peak of Laṅkā stood a mansion, where gatherings of dance and song, most wonderful, were held. Rāvaṇa went and sat in that palace, and the kinnaras began to sing of his many virtues. ॥4॥
lanka.10.cau5: Cymbals, drums and vīṇās are playing, and skilled apsarās (heavenly dancers) dance. ॥5॥
lanka.10.do10: He lives in ceaseless pleasure, like a hundred Indras; a most mighty enemy stands over his head, yet he feels neither worry nor fear. ॥10॥
lanka.11.cau1: Here Śrī Rāma came down on Mount Suvela with his army in a great throng. He saw a very lofty peak, supremely lovely, level and especially bright. ॥1॥
lanka.11.cau2: There Lakṣmaṇa arranged and spread with his own hands tender shoots and lovely flowers from the trees. Over them lies a fine, soft deerskin, and on that seat the compassionate Lord sits. ॥2॥
lanka.11.cau3: The Lord rests his head in the lap of Sugrīva, king of the monkeys; his bow lies on his left and his quiver on his right. With both lotus hands he is setting an arrow straight, while Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, takes counsel close at his ear. ॥3॥
lanka.11.cau4: The fortunate Aṅgada and Hanumān are pressing his lotus feet in many ways. Behind the Lord sits Lakṣmaṇa in the hero's posture, quiver at his waist, bow and arrow in his hands. ॥4॥
lanka.11.do11क: Thus sits Śrī Rāma, home of grace, beauty and virtue. Blessed are those who remain ever absorbed in meditating on him thus. ॥11 (क)॥
lanka.11.do11ख: Looking to the east, the Lord saw that the moon had risen, and said to them all: Look at the moon, fearless as a lion. ॥11 (ख)॥
lanka.12.cau1: Dwelling in the mountain cave of the eastern quarter, a mass of supreme might, splendour and strength, this lion, the moon, has torn open the brow of the maddened elephant of darkness and roams the forest of the sky. ॥1॥
lanka.12.cau2: The stars strewn across the sky are pearls, the adornment of the lovely lady Night. The Lord said: Brothers, what is the darkness in the moon? Each of you tell me what you think. ॥2॥
lanka.12.cau3: Sugrīva said: Listen, O Lord of the Raghus: what shows in the moon is the shadow of the earth. Someone said: Rāhu struck the moon, and that darkness still lies on its breast. ॥3॥
lanka.12.cau4: Another said: When Brahmā made Rati's face, he took away the moon's finest part. That hole shows in the moon's heart, and through it the shadow of the sky is seen. ॥4॥
lanka.12.cau5: The Lord said: The moon's own brother is poison; it holds him very dear and has given him a home in its heart. Spreading its host of poisoned rays, it scorches men and women parted from those they love. ॥5॥
lanka.12.do12क: Hanumān said: Listen, my Lord: the moon is your beloved servant. Your image dwells in its heart, and that darkness is its reflection. ॥12 (क)॥
lanka.12.do12ख: Hearing the words of the son of the Wind, the all-wise Śrī Rāma smiled. Then, looking towards the south, the Lord, the treasury of grace, said: ॥12 (ख)॥
lanka.13.cau1: Look, Vibhīṣaṇa, at the southern quarter: clouds are massing and lightning plays. The dark cloud thunders softly, sweetly; may no storm of hard hail follow. ॥1॥
lanka.13.cau2: Vibhīṣaṇa said: Listen, compassionate Lord: this is neither lightning nor a bank of clouds. On a peak of Laṅkā stands a palace, where Rāvaṇa is watching a show of dance and song. ॥2॥
lanka.13.cau3: Over his head he bears a huge royal umbrella, dark as a cloud: that seems the black bank of cloud. Mandodarī's earrings, my Lord, seem the flash of lightning. ॥3॥
lanka.13.cau4: Hear me, king of the gods: matchless cymbals and drums are beating there, and the sweet sound is theirs. Seeing Rāvaṇa's pride, the Lord smiled; he strung his bow and set an arrow to it. ॥4॥
lanka.13.do13क: Then with a single arrow he struck down Rāvaṇa's umbrella and crowns and Mandodarī's earrings. They fell to the ground before everyone's eyes, and no one knew the secret of it. ॥13 (क)॥
lanka.13.do13ख: Having played this wonder, Śrī Rāma's arrow came back and slipped into the quiver. Seeing the revelry so badly spoiled, Rāvaṇa's whole assembly was filled with alarm. ॥13 (ख)॥
lanka.14.cau1: The earth did not quake, nor did any strong wind blow; no eye saw missile or weapon. Each of them thought anxiously within: a dreadful and grievous ill omen has occurred. ॥1॥
lanka.14.cau2: Seeing the assembly afraid, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa laughed and spoke words with a clever turn: For one to whom even the falling of his heads has always been auspicious, how can falling crowns be an ill omen? ॥2॥
lanka.14.cau3: Go to your homes, each of you, and sleep. They all bowed their heads and went home. Ever since the earring fell to the earth, anxiety had lodged in Mandodarī's heart. ॥3॥
lanka.14.cau4: With tears in her eyes and both palms joined, she said: Lord of my life, listen to my plea. My husband, give up your hostility to Śrī Rāma; do not cling to your obstinacy, thinking him a man. ॥4॥
lanka.14.do14: Believe my words: the jewel of Raghu's line has the universe for his form; the Vedas see a world in each and every limb of his. ॥14॥
lanka.15.cau1: Pātāla is his feet, the realm of Brahmā his head, and the other worlds rest on his various limbs; the play of his brows is dread Death, the sun his eyes, and the banks of cloud his hair. ॥1॥
lanka.15.cau2: The Aśvins are his nostrils, and night and day the endless blinking of his eyes; the ten directions are his ears, say the Vedas; the wind is his breath, and the Veda his own speech. ॥2॥
lanka.15.cau3: Greed is his lip, Yama his fearsome teeth; māyā is his laughter, the guardians of the quarters his arms; fire is his mouth, Varuṇa his tongue; creation, preservation and dissolution are his activity. ॥3॥
lanka.15.cau4: The eighteen bhāras of plants (all vegetation) are the rows of hair on his body, the mountains his bones, the rivers the web of his veins; his belly is the ocean, his lower organs the hells. The Lord is the whole world; why imagine any further? ॥4॥
lanka.15.do15क: His ego is Śiva, his intellect Brahmā, his mind the moon, and his citta (inner heart) the Great One (Viṣṇu); that same Lord, Śrī Rāma, whose form is all that moves and does not move, dwells here as a man. ॥15 (क)॥
lanka.15.do15ख: Listen, lord of my life: weigh this, and give up your enmity with the Lord; love the feet of Śrī Rāma, so that I am not made a widow. ॥15 (ख)॥
lanka.16.cau1: Hearing his wife's words, Rāvaṇa laughed and said: Ah, how mighty is the power of delusion! All say truly of a woman's nature that eight faults dwell in her heart always: ॥1॥
lanka.16.cau2: rashness, falsehood, fickleness, deceit, fear, lack of discernment, impurity and pitilessness. You have sung of the enemy's whole form and told me of a very great fear. ॥2॥
lanka.16.cau3: My dear, all that is by its very nature under my control; by your favour I understand it now. I have seen through your cleverness, dear: this is your way of telling of my greatness. ॥3॥
lanka.16.cau4: Your talk is deep, doe-eyed one: a joy to understand, and on hearing it fear is dispelled. Mandodarī concluded in her mind that her husband was in the grip of Death, and so his reason had gone astray. ॥4॥
lanka.16.do16क: Amusing himself in many such ways, Rāvaṇa saw the morning come. Fearless by nature and blind with pride, the lord of Laṅkā went to the assembly. ॥16 (क)॥
lanka.16.so16ख: The cane neither flowers nor fruits, though the clouds rain nectar on it; so a fool's heart does not awaken, though he meet a guru like Brahmā. ॥16 (ख)॥
lanka.17.cau1: Here, at dawn, Śrī Rāma woke, called all his counsellors and asked their advice: Tell me quickly, what plan should we follow? Jāmbavān bowed his head at his feet and said: ॥1॥
lanka.17.cau2: Listen, all-knowing one, dweller in every heart, treasury of wisdom, strength, splendour, dharma and virtue. I give my counsel as my understanding allows: send Aṅgada, son of Vāli, as your envoy. ॥2॥
lanka.17.cau3: The good counsel pleased everyone. Śrī Rāma, the treasury of compassion, said to Aṅgada: Son of Vāli, home of wisdom, strength and virtue, go to Laṅkā, dear one, on my errand. ॥3॥
lanka.17.cau4: What need is there to explain at length to you? I know that you are very shrewd. Talk with the enemy in such a way that our work is done and his good is served as well. ॥4॥
lanka.17.so17क: Taking the Lord's command upon his head and bowing to his feet, Aṅgada rose and said: O Lord Rāma, he alone on whom you bestow your grace becomes an ocean of virtues. ॥17 (क)॥
lanka.17.so17ख: All my master's work accomplishes itself; my Lord has only done me honour. So reflecting, the crown prince thrilled in body and rejoiced in heart. ॥17 (ख)॥
lanka.18.cau1: Saluting the Lord's feet and keeping his greatness in mind, Aṅgada set out, bowing his head to everyone. With the Lord's glory in his heart, the son of Vāli, a bold and formidable fighter, was fearless by nature. ॥1॥
lanka.18.cau2: Just inside the city he ran into one of Rāvaṇa's sons, at his play. Words led on to words and the quarrel grew; the strength of both was beyond measure, and both were young as well. ॥2॥
lanka.18.cau3: He raised a kick at Aṅgada; Aṅgada seized his leg, whirled him round and flung him down on the ground. Seeing so mighty a warrior, the crowds of demons scattered every way, unable even to raise a cry. ॥3॥
lanka.18.cau4: No one told another the truth of it; realising that Rāvaṇa's son had been slain, they all kept silent. A clamour went up through the city: the monkey who burnt Laṅkā has come. ॥4॥
lanka.18.cau5: In great fear they all wondered what the Creator would do now. Without being asked they showed him the way; whoever Aṅgada looked at shrank and withered. ॥5॥
lanka.18.do18: Then, remembering Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, Aṅgada came to the doors of the court where the assembly sat. Steadfast and heroic, a mass of strength, he stood with a lion's bearing and looked this way and that. ॥18॥
lanka.19.cau1: At once a demon was sent, and he gave Rāvaṇa the news. Hearing it, the ten-headed Rāvaṇa laughed and said: Call him and bring him here; where does this monkey come from? ॥1॥
lanka.19.cau2: At his command many messengers ran and brought back Aṅgada, the elephant among monkeys. Aṅgada saw the ten-faced Rāvaṇa sitting there like a mountain of soot come to life. ॥2॥
lanka.19.cau3: His arms were like trees and his heads like mountain peaks; the hair on his body was like creepers of many kinds. His mouths, noses, eyes and ears looked like the caves and hollows of a mountain. ॥3॥
lanka.19.cau4: The son of Vāli, mighty and bold, went into the assembly without the least wavering of mind. The courtiers rose at the sight of the monkey, and Rāvaṇa's heart filled with fierce anger. ॥4॥
lanka.19.do19: As a lion walks into a herd of maddened elephants, so Aṅgada went in, and, remembering Śrī Rāma's glory in his mind, bowed his head and sat down in the assembly. ॥19॥
lanka.20.cau1: Rāvaṇa said: Who are you, monkey? Aṅgada said: Ten-headed one, I am the messenger of Śrī Rāma. You were my father's friend, brother, and I have come here for your good. ॥1॥
lanka.20.cau2: You come of a noble line, a grandson of the sage Pulastya; you worshipped Śiva and Brahmā in many ways. You won boons and achieved all you set out to do; you conquered the guardians of the worlds and all kings. ॥2॥
lanka.20.cau3: Whether from a king's pride or from delusion, you have stolen away Sītā, mother of the world. Now hear the good counsel I give you: the Lord will forgive you all your offences. ॥3॥
lanka.20.cau4: Take a blade of grass between your teeth, hang an axe at your throat, and bring your family and your own wives with you; with Janaka's daughter placed respectfully before you, go in this way, putting aside all fear, ॥4॥
lanka.20.do20: and cry: Protector of those who bow to you, jewel of Raghu's line, save me now, save me. Hearing that cry of distress, the Lord will at once free you from fear. ॥20॥
lanka.21.cau1: Rāvaṇa said: Mind your words, monkey cub. Fool, do you not know me, the enemy of the gods? Tell me your name, brother, and your father's: on what ground is this friendship to be owned? ॥1॥
lanka.21.cau2: Aṅgada said: My name is Aṅgada, and I am the son of Vāli. Did you ever meet him? At Aṅgada's words Rāvaṇa grew uneasy and said: There was a monkey called Vāli; I knew of him. ॥2॥
lanka.21.cau3: So, Aṅgada, you are the son of Vāli? Wrecker of your house, you were born as a fire in the bamboo of your own line. Better you had been lost in the womb; you were born for nothing, you who style yourself, from your own lips, an ascetic's messenger. ॥3॥
lanka.21.cau4: Now tell me, is Vāli well, and where is he? Then Aṅgada laughed and replied: Let ten days pass; then you will be with Vāli, and can clasp your friend to your heart and ask him how he fares. ॥4॥
lanka.21.cau5: What sort of welfare comes of enmity with Śrī Rāma, he will tell you all of it himself. Listen, fool: discord takes root only in the mind of one in whose heart Śrī Rāma does not dwell. ॥5॥
lanka.21.do21: True enough: I am the ruin of my race, and you, ten-headed one, are the guardian of yours. Not even the blind and the deaf would say such a thing, and you have twenty eyes and twenty ears. ॥21॥
lanka.22.cau1: He whose feet Śiva, Brahmā, the gods and the hosts of sages long to serve — by becoming his messenger have I sunk my family? With such a thought in it, does your heart not burst? ॥1॥
lanka.22.cau2: Hearing the monkey's harsh words, the ten-faced Rāvaṇa glared and said: Villain, I am bearing every harsh word of yours; I know what policy and dharma require. ॥2॥
lanka.22.cau3: Aṅgada said: I too have heard of your righteousness: you stole another man's wife. And how you guard an envoy I have seen with my own eyes. Keeper of the vow of dharma, why do you not go and drown yourself? ॥3॥
lanka.22.cau4: When you saw your sister without ears and nose, you weighed dharma and forgave. Your righteousness is the talk of the whole world, and I too count myself lucky to have seen you. ॥4॥
lanka.22.do22क: Rāvaṇa said: Stop your prattle, dull brute of a monkey, you fool; look at my arms. Every one of them is a Rāhu, ready to swallow the moon of the guardians' vast strength. ॥22 (क)॥
lanka.22.do22ख: And once, in the lake of the sky, resting on the lotuses of my hands, Kailāsa, with Śiva upon it, shone like a swan. ॥22 (ख)॥
lanka.23.cau1: Listen, Aṅgada: tell me, what warrior in your army will take me on? Your master has lost his strength pining for his wife, and his younger brother is wretched and downcast with his grief. ॥1॥
lanka.23.cau2: You and Sugrīva are both trees on a riverbank; my younger brother too is a great coward. The minister Jāmbavān is very old; how could he take to the field now? ॥2॥
lanka.23.cau3: Nala and Nīla know the craft of building. There is one monkey of great strength, the one who came first and burnt the city. Hearing this, the son of Vāli said: ॥3॥
lanka.23.cau4: Tell me truly, lord of the demons: did a monkey really burn your city? A little monkey burns the city of Rāvaṇa! Who would hear such a tale and call it true? ॥4॥
lanka.23.cau5: Rāvaṇa, that great warrior you were praising is a mere errand-runner of Sugrīva's. A great walker is no fighter; he is the one we sent out to gather news. ॥5॥
lanka.23.do23क: So it is true that the monkey burnt the city without his master's leave; for fear of that he never went back to Sugrīva, but stayed in hiding. ॥23 (क)॥
lanka.23.do23ख: All that you say is true, ten-headed one; hearing it, I feel no anger at all. In our army there is no one whom it would become to fight with you. ॥23 (ख)॥
lanka.23.do23ग: Friendship and enmity are for one's equals: that is what policy says. If a lion killed frogs, would anyone think well of him? ॥23 (ग)॥
lanka.23.do23घ: Though it would demean Śrī Rāma to kill you, and be a great wrong besides, yet hear this, ten-headed one: the wrath of the warrior race is a terrible thing. ॥23 (घ)॥
lanka.23.do23ङ: With sarcasm for a bow and words for arrows, the monkey set his enemy's heart on fire, and the warrior ten-headed one seemed to pull the arrows out with the tongs of his retorts. ॥23 (ङ)॥
lanka.23.do23च: Then the ten-headed Rāvaṇa laughed and said: A monkey has one great virtue: whoever keeps him, he tries every means to serve that master's good. ॥23 (च)॥
lanka.24.cau1: Bravo the monkey, who for his master's sake casts off shame and dances wherever he may be, and with his capering wins the crowd and serves his master's turn: such is his skill in duty. ॥1॥
lanka.24.cau2: Aṅgada, your kind are loyal to their masters; why should you not sing your master's praises like this? I value merit and am wise above all, so I pay no heed to your bitter harping. ॥2॥
lanka.24.cau3: Aṅgada said: Hanumān, son of the Wind, has told me the truth about your eye for merit. He wrecked your grove, slew your son and set your city ablaze; even so, he did you no harm at all. ॥3॥
lanka.24.cau4: It was with that pleasing nature of yours in mind, ten-headed one, that I made so bold. I have come and seen what Hanumān told me: you know neither shame nor wrath nor resentment. ॥4॥
lanka.24.cau5: With a mind like that, monkey, no wonder you devoured your father. So saying, Rāvaṇa laughed. Aṅgada said: Having eaten my father I would have eaten you as well, but something has just occurred to me. ॥5॥
lanka.24.cau6: Base and arrogant as you are, I do not kill you, for I see in you a vessel of Vāli's spotless fame. Say, Rāvaṇa, how many Rāvaṇas does the world hold? Listen to all those I have heard of with my own ears. ॥6॥
lanka.24.cau7: One went down to Pātāla to conquer Bali, and the children there kept him tied up in the stables. Boys at play kept going up to him and hitting him; at last Bali was moved to pity and got him freed. ॥7॥
lanka.24.cau8: Then Sahasrabāhu caught sight of another, ran and seized him like some rare beast, and took him home for amusement; it was the sage Pulastya who went and got him freed. ॥8॥
lanka.24.do24: Of one I am quite ashamed to speak: he spent his time in Vāli's armpit. Which of these are you, Rāvaṇa? Put aside your temper and tell the truth. ॥24॥
lanka.25.cau1: Rāvaṇa said: Listen, fool: I am that mighty Rāvaṇa, the play of whose arms is known to Kailāsa, the mountain of Śiva; whose valour is known to Śiva, Umā's lord, whom I worshipped with my heads offered up as flowers. ॥1॥
lanka.25.cau2: With my own hands I took off the lotuses of my heads and worshipped Śiva, the foe of Tripura, more times than can be counted. The guardians of the quarters know the might of my arms, fool; it rankles in their hearts to this day. ॥2॥
lanka.25.cau3: The elephants of the quarters know how hard my chest is, from every time I went and fought them by force; their fearsome tusks never broke into it, but snapped like radishes as they struck. ॥3॥
lanka.25.cau4: When I walk, the earth sways the way a small boat does when a maddened elephant climbs aboard; I am that Rāvaṇa, renowned in the world for his power. Have you never heard of him, you lying babbler? ॥4॥
lanka.25.do25: You call that Rāvaṇa small and sing the praises of a man? Uncouth, puny, wicked monkey, now I have seen what your wisdom is worth. ॥25॥
lanka.26.cau1: Hearing this, Aṅgada answered in anger: Mind your words, you vile, arrogant creature. He whose axe was a fire to burn the vast, dense forest of Sahasrabāhu's arms, ॥1॥
lanka.26.cau2: whose axe was an ocean in whose sharp current countless kings drowned time after time: the pride of that Paraśurāma fled at the mere sight of him. How is he a man, wretched ten-headed one? ॥2॥
lanka.26.cau3: You crooked fool, how is Śrī Rāma a man? Is Kāmadeva just a bowman, and the Gaṅgā just a river? Is the wish-granting cow just a beast, the wish-granting tree just a tree, the giving of food just a gift, and nectar just a drink? ॥3॥
lanka.26.cau4: Is Garuḍa a bird, the thousand-headed Śeṣa a snake, and the wish-fulfilling gem a stone, ten-headed one? Listen, dull-wit: is Vaikuṇṭha merely a world, and unfailing devotion to Śrī Rāma merely a gain? ॥4॥
lanka.26.do26: He churned your pride and that of your army, laid waste the grove and burnt the city, and went away after killing your son: how, you fool, is Hanumān a monkey? ॥26॥
lanka.27.cau1: Listen, Rāvaṇa: give up your cunning. Why do you not worship Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy? Wretch, if you have made yourself Śrī Rāma's enemy, neither Brahmā nor Rudra can protect you. ॥1॥
lanka.27.cau2: Fool, do not brag in vain. Enmity with Śrī Rāma will bring you to this: struck by Śrī Rāma's arrows, your heads will fall in heaps on the ground before the monkeys, ॥2॥
lanka.27.cau3: and bears and monkeys will play polo with those many heads of yours for balls. When Śrī Rāma is roused to anger in battle and his many terrible arrows fly, ॥3॥
lanka.27.cau4: will your mouth run on like this then? Think of this and worship the generous Śrī Rāma. At these words Rāvaṇa blazed up, like a great fire on which ghee has been poured. ॥4॥
lanka.27.do27: Rāvaṇa said: I have a brother like Kumbhakarṇa, and my son is the famous foe of Indra. Have you not heard of my prowess, how I conquered all things moving and unmoving? ॥27॥
lanka.28.cau1: Fool, he gathered monkeys to help him and bridged the ocean: that is all his greatness. Many birds fly across the ocean, but listen, monkey: that does not make them all heroes. ॥1॥
lanka.28.cau2: My arms are oceans brimming with the water of strength, in which many brave gods and men have drowned. They are twenty oceans, fathomless and boundless: what hero is there who could reach their farther shore? ॥2॥
lanka.28.cau3: I have made the guardians of the quarters carry water for me, and you, wretch, recite to me the fame of a king. if he is truly a great warrior in battle, that master of yours whose praises you sing over and over, ॥3॥
lanka.28.cau4: then why does he send an envoy? Does it not shame him to make friends with his foe? Look at these arms of mine that shook Mount Kailāsa, and then, foolish monkey, praise your master. ॥4॥
lanka.28.do28: What hero is there like Rāvaṇa? With his own hands he cut off his heads and offered them into the fire time after time with great joy; Śiva, lord of Gaurī, is witness. ॥28॥
lanka.29.cau1: As my skulls burned, I saw the letters the Creator had written on my forehead. Reading there my death at the hands of a man, I laughed, knowing the Creator's word to be false. ॥1॥
lanka.29.cau2: Even bearing that in mind, I feel no fear: old Brahmā wrote it with a mind gone astray. Fool, casting off shame and honour, you speak again and again before me of another hero's strength. ॥2॥
lanka.29.cau3: Aṅgada said: Rāvaṇa, there is no one in the world as modest as you. Modesty is your very nature; you never tell your own merits with your own mouth. ॥3॥
lanka.29.cau4: The tale of your heads and the mountain has stuck in your mind, so you have repeated it twenty times. But that strength of arm you have kept buried in your heart, the strength by which you conquered Sahasrabāhu, Bali and Vāli. ॥4॥
lanka.29.cau5: Listen, dull-wit, have done now. Does anyone become a hero by cutting off heads? A conjurer cuts up his whole body with his own hands, yet no one calls him a hero. ॥5॥
lanka.29.do29: Moths burn themselves in their infatuation, and herds of donkeys carry loads; but they are not called heroes. Think it over and see, dull-wit. ॥29॥
lanka.30.cau1: Wretch, argue no further; hear my words and give up your pride. Ten-headed one, I have not come as an envoy; Śrī Rāma sent me with this in mind. ॥1॥
lanka.30.cau2: The compassionate Lord says again and again that a lion wins no glory by killing a jackal. Keeping the Lord's words in mind, fool, I have borne your harsh words. ॥2॥
lanka.30.cau3: Were it not so, I would have broken your face and taken Sītā by force. Vile enemy of the gods, I knew your strength when you stole another's wife while no one was by. ॥3॥
lanka.30.cau4: You are king of the demons and full of pride; I am only the messenger of a servant of Śrī Rāma. If I did not fear dishonouring Śrī Rāma, I would put on such a show before your eyes: ॥4॥
lanka.30.do30: I would dash you to the ground, kill your army and lay waste your town, and take away Janaka's daughter, you fool, along with your young wives. ॥30॥
lanka.31.cau1: Even if I did this, there would be no glory in it; there is no manhood in killing the dead. One who follows the left-hand path, one ruled by lust, one who is miserly, one utterly foolish, one very poor, one in disgrace, one very old, ॥1॥
lanka.31.cau2: one always sick, one always angry, one turned away from Viṣṇu, one hostile to the Vedas and the saints, one who lives only to feed his body, a slanderer, and a mine of sin: these fourteen are as corpses while they live. ॥2॥
lanka.31.cau3: Thinking of this, wretch, I do not kill you; now do not stir up my anger. Hearing this, the king of the demons, biting his lips and wringing his hands, said in fury: ॥3॥
lanka.31.cau4: Vile monkey, you want to die now; that is why you speak big words from a small mouth. Dull monkey, the one on whose strength you prate so bitterly has no strength, glory, wit or splendour. ॥4॥
lanka.31.do31क: His father, finding him without merit or honour, sent him to live in the forest. On him lie that grief, then separation from his young wife, and day and night his fear of me. ॥31 (क)॥
lanka.31.do31ख: Men like him whose strength makes you proud are many; demons eat them day and night. Fool, give up your obstinacy and understand. ॥31 (ख)॥
lanka.32.cau1: When he reviled Śrī Rāma, Aṅgada, best of the monkeys, grew furious. Whoever hears Śrī Hari or Śiva reviled is guilty of a sin equal to slaying a cow. ॥1॥
lanka.32.cau2: The mighty monkey ground his teeth and furiously struck both his great arms on the ground. The earth shook, the courtiers fell, and, seized by the wind of fear, they took to flight. ॥2॥
lanka.32.cau3: Rāvaṇa, falling, caught himself and stood up; his splendid crowns dropped to the earth. Some he picked up and set right on his heads; some Aṅgada hurled across to the Lord. ॥3॥
lanka.32.cau4: Seeing the crowns coming, the monkeys fled: Heavens, are meteors falling in broad daylight? Or has Rāvaṇa in his anger hurled four thunderbolts, that come rushing on so fast? ॥4॥
lanka.32.cau5: The Lord laughed and said: Have no fear in your hearts; these are not meteors or thunderbolts, nor Ketu nor Rāhu. These are the crowns of ten-headed Rāvaṇa, flung this way by Vāli's son. ॥5॥
lanka.32.do32क: Hanumān, son of the Wind, leapt up, caught them in his hands, brought them and laid them by the Lord. The bears and monkeys gazed at the marvel; the crowns shone like the sun. ॥32 (क)॥
lanka.32.do32ख: Over there, Rāvaṇa, in a rage, angrily told them all: Seize the monkey, seize him and kill him. Hearing this, Aṅgada smiled. ॥32 (ख)॥
lanka.33.cau1: Kill him, then all you warriors run at once and eat the bears and monkeys wherever you find them. Go and rid the earth of monkeys, and take the two ascetic brothers alive. ॥1॥
lanka.33.cau2: Then the crown prince spoke again in anger: Are you not ashamed to keep wagging your jaws? Shameless wrecker of your own line, cut your throat and die! Does your heart not burst at the sight of such strength? ॥2॥
lanka.33.cau3: You thief of women, walker on the evil path, wretch, heap of filth, dull-witted and lustful! You babble abuse as if in delirium; wretched eater of men, death has you in its grip. ॥3॥
lanka.33.cau4: You will reap the fruit of this later, when the monkeys and bears land their blows on you. Proud one, as you say such words, that Śrī Rāma is a man, how is it your tongues do not fall? ॥4॥
lanka.33.cau5: Your tongues will fall, without a doubt, and your heads with them, on the field of battle. ॥5॥
lanka.33.so33क: Ten-headed one, how is he a man, who slew Vāli with a single arrow? Base-born dullard, you are blind with all twenty eyes; shame on your birth. ॥33 (क)॥
lanka.33.so33ख: The host of Śrī Rāma's arrows is thirsting for your blood. It is for fear of that, vile demon of bitter babble, that I let you go. ॥33 (ख)॥
lanka.34.cau1: I am able to break your teeth, but Śrī Rāma has not given me the order. Such is my anger that I could smash all ten of your mouths, and seize Laṅkā and sink it in the ocean. ॥1॥
lanka.34.cau2: Your Laṅkā is like a cluster fig, and you all live inside it like insects, unafraid. I am a monkey; eating the fruit would take me no time, but the generous Śrī Rāma has not given the order. ॥2॥
lanka.34.cau3: Hearing this clever talk, Rāvaṇa smiled: Fool, where did you learn so much lying? Vāli never boasted like this; keeping company with ascetics, you have become a liar. ॥3॥
lanka.34.cau4: Aṅgada said: Twenty-armed one, I am truly a liar if I do not tear out your ten tongues. Bearing in mind Śrī Rāma's glory, Aṅgada was filled with anger, and in the middle of the court he made a vow and planted his foot. ॥4॥
lanka.34.cau5: Aṅgada said: Fool, if you can move my foot, Śrī Rāma will turn back, and I have lost Sītā. Rāvaṇa said: Listen, all you warriors: seize the monkey by the foot and dash him to the ground. ॥5॥
lanka.34.cau6: Indrajit and many other mighty warriors rose here and there, delighted. They lunge with all their strength and many a device, but the foot does not move, and they sit down with bowed heads. ॥6॥
lanka.34.cau7: The enemies of the gods rise again and lunge, but the monkey's foot stays where it is, just as, Garuḍa, men of false yoga cannot uproot the tree of delusion. ॥7॥
lanka.34.do34क: Millions of warriors as mighty as Meghanāda rose gladly. They lunge, but the monkey's foot will not stir, and once more they bow their heads and sit. ॥34 (क)॥
lanka.34.do34ख: The monkey's foot does not leave the ground; seeing this, the enemy's pride fell away, the foot held as a saint's mind holds to what is right in the face of countless obstacles. ॥34 (ख)॥
lanka.35.cau1: Seeing Aṅgada's strength, they all lost heart; then, at his challenge, Rāvaṇa rose himself. As he reached for the foot, Vāli's son said: Clutching my feet will not save you. ॥1॥
lanka.35.cau2: Why not go, fool, and take hold of Śrī Rāma's feet? Hearing this, he turned back, deeply abashed. His lustre was lost and all his splendour gone; he looked like the moon in the middle of the day. ॥2॥
lanka.35.cau3: He sat down on the throne with his head bowed, as though he had lost all his wealth. Śrī Rāma is the soul of the world and the lord of life; how can one who turns away from him find rest? ॥3॥
lanka.35.cau4: Umā, at the mere play of Śrī Rāma's eyebrow the universe comes into being and then perishes again. He makes a thunderbolt of a blade of grass and grass of a thunderbolt; tell me, how could his messenger's vow fail? ॥4॥
lanka.35.cau5: Then Aṅgada spoke to him of right policy in many ways, but he would not listen: his death had drawn near. Having churned up the enemy's pride, he proclaimed the Lord's fair fame, and with these words the son of King Vāli set off: ॥5॥
lanka.35.cau6: Until I have toyed with you on the battlefield and slain you, why should I praise myself now? Aṅgada had already killed his son; hearing of it, Rāvaṇa was grieved. ॥6॥
lanka.35.cau7: Seeing Aṅgada's vow hold, all the demons were utterly shaken with fear. ॥7॥
lanka.35.do35क: Having trampled on the enemy's might, Vāli's son, that mass of strength, was filled with joy. His body thrilling and his eyes wet with tears, he clasped Śrī Rāma's lotus feet. ॥35 (क)॥
lanka.35.do35ख: Seeing that evening had come, Rāvaṇa went to his palace in dejection. There Mandodarī once more counselled him and said: ॥35 (ख)॥
lanka.36.cau1: My husband, think it over and give up this folly; a war with Śrī Rāma does not become you. Śrī Rāma's younger brother drew a little line, and even that you could not cross: such is your manhood. ॥1॥
lanka.36.cau2: Beloved, will you defeat in battle him whose messenger did all this? That lion among monkeys leapt across the ocean in play and came fearlessly into your Laṅkā. ॥2॥
lanka.36.cau3: He killed the guards and laid the grove waste, and slew Akṣaya Kumāra before your very eyes. He set the whole city on fire and left it in ashes; where then were your strength and your pride? ॥3॥
lanka.36.cau4: Now, my lord, stop these idle boasts, and give some thought in your heart to what I say. Husband, Śrī Rāma is no ordinary king, so do not take him for one; he is Lord of everything that moves and everything that stands still, and his might has no equal: know that. ॥4॥
lanka.36.cau5: Mārīca knew the power of his arrows, yet you would not heed even what that lowly one told you. In Janaka's assembly there were kings beyond counting, and you were there too, with all your vast and matchless strength. ॥5॥
lanka.36.cau6: There he broke the bow and married Jānakī; why then did you not beat him in battle? Indra's son knows a little of his strength: he let him live, only catching him and putting out an eye. ॥6॥
lanka.36.cau7: You saw what became of Śūrpaṇakhā, and still there is little shame in your heart. ॥7॥
lanka.36.do36: He slew Virādha, killed Khara and Dūṣaṇa and struck down Kabandha as if in play; he killed Vāli with a single arrow. Know him for who he is, O ten-headed one. ॥36॥
lanka.37.cau1: He had the ocean bridged with ease, and the Lord has come down with his army onto Mount Suvela; that compassionate banner of the solar race sent an envoy for your own good — ॥1॥
lanka.37.cau2: an envoy who, in the middle of the assembly, crushed your strength as a lion crushes a herd of elephants. He whose followers are Aṅgada and Hanumān, heroes most formidable and gallant in battle — ॥2॥
lanka.37.cau3: him, beloved, you keep calling a man, and you carry the load of pride, attachment and arrogance for nothing. Alas, my husband, you have made an enemy of Śrī Rāma; in the grip of death, your mind cannot come to its senses. ॥3॥
lanka.37.cau4: Death does not take up a stick to strike anyone; it takes away his dharma, strength, intellect and judgement. My lord, one whose death is drawing near falls into delusion, just as you have. ॥4॥
lanka.37.do37: Two of your sons are dead and the city is burnt; even now, beloved, bring this to an end. My lord, worship Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, and gain a spotless name. ॥37॥
lanka.38.cau1: Hearing his wife's words, sharp as arrows, he rose at daybreak and went to the assembly. He went and sat on the throne, swollen with pride; in his great arrogance he forgot all fear. ॥1॥
lanka.38.cau2: Here Śrī Rāma sent for Aṅgada; he came and bowed his head to the Lord's lotus feet. Seating him close by with great honour, the compassionate Lord, slayer of Khara, smiled and said: ॥2॥
lanka.38.cau3: Son of Vāli, I am very curious; I ask you, my dear, tell me truly. Rāvaṇa is the crown of the demon race, and the matchless might of his arms is renowned through the world. ॥3॥
lanka.38.cau4: You flung four of his crowns; tell me, my dear, how did they come into your hands? Aṅgada said: Listen, all-knowing one, giver of joy to those who bow to you: they are not crowns but the four virtues of a king. ॥4॥
lanka.38.cau5: My Lord, the Vedas say that conciliation, gifts, force and division dwell in the heart of a king. They are the fair feet of statecraft and dharma; knowing this in their hearts, they have come to my Lord. ॥5॥
lanka.38.do38क: The ten-headed Rāvaṇa has no dharma, has turned from the Lord's feet and is in the power of death. So, hear me, Lord of Kosala: these virtues left him and came to you. ॥38 (क)॥
lanka.38.do38ख: Hearing this most clever answer, the noble Śrī Rāma smiled. Then Vāli's son told him all the news of the fort. ॥38 (ख)॥
lanka.39.cau1: When he had the news of the enemy, Śrī Rāma called all his counsellors to him. Laṅkā has four formidable gates; consider how they should be attacked. ॥1॥
lanka.39.cau2: Then Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Jāmbavān, king of the bears, and Vibhīṣaṇa remembered in their hearts the ornament of the solar race. After deliberating they settled their plan and formed the monkey army into four divisions. ॥2॥
lanka.39.cau3: They made commanders as each was fit; then they called together all the troop leaders. They spoke of the Lord's glory and instructed them all; hearing it, the monkeys rushed off with roars like lions. ॥3॥
lanka.39.cau4: Joyfully they bow their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet, and all the heroes rush on, carrying mountain peaks. The bears and monkey chiefs roar and threaten: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, the Lord of Kosala! ॥4॥
lanka.39.cau5: Though they knew Laṅkā to be a most formidable fortress, the monkeys went on without fear, by the Lord's glory. Massing like storm clouds, they hemmed it in on all four sides and sounded drums and kettledrums with their mouths. ॥5॥
lanka.39.do39: Glory to Śrī Rāma, glory to Lakṣmaṇa, glory to Sugrīva, king of the monkeys: so the monkeys and bears, the very limit of great strength, roar their lion-roars. ॥39॥
lanka.40.cau1: A great tumult rose in Laṅkā, and Rāvaṇa, in his great arrogance, heard it. Rāvaṇa said: Just look at the impudence of these monkeys. And with a laugh he called up the demon army. ॥1॥
lanka.40.cau2: These monkeys have come, driven by death, and my demons are all hungry. Saying this, the fool burst into a loud laugh: Fate has sent us food without our leaving home. ॥2॥
lanka.40.cau3: Warriors, go out, all of you, in every direction; seize the bears and monkeys one by one and eat them all. Umā, Rāvaṇa's pride was like that of the lapwing, which sleeps lying on its back. ॥3॥
lanka.40.cau4: Taking their orders, the demons set out, holding javelins and fine spears in their hands, lances, maces, fierce axes, tridents, swords, iron clubs and lumps of mountain rock. ॥4॥
lanka.40.cau5: As foolish birds that feed on flesh swoop on a heap of red stones when they see it, never thinking of the pain of a broken beak, so the senseless man-eaters rushed out. ॥5॥
lanka.40.do40: Mighty demon warriors, bearing bows, arrows and weapons of every kind, staunch in battle and countless in number, climbed onto the battlements of the ramparts. ॥40॥
lanka.41.cau1: How do they look upon the battlements? As if clouds had settled on the peaks of Meru. War drums and kettledrums are beating, and at their sound the warriors' hearts are eager. ॥1॥
lanka.41.cau2: Kettledrums and pipes sound without end; hearing them, the hearts of cowards split. Going out, they saw the throngs of monkeys and the bear warriors with their huge bodies. ॥2॥
lanka.41.cau3: They charge on, making nothing of rough ravines; they grip the mountains, break them open and make their way through. Millions of warriors gnash their teeth and roar; they bite their lips and hurl fierce threats. ॥3॥
lanka.41.cau4: On that side they call on Rāvaṇa, on this side on Śrī Rāma; with cries of victory, victory, the battle broke out. The demons hurl down masses of peaks; the monkeys leap up, catch them and throw them back. ॥4॥
lanka.41.cha1: The fierce monkeys and bears lift pieces of mountain and hurl them at the fort. They lunge, seize the demons by the feet, dash them to the ground, run off and challenge them again. Most nimble and at the height of their vigour, they spring up and, in their fury, climbed onto the fort again and again. Monkeys and bears climbed onto the mansions here and there and began to sing Śrī Rāma's praise. ॥1॥
lanka.41.do41: Then each monkey seized a demon and made off; themselves on top and the demon warriors beneath, they come crashing to the ground. ॥41॥
lanka.42.cau1: Mighty through Śrī Rāma's glory, the monkey troops crush the hosts of demon warriors. Again the monkeys climbed the fort here and there, crying: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, the sun of glory! ॥1॥
lanka.42.cau2: The demon hordes fled like banks of cloud before a strong wind. A great cry of woe went up in the city; children and frightened women wept. ॥2॥
lanka.42.cau3: Together they all heap abuse on Rāvaṇa: in the midst of his reign this man has summoned death. When he heard with his own ears that his army was breaking, the lord of Laṅkā turned the warriors back, in a rage. ॥3॥
lanka.42.cau4: Rāvaṇa said: Anyone I hear of turning his back on the battle, I will kill with my terrible sword. You have eaten all I have and enjoyed every kind of pleasure, and now on the battlefield your lives have become dear to you! ॥4॥
lanka.42.cau5: Hearing such fierce words they all took fright, and the warriors, stung with shame, set off in anger. To die facing the foe is a warrior's glory; so they let go of their love of life. ॥5॥
lanka.42.do42: Bearing many weapons, all the warriors closed in, issuing challenge after challenge. Striking with iron clubs and tridents, they threw the bears and monkeys into distress. ॥42॥
lanka.43.cau1: Umā, the monkeys, distraught with fear, began to flee, though it is they who will win in the end. Someone cried: Where are Aṅgada and Hanumān? And Nala, Nīla and the mighty Dvivida, where are they? ॥1॥
lanka.43.cau2: The mighty Hanumān, who was at the western gate, heard that his own army was in distress. Meghanāda was fighting there; the gate would not break, and it was very hard going. ॥2॥
lanka.43.cau3: Great anger rose in the heart of Hanumān, son of the Wind, and the mighty warrior roared like Death. Leaping, he came up onto the fort of Laṅkā, and, seizing a mountain, ran at Meghanāda. ॥3॥
lanka.43.cau4: He smashed the chariot, struck down the charioteer, and kicked Meghanāda in the chest. Another charioteer, seeing him stunned, laid him in a chariot and at once brought him home. ॥4॥
lanka.43.do43: Aṅgada heard that Hanumān, son of the Wind, had gone onto the fort alone; and Vāli's son, a gallant in battle, sprang up onto the fort as if it were a monkey's game. ॥43॥
lanka.44.cau1: Both monkeys, furious against the foe in battle, remembered within their hearts the glory of Śrī Rāma; the two ran and climbed onto Rāvaṇa's palace, crying out the name of the Lord of Kosala. ॥1॥
lanka.44.cau2: They seized the palace and brought it down, pinnacle and all; seeing this, the king of the demons was afraid. Crowds of women beat their breasts with their hands: Now two troublemaking monkeys have come! ॥2॥
lanka.44.cau3: With monkey antics they frighten them, and recite to them the fair fame of Śrī Rāma. Then, taking hold of the golden pillars, they said: Now let the havoc begin. ॥3॥
lanka.44.cau4: Roaring, they dropped into the midst of the enemy's army and began to crush it with the great strength of their arms. Kicking one and slapping another, they say: You do not worship Śrī Rāma; take the fruit of that. ॥4॥
lanka.44.do44: They crush one against another, and wrench off heads and hurl them. The heads fall before Rāvaṇa as if pots of curd were bursting. ॥44॥
lanka.45.cau1: Whatever great chiefs they lay hands on, they seize by the feet and fling to where the Lord is. Vibhīṣaṇa tells their names, and Śrī Rāma gives even them his own abode. ॥1॥
lanka.45.cau2: Wicked man-eaters who fed on the flesh of brāhmaṇas attain the state that yogīs pray for. Umā, Śrī Rāma is tender-hearted, a mine of compassion: the demons remember me, though it is in enmity — ॥2॥
lanka.45.cau3: knowing this in his heart, he grants them the supreme state. Say, Bhavānī: who is as merciful as he? Those who hear of such a Lord and still do not cast off delusion and worship him are dull-witted and most unfortunate. ॥3॥
lanka.45.cau4: The Lord of Avadh said: Aṅgada and Hanumān have entered the fort. The two monkeys in Laṅkā look as splendid as two Mount Mandaras churning the ocean. ॥4॥
lanka.45.do45: With the might of their arms they ground the enemy's ranks to pieces; then, seeing that the day was ending, the two leapt down, free of weariness, and returned to the Lord. ॥45॥
lanka.46.cau1: They laid their heads at the Lord's lotus feet, and the sight of such fine warriors gladdened Śrī Rāma's heart. Śrī Rāma turned a gracious glance on the pair; their weariness was gone, and they were filled with the highest joy. ॥1॥
lanka.46.cau2: Knowing that Aṅgada and Hanumān had gone, the many bear and monkey warriors turned back too. Gaining strength from the dusk, the demons rushed out, crying the name of Rāvaṇa. ॥2॥
lanka.46.cau3: Seeing the demon army, the monkeys turned round, and warriors clashed here and there, gnashing their teeth. Both armies are strong; challenging again and again, the warriors fight on and will not own defeat. ॥3॥
lanka.46.cau4: The demons, all of them dark, are mighty heroes; the monkeys are of many hues and massive. Each army is powerful, its fighters a match for the other's; showing their prowess, they battle in fury. ॥4॥
lanka.46.cau5: It is as if dense clouds of the rains and of autumn were fighting, driven on by the wind. Seeing their army waver, the commanders Akampana and Atikāya worked māyā. ॥5॥
lanka.46.cau6: In the blink of an eye it grew very dark, and a rain of blood, stones and ashes began to fall. ॥6॥
lanka.46.do46: The monkey army saw thick darkness in all ten directions and was seized with panic. No one can see anyone else, and everywhere they are crying out. ॥46॥
lanka.47.cau1: Śrī Rāma understood the whole secret, and sent for Aṅgada and Hanumān. He told them everything and explained it; hearing it, the two great monkeys rushed off in anger. ॥1॥
