lanka.47.cau2: Then the compassionate Lord smiled, strung his bow and at once let fly a fiery arrow. Light spread and nowhere was there darkness, as doubts vanish when knowledge dawns. ॥2॥
lanka.47.cau3: With the light, the bears and monkeys ran forward joyfully, free of weariness and fear. Hanumān and Aṅgada roared on the battlefield; at the sound of their shout the demons fled. ॥3॥
lanka.47.cau4: The bears and monkeys seize the fleeing warriors and dash them to the ground; wondrous are the deeds they do. Grabbing them by the feet they throw them into the ocean, where crocodiles, serpents and fish catch them one by one and eat them. ॥4॥
lanka.47.do47: Some were killed, some wounded, and some fled and climbed back up the fort. Having broken the strength of the enemy army, the bears and monkeys roar. ॥47॥
lanka.48.cau1: Knowing that night had come, all four divisions of the monkeys came to where the Lord of Kosala was. Śrī Rāma looked on them all with grace, and at that very moment the monkeys were rid of their weariness. ॥1॥
lanka.48.cau2: Over there, Rāvaṇa summoned his ministers, told them all of the warriors who had been killed, and said: The monkeys have destroyed half the army. Tell me quickly: what plan should we form? ॥2॥
lanka.48.cau3: Mālyavān was a very old demon, the father of Rāvaṇa's mother and an excellent minister. He spoke words of right counsel, wholly pure: Dear one, hear a little advice from me. ॥3॥
lanka.48.cau4: Ever since you stole Sītā away to this place, ill omens have been appearing beyond all telling. No one who turned against Śrī Rāma, whose fame the Vedas and Purāṇas have sung, has ever found happiness. ॥4॥
lanka.48.do48क: He who slew Hiraṇyākṣa together with his brother, and the mighty Madhu and Kaiṭabha — that same Lord, the ocean of mercy, has come down as an incarnation. ॥48 (क)॥
lanka.48.do48ख: He is Death in form, the fire that burns the forest of the wicked, the home of virtues, knowledge itself made dense; Śiva and Brahmā serve him. What enmity can there be with him? ॥48 (ख)॥
lanka.49.cau1: Give up the enmity and give back Vaidehī; worship the treasury of mercy, the most loving one. His words struck Rāvaṇa like arrows, and he said: Blacken your face and be gone, you wretch. ॥1॥
lanka.49.cau2: You have grown old, or else I would kill you. Now do not show yourself before my eyes. Mālyavān reasoned in his mind that the treasury of mercy now meant to slay Rāvaṇa. ॥2॥
lanka.49.cau3: He rose and left, speaking harsh words. Then Meghanāda said in anger: In the morning, watch my feats. I shall do a great deal; why say a little of it now? ॥3॥
lanka.49.cau4: Hearing his son's words, Rāvaṇa took heart, and lovingly sat him on his lap. While they were still deliberating, day broke, and the monkeys again pressed at all four gates. ॥4॥
lanka.49.cau5: In anger the monkeys surrounded the impregnable fort, and a great uproar arose in the city. Demons bearing all kinds of weapons ran out and toppled mountain peaks down from the fort. ॥5॥
lanka.49.cha1: They toppled peaks of mountains by the million, and missiles of many kinds flew. They rumble like falling thunderbolts, and the warriors roar like the clouds of the world's dissolution. The fierce monkey warriors close in and are cut, their bodies riddled with wounds, yet they do not flag. Seizing rocks, they hurl them at the fort, and the demons are slain wherever they stand. ॥1॥
lanka.49.do49: Meghanāda heard with his own ears that the monkeys had come back and laid siege to the fort; the warrior came down from the fort and, with drums beating, went out to face them. ॥49॥
lanka.50.cau1: Meghanāda said: Where are the two brothers, lords of Kosala, archers famed in every world? Where are Nala, Nīla, Dvivida and Sugrīva? Where are Aṅgada and Hanumān, the utmost in strength? ॥1॥
lanka.50.cau2: Where is Vibhīṣaṇa, traitor to his brother? Today I will kill them all, and him above all, whatever it takes. So saying, he set fierce arrows to the string and, in towering rage, drew it back to his ear. ॥2॥
lanka.50.cau3: He began to loose swarms of arrows, as if many winged serpents were rushing through the air. Here and there monkeys were seen falling; at that time none could stand before him. ॥3॥
lanka.50.cau4: Monkeys and bears ran off in all directions; all of them forgot their wish to fight. No monkey or bear could be found in the field whom he had not left with only his life remaining. ॥4॥
lanka.50.do50: He shot ten arrows into every one of them, and the monkey heroes lay on the ground. Meghanāda, mighty and steadfast, gave a lion's roar and thundered. ॥50॥
lanka.51.cau1: Seeing the army in distress, Hanumān, son of the Wind, rushed forward in fury, as though Death itself were charging. At once he tore up a huge mountain and in great rage flung it at Meghanāda. ॥1॥
lanka.51.cau2: Seeing it coming, he went up into the sky; his chariot, charioteer and horses were all destroyed. Again and again Hanumān challenges him, but he does not come near, for he knew Hanumān's secret. ॥2॥
lanka.51.cau3: Meghanāda went near Śrī Rāma and hurled abuse of every kind. He threw missiles, weapons and arms of every sort; the Lord, as if in play, cut them all down and warded them off. ॥3॥
lanka.51.cau4: Seeing the Lord's might, the fool was vexed, and began to work māyā in many ways — as if someone were to play games with Garuḍa, holding up a tiny young snake to frighten him. ॥4॥
lanka.51.do51: He whose mighty māyā holds all, great and small, even Śiva and Brahmā, in its power — to him the demon of crooked mind displays his own māyā. ॥51॥
lanka.52.cau1: He climbed into the sky and rained down embers in plenty, and streams of water burst forth from the earth. Ghouls and she-ghouls of every kind danced about, raising the cry of kill and cut. ॥1॥
lanka.52.cau2: Now he rained down filth, pus, blood, hair and bones; now he let loose a shower of stones. He showered dust and made such darkness that no one could see his own outstretched hand. ॥2॥
lanka.52.cau3: The monkeys were thrown into turmoil at the sight of this illusion; at this rate, it seemed, death had come for them all. Seeing this trickery, Śrī Rāma smiled; he knew that all the monkeys had taken fright. ॥3॥
lanka.52.cau4: With a single arrow he cut through the whole illusion, as the sun takes away the massed darkness. He looked on the monkeys and bears with grace, and they grew so mighty that nothing could hold them back in battle. ॥4॥
lanka.52.do52: Asking Śrī Rāma's leave, and with Aṅgada and other monkeys beside him, Lakṣmaṇa set out in anger, bow and arrows in hand. ॥52॥
lanka.53.cau1: His eyes were blood-red, his chest broad and his arms long; his body, like the snowy Himālaya, had a tinge of red. On this side Rāvaṇa dispatched his best fighters; they seized missiles and weapons of many kinds and rushed in. ॥1॥
lanka.53.cau2: Armed with mountains, claws and trees, the monkeys charged, crying glory to Śrī Rāma. All closed with their matches, pair against pair; on this side and on that, the longing to win was in no way small. ॥2॥
lanka.53.cau3: They tore at the demons with fists, kicks and teeth; the victorious monkeys struck them down and then shouted at them in scorn. The cry went up: kill, kill, seize, seize, seize, kill; break the head, grab the arm and tear it off. ॥3॥
lanka.53.cau4: The din filled all nine regions of the earth, and fearsome headless trunks ran about here and there. From the sky the hosts of gods watched the spectacle, now in wonder, now in delight. ॥4॥
lanka.53.do53: Blood had filled the hollows and congealed, and dust blew up and settled over it, as though ash had spread over heaps of glowing embers. ॥53॥
lanka.54.cau1: How did the wounded warriors look? Like palāśa trees in full flower. Lakṣmaṇa and Meghanāda, both warriors, fought each other in towering rage. ॥1॥
lanka.54.cau2: Neither could defeat the other; the demon fought unfairly, by the strength of trickery. At this Lakṣmaṇa, Ananta himself, was roused to anger and in a moment shattered both chariot and charioteer. ॥2॥
lanka.54.cau3: Śeṣa struck him in many ways, until the demon had barely his life left. Rāvaṇa's son reckoned in his mind: I am in peril; he will take my life. ॥3॥
lanka.54.cau4: He hurled the warrior-slaying spear, and that blazing weapon struck Lakṣmaṇa in the chest. As the weapon struck, he fell into a swoon; then Meghanāda, his fear gone, went up close to him. ॥4॥
lanka.54.do54: Warriors like Meghanāda, a thousand million of them, tried to lift him; but Śeṣa, on whom the world rests — how could he be raised? They went away abashed. ॥54॥
lanka.55.cau1: Listen, Pārvatī: he whose fiery wrath swiftly burns up the fourteen worlds, whom gods, men and all creation, moving and unmoving, serve: who could defeat him in battle? ॥1॥
lanka.55.cau2: Only one on whom Śrī Rāma's grace rests understands this play. When evening came, both armies turned back, and each began to take stock of its own troops. ॥2॥
lanka.55.cau3: The merciful Lord, the all-pervading Brahman, unconquered ruler of the worlds, asked: Where is Lakṣmaṇa? Just then Hanumān brought him in; seeing his younger brother, the Lord was deeply grieved. ॥3॥
lanka.55.cau4: Jāmbavān said: There is a physician in Laṅkā, Suṣeṇa; whom shall we send to fetch him? Taking a tiny form, Hanumān went and brought him back at once, house and all. ॥4॥
lanka.55.do55: Suṣeṇa came and laid his head at the lotus feet of Śrī Rāma. He named the mountain and the herb and said: Son of the Wind, go and fetch it. ॥55॥
lanka.56.cau1: With Śrī Rāma's lotus feet held in his heart, and speaking of his own strength, the son of the Wind set off. Over there, a spy let out the secret, and Rāvaṇa came to Kālanemi's house. ॥1॥
lanka.56.cau2: Rāvaṇa told him the secret; hearing it, Kālanemi beat his head again and again. He said: The one who burned your city before your eyes — who can bar his way? ॥2॥
lanka.56.cau3: Worship Śrī Rāma and do yourself good; give up this false prattle, my lord. Set in your heart the one who delights the eyes, his body dark and lovely as a blue lotus. ॥3॥
lanka.56.cau4: Give up the folly of I and you and mine; you are asleep in the night of great delusion, wake up. He devours even the serpent of Time: could anyone defeat him in battle even in a dream? ॥4॥
lanka.56.do56: Hearing this, Rāvaṇa flew into a rage, and Kālanemi thought to himself: Let me rather fall by the hand of Śrī Rāma's messenger; this villain is steeped in heaps of sin. ॥56॥
lanka.57.cau1: So saying he went, and on the way he conjured an illusion, making a lake, a temple and a fine garden. The son of the Wind saw the pleasant hermitage and thought: I will ask the sage, drink some water, and my weariness will go. ॥1॥
lanka.57.cau2: There sat the demon in a false guise, hoping to beguile the messenger of the Lord of māyā. Hanumān went and bowed his head, and the demon began to tell of Śrī Rāma's virtues. ॥2॥
lanka.57.cau3: A great battle is being fought between Rāvaṇa and Śrī Rāma; Śrī Rāma will win, of that there is no doubt. Brother, I see it all while staying here; the power of my inner vision is great. ॥3॥
lanka.57.cau4: When asked for water he held out his water-pot; Hanumān said: So little water will not satisfy me. Kālanemi said: Bathe in the lake and come back quickly, and I will initiate you so that you gain knowledge. ॥4॥
lanka.57.do57: As Hanumān entered the lake, a she-crocodile, in a frenzy, seized his foot. He killed her, and she took on a divine body, mounted a celestial car and rose into the sky. ॥57॥
lanka.58.cau1: She said: Hanumān, the sight of you has freed me from sin; dear one, the great sage's curse is ended. This is no sage but a terrible demon; believe my words, Hanumān, they are true. ॥1॥
lanka.58.cau2: The moment the nymph had said this and gone, Hanumān went straight to the demon. Hanumān said: Sage, take your teacher's fee first; you can give me the mantra afterwards. ॥2॥
lanka.58.cau3: He wound his tail round the demon's head and dashed him down; as he died, the demon showed his own true body. Saying Rāma, Rāma, he gave up his life; hearing it, Hanumān went on, glad at heart. ॥3॥
lanka.58.cau4: The mountain he saw, but the herb he could not make out; so Hanumān suddenly uprooted the whole peak. Holding the mountain, he sped through the night sky and passed over the city of Ayodhyā. ॥4॥
lanka.58.do58: Bharata saw a huge form and, judging in his mind that it was a demon, drew his bow to his ear and shot an arrow without a head. ॥58॥
lanka.59.cau1: The arrow struck, and he fell senseless to the ground, calling: Rāma, Rāma, O Lord of the Raghus. At these dear words Bharata ran to him and came to the monkey's side in great haste. ॥1॥
lanka.59.cau2: Seeing the monkey stricken, he clasped him to his breast and tried in many ways to rouse him, but he did not wake. His face fell and his heart was filled with sorrow; with tears in his eyes he spoke: ॥2॥
lanka.59.cau3: The fate that set me apart from Śrī Rāma has now dealt me this cruel blow too. If my love for Śrī Rāma's lotus feet is free of guile in mind, word and body, ॥3॥
lanka.59.cau4: then may this monkey be rid of weariness and pain, if Śrī Rāma looks on me with favour. At these words the monkey chief sat up, crying: Glory, glory to the Lord of Kosala! ॥4॥
lanka.59.so59: Bharata clasped Hanumān to his breast, his body thrilling and his eyes wet with tears. As he thought of Śrī Rāma, his love was more than his heart could hold. ॥59॥
lanka.60.cau1: Bharata said: Dear one, tell me how the Lord, the home of all joy, is faring, with his younger brother and Mother Jānakī. Hanumān told him in brief all that had happened; Bharata was grieved and full of regret within. ॥1॥
lanka.60.cau2: Alas, fate, why was I born into the world, when I have been of no use to the Lord in a single task? Then, knowing it was no time for this, the mighty hero steadied his mind and spoke again to Hanumān: ॥2॥
lanka.60.cau3: Dear one, you will be late getting there, and at daybreak the work will be undone. Mount my arrow with the mountain, and I shall send you to where the abode of grace is. ॥3॥
lanka.60.cau4: When Hanumān heard this, pride arose in his mind: how will an arrow fly with my weight on it? Then, thinking again of Śrī Rāma's power, he paid homage at Bharata's feet, and with joined palms he said: ॥4॥
lanka.60.do60क: My lord and master, holding your glory in my heart I shall go at once. With these words, and with leave given, Hanumān bowed at his feet and set off. ॥60 (क)॥
lanka.60.do60ख: Bharata's strength of arm, his gentle nature, his virtues and his boundless love for the Lord's feet: these the son of the Wind praised again and again in his mind as he went. ॥60 (ख)॥
lanka.61.cau1: There, gazing at Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma spoke words such as a mortal man would speak: Half the night is gone and Hanumān has not come. Then Śrī Rāma lifted his younger brother and held him to his breast. ॥1॥
lanka.61.cau2: Brother, the sight of my sorrow was always more than you could bear, so tender has your nature ever been. For my sake you left father and mother, and endured the forest's cold, its sun and its winds. ॥2॥
lanka.61.cau3: Where is that love now, brother? You do not rise, though you hear my anguished words. If I had known that the forest would part me from my brother, I would not have heeded even that command of my father. ॥3॥
lanka.61.cau4: Sons, wealth, wife, home and family come and go in the world time after time. Think of this and wake, dear one: in all the world a brother of one's own blood is not found again. ॥4॥
lanka.61.cau5: As a bird without wings is wretched, a serpent without its jewel, a great elephant without its trunk, such will my life be without you, brother, if unfeeling fate keeps me alive. ॥5॥
lanka.61.cau6: With what face shall I go to Ayodhyā, having lost my dear brother for the sake of a wife? Better I had borne the world's reproach: the loss of a wife would have been no special harm. ॥6॥
lanka.61.cau7: Now, my son, this hard and pitiless heart of mine must bear both the disgrace and the grief for you. You are your mother's only son, dear one, the very support of her life. ॥7॥
lanka.61.cau8: Knowing me to be a giver of every kind of joy and wholly devoted to your good, she put your hand in mine and gave you to my care. When I go to her, what answer am I to give? Brother, why not rise and tell me what to do? ॥8॥
lanka.61.cau9: He who frees others from sorrow grieved in many ways, and tears flowed from his lotus-petal eyes. Umā, Śrī Rāma is one and undivided; the Lord, merciful to his devotees, was showing the ways of a man. ॥9॥
lanka.61.so61: The hosts of monkeys were distraught to hear the Lord's lament. Then Hanumān arrived, like the heroic mood arriving in the midst of the mood of grief. ॥61॥
lanka.62.cau1: Śrī Rāma joyfully embraced Hanumān; the Lord is deeply grateful and supremely wise. Then the physician quickly applied his remedy, and Lakṣmaṇa sat up, full of joy. ॥1॥
lanka.62.cau2: Holding his brother close to his heart, the Lord embraced him, and the bear and monkey hosts were all glad. Then Hanumān carried the physician home again, just as he had fetched him. ॥2॥
lanka.62.cau3: Rāvaṇa heard this news and, in deep dejection, beat his head again and again. In distress he came to Kumbhakarṇa and, by many kinds of effort, roused him. ॥3॥
lanka.62.cau4: Awake, the demon looked like Death himself sitting there in bodily form. Kumbhakarṇa asked: Tell me, brother, why have your faces gone so dry and drawn? ॥4॥
lanka.62.cau5: The proud one told him the whole story of how he had carried off Sītā, and said: Brother, every one of the demons has fallen to the monkeys; they have slain the greatest of warriors. ॥5॥
lanka.62.cau6: Durmukha, the foe of the gods, the eater of men, the mighty warriors Atikāya and Akampana, and other heroes such as Mahodara, all of them steadfast in battle, lie fallen on the field. ॥6॥
lanka.62.do62: Then, hearing Rāvaṇa's words, Kumbhakarṇa cried out in grief: You carried off the Mother of the world, fool, and now you hope for good? ॥62॥
lanka.63.cau1: Lord of the demons, you did ill. What use is it now to come and wake me? Even now, brother, give up your pride and worship Śrī Rāma, and good will come to you. ॥1॥
lanka.63.cau2: Rāvaṇa, is Śrī Rāma only a man, he whose servants are the like of Hanumān? Alas, brother, you did wrong in not coming to tell me at the very start. ॥2॥
lanka.63.cau3: My lord, you have set yourself against that god whose servants are Śiva, Brahmā and the gods. The sage Nārada once taught me wisdom I meant to pass on to you; that chance is gone now. ॥3॥
lanka.63.cau4: Now, brother, take me in your arms and embrace me; let me go and make my eyes fruitful. Let me go and see him, dark of body and lotus-eyed, who frees from the three kinds of suffering. ॥4॥
lanka.63.do63: Remembering Śrī Rāma's form and virtues, he was lost in them for a moment. Rāvaṇa sent for countless jars of wine and many buffaloes. ॥63॥
lanka.64.cau1: He ate the buffaloes, drank the wine, and roared like the crash of a thunderbolt. Wild with drink and eager for battle, Kumbhakarṇa left the fort and set out, with no army at his side. ॥1॥
lanka.64.cau2: Seeing him, Vibhīṣaṇa came forward, fell at his feet and gave his name. Kumbhakarṇa lifted his younger brother to his breast and loved him the more, knowing him for Śrī Rāma's devotee. ॥2॥
lanka.64.cau3: Vibhīṣaṇa said: Brother, Rāvaṇa kicked me when I gave him well-considered counsel for his highest good. Stung by that, I came to Śrī Rāma, and the Lord, seeing me forlorn, was pleased with me. ॥3॥
lanka.64.cau4: Kumbhakarṇa said: Listen, son: Rāvaṇa is in the grip of death; will he heed the best of counsel now? Blessed, blessed, blessed are you, Vibhīṣaṇa; dear one, you have become an ornament to the demon clan. ॥4॥
lanka.64.cau5: Brother, you have made our line illustrious, for you worshipped Śrī Rāma, the ocean of beauty and joy. ॥5॥
lanka.64.do64: Cast off deceit in word, deed and thought, and worship Śrī Rāma, the steadfast in battle. Go now, brave one; I can no longer tell my own from others, for I have fallen into the power of death. ॥64॥
lanka.65.cau1: Hearing his brother's words, Vibhīṣaṇa left and came to where Śrī Rāma, the ornament of the three worlds, was. He said: My Lord, Kumbhakarṇa, steadfast in battle, with a body like a mountain, is coming. ॥1॥
lanka.65.cau2: As soon as the monkeys heard this much, the mighty ones rushed forward with shrill cries. They lifted trees and mountains and, gnashing their teeth, hurled them upon him. ॥2॥
lanka.65.cau3: Each bear and monkey, at every throw, strikes him with mountain peaks by the million. Yet his resolve never wavered and his body would not be shifted, try as they might: an elephant struck with arka fruit cares as little. ॥3॥
lanka.65.cau4: Then Hanumān, son of the Wind, struck him with his fist; he fell to the earth, dazed, and beat his head. Rising again, he struck Hanumān, who reeled and at once fell to the ground. ॥4॥
lanka.65.cau5: Then he threw Nala and Nīla to the ground, and dashed down warriors here and there. The monkey army fled, stricken with great fear; no one would face him. ॥5॥
lanka.65.do65: He knocked Aṅgada and the other monkeys senseless, Sugrīva with them, and he, the very bound of boundless strength, went off with the king of the monkeys pressed under his arm. ॥65॥
lanka.66.cau1: Umā, Śrī Rāma is playing a human part, as Garuḍa might play, mingling with a crowd of snakes. Does such a fight befit him who devours Death itself with a knitting of his brows? ॥1॥
lanka.66.cau2: He will spread a fame that purifies the world, and by singing it again and again people will cross the ocean of worldly existence. His swoon passed, Hanumān, son of the Wind, came to, and then began to search for Sugrīva. ॥2॥
lanka.66.cau3: Sugrīva too came out of his swoon and slipped free, for Kumbhakarṇa believed him dead. He bit off his nose and ears and, roaring, made off through the sky; only then did Kumbhakarṇa know. ॥3॥
lanka.66.cau4: Kumbhakarṇa seized him by the feet and dashed him to the ground; with great agility Sugrīva rose and struck him again. Then the mighty Sugrīva came back to the Lord, crying: Glory, glory, glory to you, treasury of compassion! ॥4॥
lanka.66.cau5: Knowing in his heart that his nose and ears had been cut off, he turned back in anger, mortified. Fearsome by nature, and now without ears or nose, he struck terror into the monkey ranks at the sight. ॥5॥
lanka.66.do66: Glory, glory, glory to the jewel of Raghu's line! With this war-cry the monkeys charged, and all at once they let fly at him masses of mountains and trees. ॥66॥
lanka.67.cau1: Kumbhakarṇa, fired for battle, advanced to meet them like Death himself in fury. He seized monkeys by the million and devoured them, as if locusts were pouring into a mountain cave. ॥1॥
lanka.67.cau2: Millions he seized and crushed against his body; millions he ground to nothing and mixed with the dust of the earth. Throngs of bears and monkeys come out by way of his mouth, nose and ears, and flee. ॥2॥
lanka.67.cau3: The demon, reeling with the madness of war, was as proud as if Brahmā had made him a gift of the universe to devour. All the great warriors turned back and would not return when rallied; their eyes saw nothing, and they did not hear when called. ॥3॥
lanka.67.cau4: Kumbhakarṇa scattered the monkey army; hearing of it, the demon host also rushed out. Śrī Rāma saw his army in distress, and enemy forces of many kinds arriving. ॥4॥
lanka.67.do67: Listen, Sugrīva, Vibhīṣaṇa and my brother: take care of the army. I will take the measure of this wretch's strength and his host, said the lotus-eyed Śrī Rāma. ॥67॥
lanka.68.cau1: Śārṅga bow in hand, quiver girt about his waist, Śrī Rāma went out to grind the enemy host to pieces. First the Lord twanged his bow, and at its roar the enemy host was struck deaf. ॥1॥
lanka.68.cau2: Śrī Rāma, true to his word, loosed a hundred thousand arrows, which flew like winged serpents of death. Iron shafts flew in great numbers everywhere, and fearsome fiendish warriors began to be cut down. ॥2॥
lanka.68.cau3: Feet, chests, heads and mighty arms are lopped away, and many warriors are left lying in a hundred pieces. The wounded spin round and round and fall to the earth; the stoutest rise, steady themselves and fight again. ॥3॥
lanka.68.cau4: As the arrows strike, they roar like thunderclouds; many flee at the mere sight of those cruel shafts. Fierce headless trunks run about, raising the cry: Seize, seize! Kill, kill! ॥4॥
lanka.68.do68: In a moment the Lord's arrows cut down the fearsome fiends. and every arrow came back and slipped into Śrī Rāma's quiver. ॥68॥
lanka.69.cau1: Kumbhakarṇa considered in his mind and saw that the demon host had been slain in a moment. The mighty warrior grew furious and gave a deep roar like a lion's. ॥1॥
lanka.69.cau2: In his rage he tears up mountains and hurls them where the mighty monkey warriors stand. Seeing the huge rocks coming, the Lord cut them with his arrows and reduced them to dust. ॥2॥
lanka.69.cau3: Then Śrī Rāma, angered, drew his bow again and loosed many most terrible arrows. The arrows pass into his body and out again, like lightning vanishing into a cloud. ॥3॥
lanka.69.cau4: The blood streaming over his black body looked like rills of red ochre running down a mountain of lampblack. Seeing him shaken, the bears and monkeys rushed at him; as soon as they came close, he laughed. ॥4॥
lanka.69.do69: With a mighty roar he bellowed and seized monkeys by the million; like a great elephant he dashes them to the ground, swearing by Rāvaṇa. ॥69॥
lanka.70.cau1: The troops of bears and monkeys ran, as a flock of sheep runs on seeing a wolf. Bhavānī, the monkeys and bears ran in panic, crying out in anguished voices. ॥1॥
lanka.70.cau2: They cried: This demon is like a famine that now means to fall upon the land of the monkey race. Rāma, cloud of mercy, slayer of Khara, remover of the suffering of those who bow to you, save us, save us! ॥2॥
lanka.70.cau3: As soon as he heard their piteous words, the Lord set out, making ready his bow and arrows. Śrī Rāma kept his army behind him and, mighty beyond measure, went forward in anger. ॥3॥
lanka.70.cau4: He drew the bow and set a hundred arrows to it; once loosed, they sank into the demon's body. Struck by them, he charged, full of rage; the mountains swayed and the earth shook. ॥4॥
lanka.70.cau5: He tore up a mountain; Śrī Rāma cut off that very arm. He charged with the mountain in his left arm; the Lord cut off that arm too and laid it on the ground. ॥5॥
lanka.70.cau6: With his arms cut off, how did the wretch look? Like Mount Mandara shorn of its wings. He glared fiercely at the Lord, as if he wished to swallow the three worlds. ॥6॥
lanka.70.do70: With a fearful, piercing shriek he charged, his mouth gaping wide. In the sky the siddhas and gods cried out in terror: Alas, alas! ॥70॥
lanka.71.cau1: The Lord, treasury of compassion, saw that the gods were afraid, and drew his bow back to his ear. He filled the demon's mouth with a mass of arrows; even so, the mighty one did not fall to the ground. ॥1॥
lanka.71.cau2: His mouth stuffed with arrows, he charged straight at the Lord, as if Death's own quiver had come alive and was advancing. Then the Lord in anger took up a sharp arrow and severed his head from his trunk. ॥2॥
lanka.71.cau3: The head fell before Rāvaṇa, who was as distraught as a serpent that has lost its jewel. The earth gave way as the fearsome trunk ran on; then the Lord cut it into two pieces. ॥3॥
lanka.71.cau4: The pieces fell to the earth like mountains dropping from the sky, crushing monkeys, bears and demons beneath them. His radiance entered the Lord's face, and gods and sages alike were filled with wonder. ॥4॥
lanka.71.cau5: The gods beat their drums and rejoice; they sing praises and shower down flowers in plenty. Having made their prayers, all the gods departed; at that very time the divine sage Nārada came. ॥5॥
lanka.71.cau6: From high in the sky he sang of Śrī Hari's many virtues, and their fine heroic strain pleased the Lord's heart. The sage left, bidding him slay the wicked one quickly, and Śrī Rāma stood resplendent on the field of battle. ॥6॥
lanka.71.cha1: Śrī Rāma, the Lord of Kosala, of matchless strength, shines on the field of battle. There are drops of sweat on his face, his lotus eyes are red, and drops of blood are on his body. With both arms he twirls arrow and bow, and bears and monkeys make a fine sight on every side. Tulasīdāsa says: Not even Śeṣa, with his many mouths, could describe that beauty. ॥1॥
lanka.71.do71: To that vile demon, a mine of sin, the Lord gave his own abode. Pārvatī, dull-witted are those who do not worship Śrī Rāma. ॥71॥
lanka.72.cau1: At the close of day both armies turned back; the warriors were sorely wearied by the fight. By Śrī Rāma's grace the strength of the monkey host grew, as a fire blazes up when it finds grass. ॥1॥
lanka.72.cau2: Day and night the demons dwindle, as merit dwindles when one proclaims it with one's own mouth. Rāvaṇa laments bitterly, pressing his brother's head to his breast again and again. ॥2॥
lanka.72.cau3: The women weep, beating their breasts with their hands and recounting his great splendour and might. At that moment Meghanāda arrived and consoled his father with many words. ॥3॥
lanka.72.cau4: Meghanāda said: Tomorrow you will see my prowess; why should I boast much now? Father, the strength and the chariot I won from my chosen deity: that strength I have not yet shown you. ॥4॥
lanka.72.cau5: While he boasted thus, the day dawned, and monkeys in great numbers pressed against the four gates. On this side stood monkeys and bears, heroes like Death; on that, demons steadfast in battle. ॥5॥
lanka.72.cau6: The warriors fight, each for his own side's victory; Garuḍa, that battle is beyond description. ॥6॥
lanka.72.do72: Meghanāda mounted his chariot of illusion and rose into the sky. He roared with a loud peal of laughter, and terror seized the monkey host. ॥72॥
lanka.73.cau1: He hurled spears, pikes, swords, scimitars, missiles and weapons of many kinds, and thunderbolts; he flung axes, iron clubs and rocks, and began to rain down arrows in multitudes. ॥1॥
lanka.73.cau2: Arrows covered the sky in all ten directions, as though the clouds of Maghā had set in a steady downpour. Seize him, seize him, strike! — the cry rang in their ears, but no one could tell who was striking. ॥2॥
lanka.73.cau3: The monkeys leap into the sky with rocks and trees, but cannot see him, and come back dismayed. By the power of illusion he turned the rugged passes, paths, hills and caves into a cage of arrows. ॥3॥
lanka.73.cau4: Where could they go? The monkeys were in distress, like mountains such as Mandara held captive by Indra. Hanumān, son of the Wind, Aṅgada, Nala and Nīla: all these mighty ones he threw into confusion. ॥4॥
lanka.73.cau5: Next he struck Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa with arrows until their bodies were torn. Then he began to fight Śrī Rāma; the arrows he loosed turned into serpents as they struck. ॥5॥
lanka.73.cau6: Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara, who is subject to none but himself, infinite, one and changeless, came under the power of the serpent noose. Like an actor, the one Lord, ever free, performs many feigned acts. ॥6॥
lanka.73.cau7: For the splendour of the battle the Lord let himself be bound in the serpent noose, and the gods took fright. ॥7॥
lanka.73.do73: Pārvatī, he whose name the sages repeat to cut the bonds of worldly existence — can he, the all-pervading abode of the universe, ever come under bondage? ॥73॥
lanka.74.cau1: Pārvatī, the deeds of Śrī Rāma in his embodied form cannot be reasoned out by the power of intellect or speech. Knowing this, those who know the truth and are free of attachment leave all argument aside and worship Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
lanka.74.cau2: Meghanāda threw the army into disarray; then he showed himself and began to speak abuse. Jāmbavān said: Stand there, villain! Hearing this, his fury rose higher still. ॥2॥
lanka.74.cau3: Meghanāda said: Fool, I spared you because you were old; and now, wretch, you dare challenge me? So saying, he hurled his flashing trident; Jāmbavān caught that very trident in his hand and ran at him. ॥3॥
lanka.74.cau4: He drove it into Meghanāda's chest, and the slayer of gods spun round and dropped to the earth. Then in rage Jāmbavān seized him by the feet, whirled him round and dashed him on the earth, showing his own strength. ॥4॥
lanka.74.cau5: By virtue of a boon he would not die though struck; so Jāmbavān seized him by the foot and flung him on to Laṅkā. Meanwhile the divine sage Nārada had sent Garuḍa, who came swiftly to Śrī Rāma's side. ॥5॥
lanka.74.do74क: Garuḍa, king of birds, seized and devoured all the swarms of illusory serpents. The illusion was gone, and all the bands of monkeys rejoiced. ॥74 (क)॥
lanka.74.do74ख: Wielding rocks, trees and stones, and their claws, the enraged monkeys dashed forward. The demons, more distraught than ever, fled and climbed up into the fort. ॥74 (ख)॥
lanka.75.cau1: Meghanāda came out of his swoon, and on seeing his father was deeply ashamed. At once he went to a cave in a great mountain, resolved to perform a sacrifice that would make him invincible. ॥1॥
lanka.75.cau2: Here Vibhīṣaṇa thought of a plan and said: Listen, my Lord, generous one of matchless strength: Meghanāda, the wicked sorcerer who torments the gods, is performing an unholy sacrifice. ॥2॥
lanka.75.cau3: My Lord, if he brings it to completion, then, master, he will not be conquered quickly. Hearing this, Śrī Rāma was greatly pleased and spoke to Aṅgada and many other monkeys: ॥3॥
lanka.75.cau4: Go, all of you, my brothers, with Lakṣmaṇa, and destroy the sacrifice there. Lakṣmaṇa, you must slay him in battle; it grieves me deeply to see the gods in fear. ॥4॥
lanka.75.cau5: Listen, brother: slay him by strength, wit and stratagem, in such a way that the demon perishes. Jāmbavān, Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa, you three stay with the army. ॥5॥
lanka.75.cau6: When Śrī Rāma gave the command, Lakṣmaṇa bound his quiver at his waist and made ready his bow; then, firm in battle, with the Lord's might held in his heart, he spoke words as deep as a rumbling cloud: ॥6॥
lanka.75.cau7: If I return today without killing him, let me not be called Śrī Rāma's servant. Even if a hundred Śivas come to his aid, I swear by Śrī Rāma, I will slay him. ॥7॥
lanka.75.do75: Bowing his head at Śrī Rāma's feet, Lakṣmaṇa, who is Ananta, set off at once, and with him went the great warriors Aṅgada, Nīla, Mainda, Nala and Hanumān. ॥75॥
lanka.76.cau1: The monkeys went and saw him sitting there, offering blood and buffaloes as oblations. They wrecked the whole sacrifice, and when still he did not rise, they began to praise him. ॥1॥
lanka.76.cau2: Even so he did not rise; then they went and seized him by the hair, and kicking him again and again they ran off. He gave chase with his trident; the monkeys fled and came to where Lakṣmaṇa stood before them. ॥2॥
lanka.76.cau3: He came on, overcome with fury, roaring again and again with a terrible cry. Hanumān and Aṅgada rushed at him in anger; he hit them in the chest with the trident and brought them down. ॥3॥
lanka.76.cau4: He flung the fierce trident at Lakṣmaṇa, the Lord; with an arrow Ananta cut it into two pieces. Hanumān and the crown prince Aṅgada rose again and struck at him furiously, but no blow told on him. ॥4॥
lanka.76.cau5: The heroes fell back, for the foe would not die though struck; then he charged with a terrible roar. Seeing him come on like Death in wrath, Lakṣmaṇa loosed his dreadful arrows. ॥5॥
lanka.76.cau6: Seeing the arrows come at him like thunderbolts, the villain vanished at once. Taking on many disguises he fought on, now showing himself, now hidden. ॥6॥
lanka.76.cau7: When they saw that the foe could not be overcome, the monkeys took fright, and Lakṣmaṇa, lord of serpents, became furious beyond measure. Lakṣmaṇa made up his mind: I have played with this sinner long enough. ॥7॥
lanka.76.cau8: Remembering the glory of the Lord of Kosala, he fitted an arrow with all his might. He let it fly, and it struck the demon full in the chest; at the moment of death he cast off all deceit. ॥8॥
lanka.76.do76: Where is Rāma's younger brother, where is Rāma? So saying, he gave up his life. Aṅgada and Hanumān said: Blessed, blessed is your mother! ॥76॥
lanka.77.cau1: Hanumān lifted him without effort, laid him at the gate of Laṅkā and came back. Hearing of his death, the gods and gandharvas all came into the sky, riding their aerial cars. ॥1॥
lanka.77.cau2: Showering flowers and beating their drums, they sing the spotless glory of Śrī Rāma. Glory to you, Ananta! Glory to the support of the world! Lord, you have delivered all the gods. ॥2॥
lanka.77.cau3: Having sung their praises, the gods and siddhas departed, and Lakṣmaṇa came back to the ocean of mercy. The moment Rāvaṇa heard of his son's death, he fainted and fell to the ground. ॥3॥
lanka.77.cau4: Mandodarī wails aloud; she beats her breast and cries out in many ways. All the people of the city are distraught with grief, and every one of them calls Rāvaṇa vile. ॥4॥
lanka.77.do77: Then Rāvaṇa consoled all the women in many ways: The whole world is a perishable form; consider it in your hearts and see. ॥77॥
lanka.78.cau1: Rāvaṇa instructed them in wisdom; base as he himself was, his words were auspicious and holy. Many are skilled at teaching others; but those who live by it themselves are not many. ॥1॥
lanka.78.cau2: The night ended and dawn broke; the bears and monkeys pressed up to all four gates. Rāvaṇa called his chief warriors and said: Whoever feels his heart waver when facing battle ॥2॥
lanka.78.cau3: had better run away right now; there is no good in turning one's back once in the fight. I have stoked this enmity by the strength of my own arms; I myself will answer the enemy who has marched against us. ॥3॥
lanka.78.cau4: With these words he had a chariot swift as the wind made ready, and all the instruments of war struck up. All the heroes, of matchless strength, set out as though a storm of lampblack were sweeping along. ॥4॥
lanka.78.cau5: Countless ill omens appeared at that time, but in the vast pride of his strength of arm he paid them no heed. ॥5॥
lanka.78.cha1: Proud beyond measure, he gave no thought to omens, good or bad; weapons slipped from their hands. Warriors tumbled from chariots; horses and elephants trumpeted and screamed and bolted from their company. Jackals, vultures and donkeys raised harsh and fearful cries, and dogs howled in great numbers. Owls hooted with utterly dreadful voices, as if they were the messengers of death. ॥1॥
lanka.78.do78: Can wealth, good omens or peace of mind come, even in a dream, to one who is bent on harming living beings, is in the grip of delusion, has turned from Śrī Rāma and delights in desire? ॥78॥
lanka.79.cau1: The boundless demon army set out, the fourfold host in many divisions. There were mounts, chariots and carriages of every kind, and pennants and flags without number in many colours. ॥1॥
lanka.79.cau2: Many herds of frenzied elephants moved on, like rain-clouds of the monsoon driven by the wind. There were hosts of famed warriors of every sort, brave in battle and versed in many kinds of magic. ॥2॥
lanka.79.cau3: That most colourful army looked as splendid as if the hero Spring had marshalled his forces. As the army moved, the elephants of the quarters tottered, the ocean heaved and the mountains shook. ॥3॥
lanka.79.cau4: Dust rose and the sun was hidden; the wind fell still and the earth was in distress. Drums and kettledrums sounded with a fearful din, like the clouds thundering at the dissolution of the world. ॥4॥
lanka.79.cau5: Kettledrums, trumpets and shehnais sounded the Mārū, the martial strain that delights warriors. All the heroes gave lion-like roars and boasted of their own strength and valour. ॥5॥
lanka.79.cau6: Rāvaṇa said: Listen, my warriors. Crush the throngs of bears and monkeys. I will kill the two royal brothers. With these words he moved his army forward to face the foe. ॥6॥
lanka.79.cau7: When all the monkeys learned of this, they rushed out calling on the name of Śrī Rāma. ॥7॥
lanka.79.cha1: The huge and fearsome monkeys and bears, like Death itself, charged, as if flocks of winged mountains of many hues were flying. Claws, teeth, rocks and mighty trees were their weapons; strong as they were, they knew no fear. Hailing Śrī Rāma, the lion to that frenzied elephant Rāvaṇa, they sang of his fair renown. ॥1॥
lanka.79.do79: On both sides they shouted for victory; each warrior singled out an opponent of his own, and they clashed, the one side praising Śrī Rāma, the other Rāvaṇa. ॥79॥
lanka.80.cau1: Seeing Rāvaṇa in a chariot and Śrī Rāma without one, Vibhīṣaṇa grew uneasy. His great love stirred a doubt in his mind, and bowing at the Lord's feet he spoke with affection: ॥1॥
lanka.80.cau2: My Lord, you have no chariot, no armour to guard your body, no shoes for your feet; how will you overcome that mighty warrior? The treasury of compassion said: Listen, friend. The chariot that brings victory is a different one. ॥2॥
lanka.80.cau3: Valour and steadfastness are the wheels of that chariot; truth and good conduct are its unshaken flag and banner. Its horses are strength, discernment, self-restraint and doing good to others, yoked to it with forgiveness, compassion and equanimity for reins. ॥3॥
lanka.80.cau4: Worship of God is its skilled charioteer; its shield is dispassion, its sword contentment. Charity is the axe, intellect the fierce lance, and the highest realised knowledge the stiff bow. ॥4॥
lanka.80.cau5: A pure and unwavering mind is the quiver; calm of mind, the yamas and the niyamas are its many arrows. Reverence for brāhmaṇas and the guru is armour that nothing can pierce; there is no other means of victory to equal this. ॥5॥
lanka.80.cau6: Friend, for one who has such a chariot, made of dharma, there is no enemy anywhere left to conquer. ॥6॥
lanka.80.do80क: That hero can conquer even worldly existence, the great and unconquerable foe, who has such a firm chariot. Listen, my friend of steady mind. ॥80 (क)॥
lanka.80.do80ख: The Lord's words filled Vibhīṣaṇa with joy, and he took hold of his lotus feet and said: Rāma, treasure of grace and joy, by this means you have given me your teaching. ॥80 (ख)॥
lanka.80.do80ग: Over there Rāvaṇa was calling out challenges; over here, Aṅgada and Hanumān. Demons, bears and monkeys all fought, each swearing by his own master. ॥80 (ग)॥
lanka.81.cau1: Brahmā and the other gods, with many siddhas and sages, watched the battle from the sky in their aerial chariots. Umā, I too was with them, watching Śrī Rāma's deeds in the fervour of battle. ॥1॥
lanka.81.cau2: The warriors on both sides were drunk with the thrill of battle; the monkeys were winning, by the strength of Śrī Rāma. They grappled one to one, hurling challenges, and crushed one another and threw each other to the ground. ॥2॥
lanka.81.cau3: They struck, hacked, seized and threw down their foes; they broke off heads and struck others with those heads. They ripped open bellies, tore away arms, and seized warriors by the feet and dashed them to the ground. ॥3॥
lanka.81.cau4: The bears buried demon warriors in the earth and heaped sand over them. The brave monkeys, pitted against the foe, seemed like a host of Deaths in wrath. ॥4॥
lanka.81.cha1: Like Yama in his wrath, the monkeys made a splendid sight, blood streaming from their bodies. Those mighty fighters crushed the warriors of the demon army and thundered like clouds. With a roar of rebuke they struck with slaps, bit with their teeth and trampled with their kicks. Monkeys and bears shrieked and used cunning and force to bring the wicked to ruin. ॥1॥
lanka.81.cha2: Seizing their foes, they tore their cheeks, split their chests and hung the entrails about their own necks, as if the Lord of Prahlāda, Narasiṁha, had taken many bodies and were at play in the arena of war. Seize, kill, cut, throw down: the dreadful cries filled the sky and the earth. Glory to Śrī Rāma, who truly makes a straw a thunderbolt and a thunderbolt a straw. ॥2॥
lanka.81.do81: Rāvaṇa saw his army giving way; in his twenty arms he held ten bows. Mounting his chariot he drove forward, shouting in his arrogance: Turn back, turn back. ॥81॥
lanka.82.cau1: Rāvaṇa charged in towering rage; the monkeys went out to meet him with war-cries. Lifting trees, stones and mountains in their hands, they hurled them on him all at once. ॥1॥
lanka.82.cau2: The rocks struck his thunderbolt-hard body and burst at once into fragments. He did not budge but stood fixed, his chariot planted where it was: Rāvaṇa, mad for battle and raging beyond measure. ॥2॥
lanka.82.cau3: Pouncing this way and that and bellowing, he began to crush the monkey warriors, for his anger had risen high. Bears and monkeys in great numbers fled, crying: Save us, save us, Aṅgada, Hanumān. ॥3॥
lanka.82.cau4: Protect us, protect us, O hero of the Raghus, our master; this wretch is devouring us like Death. Seeing every monkey in flight, Rāvaṇa set arrows to his ten bows. ॥4॥
lanka.82.cha1: Fitting them to his bows he loosed a storm of arrows, which flew and struck like serpents. Arrows filled the earth and sky, the quarters and the spaces between; where could the monkeys run? A great uproar arose; the army of monkeys and bears, in distress, cried out in anguish: O hero of the Raghus, ocean of compassion, friend of the afflicted, protector of your own, O Hari. ॥1॥
lanka.82.do82: Lakṣmaṇa saw his own army in distress; he tightened the quiver at his waist and took up his bow, and then, touching his head to Śrī Rāma's feet, he strode out in anger. ॥82॥
lanka.83.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa said: Wretch, why are you killing monkeys and bears? Look upon me: I am your death. Rāvaṇa said: Slayer of my son, it is you I have been searching for. Today I will strike you down and cool the fire in my breast. ॥1॥
lanka.83.cau2: With these words he loosed fierce arrows; Lakṣmaṇa cut every one into a hundred pieces. Rāvaṇa hurled weapons by the million; Lakṣmaṇa cut them down to the size of sesame seeds and turned them aside. ॥2॥
lanka.83.cau3: Then he struck back with his own arrows, smashed the chariot and slew the charioteer. He shot a hundred arrows into each of the ten foreheads, like serpents entering the peaks of a mountain. ॥3॥
lanka.83.cau4: Then he drove a hundred arrows into his chest; Rāvaṇa fell to the ground and knew nothing. When the swoon passed, the mighty one rose again and hurled the spear that Brahmā had given him. ॥4॥
lanka.83.cha1: The fearsome spear that Brahmā had bestowed found its mark full in the breast of Lakṣmaṇa, Ananta himself. The hero fell, stricken; the ten-headed one tried to raise him, but for all its fame his peerless strength failed him. He on one of whose heads the whole mansion of the universe rests like a speck of dust: him the foolish Rāvaṇa wanted to lift, not knowing the master of the three worlds. ॥1॥
lanka.83.do83: Seeing this, Hanumān, son of the Wind, ran forward, speaking harsh words. As Hanumān came on, Rāvaṇa dealt him a most terrible blow with his fist. ॥83॥
lanka.84.cau1: Hanumān went down on one knee, yet did not fall; then he steadied himself and rose, full of anger. Hanumān struck him a single blow with his fist, and Rāvaṇa fell like a mountain hit by a thunderbolt. ॥1॥
lanka.84.cau2: The swoon left him and he came round again, and began to praise Hanumān's great strength. Hanumān said: Shame, shame on my valour, and shame on me, that you, enemy of the gods, are still alive. ॥2॥
lanka.84.cau3: With these words Hanumān carried Lakṣmaṇa back; Rāvaṇa saw it and was astonished. Śrī Rāma said: Brother, recall in your heart who you are: you devour Death himself and you protect the gods. ॥3॥
lanka.84.cau4: On hearing these words the compassionate Lakṣmaṇa sat up, and the dreadful spear went off into the sky. Taking up bow and arrows again he ran, and in eager haste came face to face with the enemy. ॥4॥
lanka.84.cha1: Swiftly again he shattered Rāvaṇa's chariot, killed the charioteer and left him reeling. His heart pierced by a hundred arrows, Rāvaṇa fell to the ground in still greater distress. Another charioteer laid him in a chariot and carried him at once to Laṅkā. Śrī Rāma's brother, a mass of glory, then bowed again at the Lord's feet. ॥1॥
lanka.84.do84: There, coming to his senses, Rāvaṇa set about performing a sacrifice. The fool, driven by obstinacy and steeped in ignorance, hoped for victory while setting himself against Śrī Rāma. ॥84॥
lanka.85.cau1: Here Vibhīṣaṇa learned all of it, and he went at once and told Śrī Rāma. My Lord, Rāvaṇa is performing a sacrifice; if it is accomplished, the wretch will not die. ॥1॥
lanka.85.cau2: Send warrior monkeys quickly, my Lord, to lay it waste, and Rāvaṇa will come out to fight. At daybreak the Lord sent out his finest warriors; Hanumān, Aṅgada and all the rest rushed off. ॥2॥
lanka.85.cau3: Leaping in sport, the monkeys scaled Laṅkā and entered Rāvaṇa's palace without fear. The moment they saw him at his sacrifice, all the monkeys were filled with fierce anger. ॥3॥
lanka.85.cau4: Shameless one, you ran from the battle and came home, and here you sit in a heron's meditation! So saying, Aṅgada kicked him; but the wretch, his mind set on his own ends, did not even look up. ॥4॥
lanka.85.cha1: When still he did not look, the monkeys in fury seized him with their teeth and kicked him. They dragged the women out by the hair, and the women cried out most piteously. Then he rose, furious as Death himself, and seizing the monkeys by the feet hurled them down. Meanwhile the monkeys had laid the sacrifice waste; seeing it, he lost heart. ॥1॥
lanka.85.do85: Having laid the sacrifice waste, the monkeys came back safe to Śrī Rāma. The demon set out in anger, giving up all hope of life. ॥85॥
lanka.86.cau1: As he set out, terrible ill omens appeared; vultures rose and alighted on his heads. But he was in the grip of death and would listen to no one; he said: Sound the drums of war. ॥1॥
lanka.86.cau2: The boundless army of the demons marched, with many elephants, chariots, foot soldiers and horsemen. How did the wicked rush at the Lord? As swarms of moths rush at a flame. ॥2॥
lanka.86.cau3: Here the gods offered praise and said: This one has brought dreadful calamity on us. Do not play with him any longer, Rāma; Sītā grieves exceedingly. ॥3॥
lanka.86.cau4: Hearing the gods, the Lord smiled; Śrī Rāma rose and set his arrows in order. His matted locks are bound firmly in a knot on his head, with flowers woven in here and there that shine among them. ॥4॥
lanka.86.cau5: Red-eyed, his body dark as a rain-cloud, he is the delight of the eyes of all the worlds. A sash girds his waist with the quiver fastened on it, and in his hand is the hard Śārṅga bow. ॥5॥
lanka.86.cha1: The Śārṅga bow is in his hand, and a fine quiver, a store of arrows, is fastened at his waist; his arms are stout, his chest broad and lovely, with the brāhmaṇa's footprint shining on it. Tulasīdāsa says: As soon as the Lord began to turn his bow and arrows in his hands, the universe, the elephants of the quarters, the Tortoise, the cosmic Serpent, the earth, the ocean and the mountains all shook. ॥1॥
lanka.86.do86: Seeing this splendour, the gods in delight rained down flowers without end. Glory, glory, glory to the treasury of compassion, the home of beauty, strength and virtue! ॥86॥
lanka.87.cau1: Meanwhile the demon army came on, dense and jostling. Seeing it, the monkey warriors advanced to meet it, like the massed clouds at the dissolution of the world. ॥1॥
lanka.87.cau2: Countless swords and sabres flashed, as if lightning gleamed in all ten directions. Elephants, chariots and horses raised a harsh din, like the roar of terrible clouds. ॥2॥
lanka.87.cau3: The monkeys' many tails spread across the sky, like lovely rainbows risen there. The dust rose like streams of rain, and arrows fell in a boundless shower of drops. ॥3॥
lanka.87.cau4: From both sides they struck with mountains, like thunderbolts falling again and again. Śrī Rāma in anger loosed a rain of arrows, and the demon host was wounded. ॥4॥
lanka.87.cau5: Struck by the arrows, the warriors screamed and, reeling round and round, fell to the ground here and there. Blood streamed from them like great waterfalls from mountains, and a river of blood flowed, striking fear into cowards. ॥5॥
lanka.87.cha1: That river of blood, fearsome to cowards and utterly unholy, flowed on. The two armies are its banks, the chariots its sand, the wheels its whirlpools; dreadful is its flow. Elephants, foot soldiers, horses, donkeys and mounts of every kind, past counting, are its water creatures; arrows, spears and javelins are its snakes, bows its waves, and shields its many tortoises. ॥1॥
lanka.87.do87: Warriors fall like trees on the bank, and marrow flows thick as foam. Cowards who see it there are afraid, while the hearts of true warriors are glad. ॥87॥
lanka.88.cau1: Ghosts, ghouls, vetālas, pramathas and huge, frightful shaggy goblins bathe in it. Crows and herons fly off with arms; one snatches from another and eats. ॥1॥
lanka.88.cau2: Some say: Fools, even in such plenty your want does not leave you! Wounded warriors lie groaning where they fell on the banks, like the dying laid half in the water here and there. ॥2॥
lanka.88.cau3: Vultures on the bank pull at entrails, like anglers intent on their fishing lines. Many warriors float down with birds riding on them, as though boating on the river. ॥3॥
lanka.88.cau4: Yoginīs fill skull-bowls with blood again and again and store them up; the wives of ghosts and ghouls dance in the sky. Cāmuṇḍās play warriors' skulls as cymbals and sing in many ways. ॥4॥
lanka.88.cau5: Packs of jackals crunch and gnaw, eat, howl, gorge themselves and snarl at one another. Millions of trunks roam about without heads, and heads lying on the ground cry: Victory, victory! ॥5॥
lanka.88.cha1: Heads cry Victory, victory, and fierce headless trunks run about. Tangled among skulls and swords they grapple, and great warriors bring other warriors down. Proud in Śrī Rāma's strength, the monkeys crush the demon hordes. Slain by Śrī Rāma's swarms of arrows, warriors sleep in the courtyard of battle. ॥1॥
lanka.88.do88: Rāvaṇa thought in his heart: The demons have been destroyed. I am alone and the monkeys and bears are many; I will work boundless māyā. ॥88॥
lanka.89.cau1: The gods saw the Lord on foot, and great distress arose in their hearts. Indra at once sent his own chariot, and Mātali brought it gladly. ॥1॥
lanka.89.cau2: The chariot was a mass of radiance, divine and matchless; the king of Kosala mounted it with joy. Four lovely, spirited horses drew it, ageless and deathless, swift as thought. ॥2॥
lanka.89.cau3: Seeing Śrī Rāma in the chariot, the monkeys gained fresh strength and charged. Unable to bear the monkeys' onslaught, Rāvaṇa then spread his māyā. ॥3॥
lanka.89.cau4: Śrī Rāma alone was untouched by that māyā; Lakṣmaṇa and the monkeys took it for real. In the demon army the monkeys saw many Lords of Kosala, each with his younger brother. ॥4॥
lanka.89.cha1: Seeing many Rāmas and Lakṣmaṇas, the monkeys and bears were struck with groundless fear. Lakṣmaṇa with them, they stood wherever they were, staring like figures in a painting. Seeing his army bewildered, the Lord of Kosala smiled and set an arrow to his bow, and in the twinkling of an eye Śrī Hari took the māyā away; the whole monkey host rejoiced. ॥1॥
lanka.89.do89: Then Śrī Rāma looked round at them all and spoke in a deep voice: You warriors are all worn out; now watch the single combat. ॥89॥
lanka.90.cau1: So saying, Śrī Rāma drove the chariot forward and bowed his head to the lotus feet of the brāhmaṇas. Then rage filled the heart of Rāvaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, and he rushed at him, roaring and threatening. ॥1॥
lanka.90.cau2: Rāvaṇa said: Those fighters you defeated in battle, ascetic, mark this, were nothing like me. My name is Rāvaṇa, my fame is known to the world, and the guardians of the worlds lie in my prison. ॥2॥
lanka.90.cau3: You killed Khara, Dūṣaṇa and Virādha, and slew poor Vāli like a hunter. You destroyed hosts of demon warriors and killed Kumbhakarṇa and Meghanāda. ॥3॥
lanka.90.cau4: Today I will settle the whole feud, king, unless you run from the battle. This day I will deliver you to Death for certain; you have fallen into the hands of the hard Rāvaṇa. ॥4॥
lanka.90.cau5: Hearing his harsh words and knowing him doomed, Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, laughed and said: All your greatness is true, quite true; but do not prattle, show your manhood. ॥5॥
lanka.90.cha1: Do not destroy your fair fame by prattling; hear what is right, and pardon me. In the world there are three kinds of men, like the pāṭala, the mango and the jackfruit. One gives flowers, one flowers and fruit, and one bears fruit alone. So one man talks; another talks and acts; and one acts and does not go about talking of it. ॥1॥
lanka.90.do90: Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, Rāvaṇa laughed and said: You would teach me wisdom! You were not afraid when you made this enmity; now your life has grown dear to you. ॥90॥
lanka.91.cau1: With these harsh words, the furious Rāvaṇa began to loose arrows like thunderbolts. Arrows of many shapes sped out and covered the quarters, the spaces between them, the sky and the earth. ॥1॥
lanka.91.cau2: Śrī Rāma loosed a fire arrow, and in an instant the demon's shafts were burnt up. In vexation he hurled a keen spear; with an arrow the Lord sent it back. ॥2॥
lanka.91.cau3: He flings millions of discuses and tridents; the Lord cuts them down and wards them off without effort. How do Rāvaṇa's arrows come to nothing? As all the wicked man's desires do. ॥3॥
lanka.91.cau4: Then he struck the charioteer with a hundred arrows; he fell to the ground crying: Glory to Śrī Rāma! Śrī Rāma graciously raised the charioteer up; then the Lord grew fiercely angry. ॥4॥
lanka.91.cha1: When Śrī Rāma turned in anger on his foe in battle, the arrows stirred restlessly in his quiver. At the fierce twang of his bow all the man-eaters stood rigid, as if struck by a seizure. Mandodarī's heart shook and trembled; the Tortoise, the earth and the mountains were afraid. The elephants of the quarters trumpeted, gripping the earth with their tusks; watching the spectacle, the gods laughed. ॥1॥
lanka.91.do91: He drew the bow back to his ear and loosed terrible shafts. Śrī Rāma's flights of arrows sped on like writhing snakes. ॥91॥
lanka.92.cau1: The arrows flew like winged serpents; first they killed the charioteer and the horses. They shattered the chariot and struck down the flag and pennon; Rāvaṇa roared mightily, but within, his strength was spent. ॥1॥
lanka.92.cau2: Vexed, he quickly mounted another chariot and loosed missiles and weapons of many kinds. All his efforts failed, as do those of a mind bent on harming others. ॥2॥
lanka.92.cau3: Then Rāvaṇa hurled ten lances and struck the four horses to the ground. Raising the horses up, Śrī Rāma in anger drew his bow and loosed his arrows. ॥3॥
lanka.92.cau4: Śrī Rāma's arrows went forth in a line like bees, to roam the lotus-grove of Rāvaṇa's heads. He struck each of the ten brows with ten arrows; they passed right through, and blood ran in torrents. ॥4॥
lanka.92.cau5: Streaming blood, the mighty demon charged; once again the Lord set arrows to the bow. Śrī Rāma loosed thirty arrows and brought the heads, with the arms, down to the ground. ॥5॥
lanka.92.cau6: As soon as they were cut they grew anew; Śrī Rāma cut off the arms and heads again. Many times the Lord struck off arms and heads, and as they fell they were at once made new. ॥6॥
lanka.92.cau7: The Lord of Kosala, who loves his sport, keeps cutting off the arms and heads. Heads and arms filled the sky, like countless Ketus and Rāhus. ॥7॥
lanka.92.cha1: It was as though many Rāhus and Ketus were racing along the paths of the sky, streaming blood. Śrī Rāma's fierce arrows keep striking them, so they never get to fall to the ground. Each arrow has pierced a cluster of heads, and as they fly through the sky they look as if the sun's rays in anger were threading Rāhus on strings here and there. ॥1॥
lanka.92.do92: The more the Lord strikes off his heads, the more endless they grow, as desire grows fresh day after day when the objects of sense are indulged. ॥92॥
lanka.93.cau1: Seeing his heads multiply, Rāvaṇa forgot about death, and a fierce anger rose in him. The deluded, overweening one roared and charged, all ten bows drawn. ॥1॥
lanka.93.cau2: On the field of battle Rāvaṇa raged and buried Śrī Rāma's chariot under a shower of arrows. For one daṇḍa (about twenty-four minutes) the chariot could not be seen at all, as though the sun had hidden in mist. ॥2॥
lanka.93.cau3: When the gods cried out in dismay, the Lord grew angry and took up his bow. Warding off the arrows, he cut off the enemy's heads, and they filled the quarters and the spaces between them, the sky and the earth. ॥3॥
lanka.93.cau4: The severed heads race along the paths of the sky, shouting victory and spreading fear: Where is Lakṣmaṇa? Where is Sugrīva, king of the monkeys? Where is Rāma, hero of the Raghus, lord of Kosala? ॥4॥
lanka.93.cha1: The hosts of heads rushed on, crying: Where is Rāma? At the sight of them the monkeys fled. Śrī Rāma smiled, set arrows to his bow and pierced the heads squarely. Many Kālikās gathered in band upon band, garlands of heads in their hands, as if, fresh from bathing in a river of blood, they were off to worship the banyan of war. ॥1॥
lanka.93.do93: Then Rāvaṇa, enraged, let loose a fearsome lance. It flew at Vibhīṣaṇa head-on, like Death's own rod. ॥93॥
lanka.94.cau1: Seeing that dreadful lance coming, Śrī Rāma thought: My vow is to end the distress of those who bow to me. At once he put Vibhīṣaṇa behind him and, standing in front, took the spear upon himself. ॥1॥
lanka.94.cau2: The lance struck and he swooned a little; it was the Lord's play, but the gods were thrown into distress. Seeing the Lord in pain, Vibhīṣaṇa seized a mace in his hand and rushed forward in anger. ॥2॥
lanka.94.cau3: Vibhīṣaṇa said: You ill-starred, wicked, base, evil-minded wretch, you have made enemies of gods, men, sages and nāgas. You offered your heads to Śiva with reverence, and so for each one you have received millions. ॥3॥
lanka.94.cau4: That is why, villain, you have lived till now; but now your death is dancing over your head. Fool, you turn your back on Rāma and still want prosperity? So saying, he struck him with the mace full in the chest. ॥4॥
lanka.94.cha1: As the mace's terrible, crushing blow struck him in the middle of the chest, Rāvaṇa fell to the ground. Blood streaming from his ten mouths, he recovered and rushed in again, full of rage. The two mighty ones grappled in a wrestling bout, face to face, each striking the other. Proud in the strength of Śrī Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa does not count him as worth the least trifle. ॥1॥
lanka.94.do94: Umā, did Vibhīṣaṇa ever so much as look Rāvaṇa in the face? Now he grapples with him like Death itself: such is the power of Śrī Rāma. ॥94॥
lanka.95.cau1: Seeing Vibhīṣaṇa sorely wearied, Hanumān came running with a mountain in his hands. He struck down the chariot, the horses and the charioteer, and kicked Rāvaṇa in the middle of the chest. ॥1॥
lanka.95.cau2: His body trembling hard, Rāvaṇa still kept his feet; Vibhīṣaṇa went to where the protector of his people stood. Then Rāvaṇa challenged Hanumān and struck him, and Hanumān rose into the sky with his tail spread out. ॥2॥
lanka.95.cau3: Rāvaṇa grabbed the tail, and Hanumān flew off with him; then the mighty Hanumān wheeled round and grappled with him. Equal fighters both, they battle in the sky, each hitting the other in his anger. ॥3॥
lanka.95.cau4: Shining in the sky, they plied trick upon trick and feat upon feat of strength, like a mountain of lampblack locked in battle with Mount Sumeru. The demon would not fall to cunning or to force; so Hanumān, son of the Wind, remembered the Lord. ॥4॥
lanka.95.cha1: Remembering Śrī Rāma, steadfast Hanumān challenged Rāvaṇa and struck him. Both fall to the ground, rise and fight again; the gods cried victory to the pair of them. Seeing Hanumān hard pressed, the monkeys and bears ran in, beside themselves with anger. But Rāvaṇa, drunk with battle, trampled all those brave warriors with the fierce might of his arms. ॥1॥
lanka.95.do95: Then, at Śrī Rāma's rallying call, the fierce monkeys charged. Seeing how great the monkeys' strength was, Rāvaṇa brought out his deceit. ॥95॥
lanka.96.cau1: For a moment he vanished; then the wicked one appeared in many forms. As many bears and monkeys as there were in Śrī Rāma's army, so many Rāvaṇas appeared on every side. ॥1॥
lanka.96.cau2: The monkeys saw Rāvaṇas beyond counting, and bears and monkeys fled this way and that. The monkeys ran, their courage gone, crying: Save us, save us, O Lakṣmaṇa, O hero of the Raghus! ॥2॥
lanka.96.cau3: Millions of Rāvaṇas rush about in all ten directions, roaring dreadfully, harshly, terrifyingly. All the gods took fright and fled, saying: Brothers, give up all hope of victory now. ॥3॥
lanka.96.cau4: One Rāvaṇa alone conquered all the gods; now there are many of him. Look for caves in the mountains. Only Brahmā, Śiva and the wise sages held their ground, all those who had known something of the Lord's greatness. ॥4॥
lanka.96.cha1: Those who knew the Lord's might stayed fearless, but the monkeys took those enemies to be real. All the monkeys and bears broke and fled in panic, crying: Protect us, compassionate Lord! Hanumān, Aṅgada, Nīla and Nala, mighty and valiant in war, fought on and crush the Rāvaṇas by millions upon millions, warriors sprung up like shoots from a soil of deceit. ॥1॥
lanka.96.do96: Seeing the gods and the monkeys in distress, the Lord of Kosala laughed, and fitting a single arrow to his bow Śārṅga, he slew all the Rāvaṇas. ॥96॥
lanka.97.cau1: In a moment the Lord had cut away all the illusion, just as the dark splits and scatters once the sun comes up. With but one Rāvaṇa before them, the gods were glad; they returned and showered the Lord with flowers. ॥1॥
lanka.97.cau2: Śrī Rāma raised his arm and brought the monkeys back; back they came, calling to one another. Strengthened by the Lord, the bears and monkeys ran forward and, swift and fired up, came onto the battlefield. ॥2॥
lanka.97.cau3: Seeing the gods singing praises, Rāvaṇa said: So by their reckoning I am only one now! Fools, you have always been the ones I beat. So saying, he rushed up into the sky in fury. ॥3॥
lanka.97.cau4: The gods fled, crying out in terror. Rāvaṇa shouted: Villains, where can you run from me? Seeing the gods in distress, Aṅgada ran up, leapt, seized him by the foot and brought him down to the ground. ॥4॥
lanka.97.cha1: Having seized him, thrown him down and kicked him, Vāli's son went back to the Lord. Recovering, the ten-headed one rose and roared with a dreadful, grating roar. In his arrogance he strung all ten bows and, fitting arrows to them, rained down arrows in plenty. He left every warrior wounded and frantic with fear, and he exulted to see his own strength. ॥1॥
lanka.97.do97: Then Śrī Rāma cut off Rāvaṇa's heads and arms, his arrows and his bows; but they grew back, many more of them, as sins committed at a holy place grow. ॥97॥
lanka.98.cau1: When they saw the enemy's heads and arms grow back, the bears and monkeys were filled with rage. This fool does not die though his heads and arms are cut! The bear and monkey warriors rushed at him in fury. ॥1॥
lanka.98.cau2: Aṅgada son of Vāli, Hanumān son of the Wind, Nala, Nīla, Sugrīva king of the monkeys, and the mighty Dvivida pelt him with trees and mountains; he catches those same mountains and trees and strikes the monkeys with them. ॥2॥
lanka.98.cau3: One tears the enemy's body with his nails and runs off; another kicks him and runs. Then Nala and Nīla clambered up onto his heads and ripped at his brows with their nails. ॥3॥
lanka.98.cau4: At the sight of the blood he was sorely dismayed, and he stretched out his arms to seize them. They slipped every grasp and roamed about on his hands, two bees at large in a forest of lotuses. ॥4॥
lanka.98.cau5: Furious, he sprang and seized both of them once more; he was hurling them to the earth when they wrenched his arms round and escaped. Then, furious, he took up his ten bows and wounded the monkeys with his arrows. ॥5॥
lanka.98.cau6: Rāvaṇa had struck Hanumān and the rest of the monkeys senseless, and evening had come; he was glad. Seeing all the monkey heroes senseless, Jāmbavān, steadfast in battle, ran forward. ॥6॥
lanka.98.cau7: The bears with him, carrying mountains and trees, began to strike Rāvaṇa, challenging him again and again. Mighty Rāvaṇa flew into a rage and, seizing them by the feet, dashed warrior after warrior to the ground. ॥7॥
lanka.98.cau8: Seeing his host struck down, the king of the bears in his anger kicked Rāvaṇa full in the chest. ॥8॥
lanka.98.cha1: The fierce blow of the kick to his chest left Rāvaṇa reeling, and he fell from his chariot to the earth. He was clutching bears in all twenty hands, like bees lodged in lotuses at night. Finding him senseless, the king of the bears kicked him once more and went to the Lord. Knowing that night had come, the charioteer laid him in the chariot and set about bringing him round. ॥1॥
lanka.98.do98: Their swoon over, all the bears and monkeys came to the Lord. All the demons, in great dread, stayed gathered round Rāvaṇa. ॥98॥
lanka.99.cau1: That very night Trijaṭā went to Sītā and told her all that had happened. When Sītā heard how the enemy's heads and arms kept growing, a great fear filled her heart. ॥1॥
lanka.99.cau2: Her face clouded and anxiety rose in her mind; then Sītā said to Trijaṭā: Mother, why do you not tell me what will happen? How is he to die, this tormentor of the world? ॥2॥
lanka.99.cau3: Even with his heads cut off by Śrī Rāma's arrows he does not die; Fate is turning everything the wrong way. What keeps him alive is my ill fortune, which tore me from Śrī Hari's lotus feet. ॥3॥
lanka.99.cau4: The Fate that conjured the false golden deer of deceit is still angry with me; the Fate that made me bear unbearable sorrow and made me speak bitter words to Lakṣmaṇa, ॥4॥
lanka.99.cau5: that has taken aim again and again and struck me with the heavy, poisoned arrows of separation from Śrī Rāma, and that keeps me alive even in such sorrow: that same Fate keeps him alive, and no other. ॥5॥
lanka.99.cau6: Jānakī laments in many ways, recalling again and again the treasury of compassion. Trijaṭā said: Hear me, princess. Let an arrow strike the gods' enemy in the heart, and he dies. ॥6॥
lanka.99.cau7: But the Lord does not strike him in the heart, because you, Vaidehī, dwell in his heart. ॥7॥
lanka.99.cha1: The Lord reasons: Jānakī dwells in his heart, and in Jānakī's heart is my dwelling; in my belly are many worlds, and once the arrow strikes, all of them will perish. Hearing this, Sītā felt great joy and great sorrow at once; seeing it, Trijaṭā spoke again: Listen, fair one, this is how the enemy will now die; put away your great doubt. ॥1॥
lanka.99.do99: As his heads are cut off he will grow frantic, and his mind will lose its hold on you. Then Śrī Rāma, who knows all, will strike Rāvaṇa in the heart. ॥99॥
lanka.100.cau1: With these words, after comforting her in many ways, Trijaṭā went back to her own house. Remembering Śrī Rāma's nature, Vaidehī was seized by the bitter pain of separation. ॥1॥
lanka.100.cau2: She finds fault with the night and with the moon in many ways: the night has become as long as an age and does not pass. Grieving in separation from Śrī Rāma, Jānakī weeps bitterly within her heart. ॥2॥
lanka.100.cau3: When the burning of separation in her heart grew unbearable, her left eye and arm throbbed. She read it as a good omen and grew calm within: now the compassionate Śrī Rāma will come to me. ॥3॥
lanka.100.cau4: Meanwhile, at midnight, Rāvaṇa woke and began to rage at his charioteer: Fool, you took me away from the battlefield! Shame, shame on you, you base, dull-witted wretch! ॥4॥
lanka.100.cau5: Holding his feet, the charioteer talked him round in many ways; at daybreak Rāvaṇa mounted his chariot and charged again. When they heard that the ten-headed one was coming, a great commotion broke out in the monkey host. ॥5॥
lanka.100.cau6: The great warriors uprooted mountains and trees on every side and charged, grinding their teeth. ॥6॥
lanka.100.cha1: Fearsome monkeys and dreadful bears rushed in, gripping mountains. They strike in towering rage, and under their blows the demons fled. The strong monkeys broke the demon host and then hemmed Rāvaṇa in again. From all four sides they slapped him and tore at his body with their nails, until he was in agony. ॥1॥
lanka.100.do100: Seeing how mighty the monkeys were, Rāvaṇa thought it over, and vanishing in the twinkling of an eye, he spread out his illusion far and wide. ॥100॥
lanka.101.cha1: When he worked this deceit, fierce creatures appeared: vampires, ghosts and ghouls, holding bows and iron arrows in their hands. ॥1॥
lanka.101.cha2: Yoginīs grip swords, and in one hand they hold human skulls. Drinking fresh blood, they dance and sing many songs. ॥2॥
lanka.101.cha3: They raise a terrible cry of Seize! Kill!, and the sound fills every quarter. They rush with gaping mouths to devour; then the monkeys began to flee. ॥3॥
lanka.101.cha4: Wherever the monkeys run, they see fire burning there. The monkeys and bears were distraught; then sand began to rain down. ॥4॥
lanka.101.cha5: Leaving the monkeys stunned and helpless here and there, Rāvaṇa roared again. All the warriors, Lakṣmaṇa and Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, among them, fell senseless. ॥5॥
lanka.101.cha6: Crying Alas, Rāma! Alas, Lord of the Raghus!, the great warriors wring their hands. Having thus broken the strength of all, he worked another deceit. ॥6॥
lanka.101.cha7: He made many Hanumāns appear, who rushed forward holding rocks. Forming hosts on every side, they went and surrounded Śrī Rāma. ॥7॥
lanka.101.cha8: Kill him! Seize him! Do not let him go! they cry, gnashing their teeth with tails raised. Tails gleam in all ten directions, and in their midst stands the king of Kosala. ॥8॥
lanka.101.cha1_2: In their midst the beautiful dark body of the king of Kosala shone with such splendour as if many rainbows had made a fine hedge round a tall tamāla tree. Seeing the Lord so, the gods felt joy and grief at once in their hearts and cried: Victory, victory, victory! Then Śrī Rāma, in anger, dispelled the illusion with a single arrow in the twinkling of an eye. ॥1॥
lanka.101.cha2_2: The illusion gone, the monkeys and bears were glad, and every one of them turned back with trees and mountains in hand. Śrī Rāma loosed a multitude of arrows, and Rāvaṇa's arms and heads fell to the ground once more. Those who might sing of the deeds of the battle between Śrī Rāma and Rāvaṇa for many aeons, though they were hundreds of Śeṣas, Sarasvatīs, Vedas and poets, would still not reach the end of them. ॥2॥
lanka.101.do101क: Of its many glories dull-witted Tulasīdāsa has told a few, just as a fly rises into the sky only as far as its own strength allows.
lanka.101.do101ख: His heads and arms were cut off many times, yet the warrior lord of Laṅkā did not die. The Lord is at play, but gods, siddhas and sages are distressed to see the ordeal.
lanka.102.cau1: As they are cut, the heads multiply, as greed grows with every gain. The enemy would not die and the toil had grown great; then Śrī Rāma looked towards Vibhīṣaṇa. ॥1॥
lanka.102.cau2: Umā, the Lord at whose will Death itself dies is testing his servant's love. Vibhīṣaṇa said: Listen, all-knowing one, lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow to you, giver of joy to gods and sages. ॥2॥
lanka.102.cau3: In the hollow of his navel lies nectar; it is by its power, my Lord, that Rāvaṇa lives. On hearing Vibhīṣaṇa's words, the compassionate Lord gladly took up fearsome arrows in his hand. ॥3॥
lanka.102.cau4: Then ill omens of many kinds began: donkeys, jackals and many dogs howled; birds cried out, foretelling distress for the world, and comets appeared here and there in the sky. ॥4॥
lanka.102.cau5: A fierce burning glow spread through all ten quarters, and the sun was eclipsed though it was not the day for it. Mandodarī's heart trembled violently, and the images shed water from their eyes. ॥5॥
lanka.102.cha1: Images wept, thunderbolts fell from the sky, a fierce wind blew and the earth quaked. Clouds rained blood, hair and dust; who could tell how many ill omens there were? Seeing countless portents, the gods in the sky grew distraught and cried: Victory! Victory! Knowing the gods to be afraid, the compassionate Lord fitted arrows to his bow. ॥1॥
lanka.102.do102: Drawing the bow back to his ear, he loosed thirty-one arrows. Śrī Rāma's arrows sped on like great serpents of death. ॥102॥
lanka.103.cau1: One arrow dried up the pool at his navel; the others struck his arms and heads in fury. The arrows went off carrying the heads and arms, and the trunk, without heads or arms, danced upon the ground. ॥1॥
lanka.103.cau2: The trunk rushed about so fiercely that the earth sank beneath it; then the Lord struck it with an arrow and cut it in two. Dying, he roared with a great and terrible cry: Where is Rāma? Let me challenge him and kill him in battle. ॥2॥
lanka.103.cau3: As Rāvaṇa fell, the earth shook, and the oceans, rivers, elephants of the quarters and mountains were thrown into turmoil. He fell to the ground with his two halves stretched out, crushing hosts of bears and monkeys beneath them. ॥3॥
lanka.103.cau4: The arrows laid the arms and heads before Mandodarī and went back to where the Lord of the world was. They all went and entered the quiver; seeing this, the gods beat their kettledrums. ॥4॥
lanka.103.cau5: His radiance passed into the Lord's face; seeing it, Śiva and four-faced Brahmā rejoiced. The whole universe rang with the cry of victory: Glory to the hero of the Raghus, mighty of arm! ॥5॥
lanka.103.cau6: Hosts of gods and sages shower flowers: Glory to the compassionate one, glory, glory to Mukunda! ॥6॥
lanka.103.cha1: Glory to you, Lord, source of grace, Mukunda, remover of the pairs of opposites, giver of joy to those who come for refuge; destroyer of the hosts of the wicked, supreme cause, ever compassionate, all-pervading one. The gods, full of joy, shower flowers, and kettledrums resound loudly. On the field of battle Śrī Rāma's limbs took on the beauty of many Kāmadevas. ॥1॥
lanka.103.cha2: On his head the crown of matted locks, with flowers here and there among them, looks most lovely, as if stars were shining with sheets of lightning on a blue mountain. As he twirls arrows and bow with his mighty arms, the drops of blood on his body look very fine, as if red munia birds were perched on a tamāla tree in great contentment. ॥2॥
lanka.103.do103: Showering his gracious glance upon them, the Lord freed the hosts of gods from fear. All the bears and monkeys rejoiced: Glory to Mukunda, abode of joy! ॥103॥
lanka.104.cau1: At the sight of her husband's heads Mandodarī fainted in anguish and fell to the ground. Crowds of young women rose and ran, weeping; they lifted her up and came to Rāvaṇa. ॥1॥
lanka.104.cau2: Seeing their husband's state, they cried aloud; their hair came loose and they took no care of their bodies. They beat their breasts in many ways and, weeping, recounted his might. ॥2॥
