lanka.104.cau3: They said: My lord, by your might the earth was ever trembling, and fire, moon and sun lost their brightness. That body whose weight Śeṣa and the cosmic tortoise could not bear lies on the ground, covered in dust. ॥3॥
lanka.104.cau4: Varuṇa, Kubera, Indra and the Wind: not one of them could stand firm before you in battle. By the strength of your arms, my lord, you conquered Time and Yama; today you lie like one who has no protector. ॥4॥
lanka.104.cau5: Your lordship is known throughout the world; the strength of your sons and kin is beyond telling. Turned away from Śrī Rāma, you have come to such a state that not one of your line is left to mourn you. ॥5॥
lanka.104.cau6: My lord, all of Brahmā's creation was under your sway, and the guardians of the quarters, afraid, bowed down to you every day. Now jackals eat your heads and arms; there is nothing improper in this for one who turns from Śrī Rāma. ॥6॥
lanka.104.cau7: Under the sway of Death, my husband, you would not heed what you were told, and took the Lord of all things moving and unmoving for a man. ॥7॥
lanka.104.cha1: You took for a man Śrī Hari himself, the fire that burns the forest of demons. Beloved, you did not worship the compassionate one, to whom Śiva, Brahmā and the gods bow. From birth this body of yours delighted in harming others and was full of a flood of sins. Even to you Śrī Rāma has given his own abode; I bow to Rāma, the Brahman free from every ill. ॥1॥
lanka.104.do104: Ah, my lord, there is no other ocean of mercy like Śrī Rāma. The Lord has given you the state that hosts of yogīs find hard to attain. ॥104॥
lanka.105.cau1: Hearing Mandodarī's words, gods, sages and siddhas all were glad. Brahmā, Maheśa, Nārada, Sanaka and his brothers, and all the great sages who speak of the highest truth ॥1॥
lanka.105.cau2: gazed their fill on Śrī Rāma and, lost in love, were all filled with joy. Vibhīṣaṇa saw all the women weeping, and went to them with a heavy heart. ॥2॥
lanka.105.cau3: Seeing his brother's state, he grieved; then the Lord gave a command to his younger brother. Lakṣmaṇa consoled him in many ways, and then Vibhīṣaṇa came back to the Lord. ॥3॥
lanka.105.cau4: The Lord turned a gracious glance on him and said: Leave off all grief and carry out the last rites. Obeying the Lord's command, and bearing in mind the place and the time, he performed the rites as prescribed. ॥4॥
lanka.105.do105: Mandodarī and all the others offered him libations of sesame and water, and went to the palace, recounting in their minds the many virtues of Śrī Rāma. ॥105॥
lanka.106.cau1: Vibhīṣaṇa came and bowed his head again; then the ocean of mercy called his younger brother. He said: You, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Aṅgada, Nala, Nīla, Jāmbavān and Hanumān, wise in counsel, ॥1॥
lanka.106.cau2: go all together with Vibhīṣaṇa and perform his installation, said Śrī Rāma. Bound by my father's word, I do not enter a city; so I send the monkeys and my brother, who are as my own self. ॥2॥
lanka.106.cau3: The monkeys left at once on hearing the Lord's words, and there they set about arranging the coronation. They respectfully placed Vibhīṣaṇa on the throne, and once the tilaka was done they began to sing his praise. ॥3॥
lanka.106.cau4: All of them bowed their heads with joined palms, and came with Vibhīṣaṇa to the Lord. Then Śrī Rāma called the monkeys to him and, speaking kind words, made them all happy. ॥4॥
lanka.106.cha1: He made them happy with words like nectar: It is by your strength that the enemy has been slain. Vibhīṣaṇa has gained the kingdom, and your fame will stay ever new in the three worlds. Those who sing with deep love of your auspicious glory together with mine will cross the boundless ocean of worldly existence without effort. ॥1॥
lanka.106.do106: The hosts of monkeys hear the Lord's words and cannot have enough of them. Again and again they all bow their heads and clasp his lotus feet. ॥106॥
lanka.107.cau1: Then the Lord called Hanumān to him. The Lord said: Go to Laṅkā. Tell Jānakī the news, and come back with word of her welfare. ॥1॥
lanka.107.cau2: Then Hanumān came into the city; hearing of it, the demons and demonesses came running. They honoured him in many ways, and then showed him Janaka's daughter. ॥2॥
lanka.107.cau3: Hanumān bowed to her from a distance, and Jānakī knew him for Śrī Rāma's messenger. Sītā said: Tell me, dear one, is all well with the Lord, abode of grace, and his younger brother and the monkey army? ॥3॥
lanka.107.cau4: Hanumān said: Mother, the Lord of Kosala is well in every way; he has conquered Rāvaṇa in battle. Vibhīṣaṇa has gained a kingdom that will not be shaken. Hearing Hanumān's words, Sītā's heart filled with joy. ॥4॥
lanka.107.cha1: Her mind overjoyed, her body thrilling, her eyes full of tears, Sītā, who is Ramā herself, said again and again: What can I give you, Hanumān? In the three worlds there is nothing at all to equal these words. Hanumān said: Listen, Mother: today, beyond doubt, I have gained the kingdom of the whole world, for I see Śrī Rāma, victorious in battle over the enemy host, safe and well, with his brother. ॥1॥
lanka.107.do107: Sītā said: Listen, my son Hanumān: may every virtue make its home in your heart, and may the king of Kosala, together with Lakṣmaṇa, who is Ananta, always look on you with favour. ॥107॥
lanka.108.cau1: Now, dear son, make such an effort that my eyes may see the Lord in his dark and tender form. Then Hanumān went to Śrī Rāma and told him that Sītā was well. ॥1॥
lanka.108.cau2: Hearing the message, the ornament of the solar race sent for Prince Aṅgada and Vibhīṣaṇa and said: Go with the son of the Wind, and bring Sītā here with due honour. ॥2॥
lanka.108.cau3: They all went straight to Sītā; every one of the demonesses there was serving her meekly. Vibhīṣaṇa quickly instructed them, and they bathed her with every kind of care. ॥3॥
lanka.108.cau4: They put many kinds of ornaments on her, then made ready a fine palanquin and brought it. Remembering the loving Śrī Rāma, the abode of bliss, Sītā joyfully mounted it. ॥4॥
lanka.108.cau5: Guards with canes in hand walked on every side, and all went along with hearts full of joy. The bears and monkeys all came to see her, and the guards rushed angrily to hold them off. ॥5॥
lanka.108.cau6: Śrī Rāma said: Friend, do as I say: bring Sītā on foot, so that the monkeys may look on her as on a mother. So the Lord Śrī Rāma said, smiling. ॥6॥
lanka.108.cau7: The bears and monkeys rejoiced at the Lord's words, and the gods showered many flowers from the sky. Sītā had earlier been placed in the fire; now the Witness within all wished to bring her forth. ॥7॥
lanka.108.do108: For this reason the treasury of compassion spoke a few harsh words. Hearing them, all the demonesses began to grieve. ॥108॥
lanka.109.cau1: Sītā, pure in mind, deed and word, took the Lord's words upon her head and said: Lakṣmaṇa, assist me in this rite of dharma, and kindle a fire at once. ॥1॥
lanka.109.cau2: Lakṣmaṇa heard Sītā's words, steeped in the pain of separation, in discernment, in dharma and in right counsel. His eyes filled with tears and he stood with palms joined; he too could say nothing to the Lord. ॥2॥
lanka.109.cau3: Seeing Śrī Rāma's look, Lakṣmaṇa ran, kindled the fire and brought plenty of wood. Seeing the fierce fire, Sītā felt joy in her heart, and no fear at all. ॥3॥
lanka.109.cau4: Sītā said: If in mind, word and deed there is in my heart no refuge other than Śrī Rāma, then may Fire, who knows the state of every heart, be as sandalwood to me. ॥4॥
lanka.109.cha1: Remembering the Lord, Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, entered the fire as if it were sandalwood. She hailed the Lord of Kosala, whose feet, worshipped by Śiva, she loves with a love wholly pure. Her reflected image and the stain of worldly reproach burned away in the blazing fire. No one perceived the Lord's play; gods, siddhas and sages stood in the sky, watching. ॥1॥
lanka.109.cha2: Then Fire took a bodily form and held the hand of the true Śrī (Sītā), known to the Vedas and the world, and, as the Ocean of Milk once gave Indirā to Viṣṇu, brought her and gave her to Śrī Rāma. She shone at Śrī Rāma's left side, her beauty exceedingly lovely, as though a bud of golden lotus stood beside a fresh blue lotus. ॥2॥
lanka.109.do109क: The gods joyfully shower flowers, and kettledrums sound in the sky. Kinnaras sing, and celestial women dance, riding in their aerial cars. ॥109 (क)॥
lanka.109.do109ख: The beauty of the Lord with Sītā is measureless and boundless. Seeing it, the bears and monkeys rejoiced and cried: Glory to the Lord of the Raghus, essence of all joy! ॥109 (ख)॥
lanka.110.cau1: Then, given leave by Śrī Rāma, Mātali bowed his head at his feet and departed. Then came the gods, ever intent on their own ends, speaking as if they sought only the highest good. ॥1॥
lanka.110.cau2: Friend of the lowly, compassionate king of the Raghus, O God, you have shown mercy to the gods. Bent on enmity against the whole world, this lustful villain, who walked the crooked path, has fallen by his own sin. ॥2॥
lanka.110.cau3: You are the imperishable Brahman, the same towards all, ever unvarying and by nature detached; without parts, beyond the guṇas, unborn, sinless, untouched by ill, unconquerable, of unfailing power and full of compassion. ॥3॥
lanka.110.cau4: You took the forms of the Fish, the Tortoise, the Boar, the Man-Lion, the Dwarf and Paraśurāma. Whenever the gods have suffered, my Lord, you yourself have taken many bodies and ended it. ॥4॥
lanka.110.cau5: This wicked one was impure, ever hostile to the gods, sunk in desire, greed and pride, and full of wrath; that this chief of the vile should attain your state fills our minds with wonder. ॥5॥
lanka.110.cau6: We gods, though highly qualified, were bent on self-interest and forgot devotion to the Lord. We have always been caught in the current of worldly existence. Now, Lord, we have come for refuge: protect us. ॥6॥
lanka.110.do110: Their prayer made, all the gods and siddhas stood where they were with palms joined. Then Brahmā, his body thrilling with deep love, began to praise him: ॥110॥
lanka.111.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, ever the home of bliss, O Hari, O Lord of the Raghus who bears bow and arrows. O Lord, you are a lion to the elephant of worldly existence, splitting it apart; ocean of virtues, all-wise, Master, all-pervading one. ॥1॥
lanka.111.cau2: Your form has the beauty of many Kāmadevas and is beyond compare; siddhas, great sages and poets sing your virtues. Your glory purifies; as Garuḍa in anger seizes a great serpent, so you seized Rāvaṇa. ॥2॥
lanka.111.cau3: Lord, you delight your devotees and break their grief and fear; you are ever free of anger, pure awareness. Your incarnation is noble and of boundless virtues; you destroy the earth's burden and are knowledge in its fullness. ॥3॥
lanka.111.cau4: Unborn, all-pervading, one, ever without beginning: compassionate Rāma, I bow to you with joy. Ornament of Raghu's line, slayer of Dūṣaṇa, you made a king of the lowly Vibhīṣaṇa. ॥4॥
lanka.111.cau5: Treasury of virtue and knowledge, free of pride, unborn, all-pervading and stainless: Rāma, I bow to you always. The might and strength of your arms are fierce; you are most skilled in rooting out the hosts of the wicked. ॥5॥
lanka.111.cau6: Kind without cause to the lowly and seeking their good, abode of beauty, I bow to you with Sītā, who is Ramā herself. You carry souls across worldly existence, you are beyond cause and effect, and you take away the dreadful faults born in the mind. ॥6॥
lanka.111.cau7: You bear lovely arrows, bow and quiver; your eyes are like red lotuses; you are the best of kings. Temple of joy, beautiful, Lord of Śrī, you quell pride, lust and false attachment. ॥7॥
lanka.111.cau8: You are faultless, undivided, beyond the reach of the senses; you are ever all forms, and yet you have not become all things. So the Vedas say; it is no idle tale: just as the sun and its light are distinct and yet not distinct. ॥8॥
lanka.111.cau9: All-pervading Lord, these monkeys have all fulfilled their lives, gazing reverently on your face. Shame on our life and our divine bodies, O Hari, for without devotion to you we lie lost in worldly existence. ॥9॥
lanka.111.cau10: Compassionate to the lowly, show mercy now and take away my mind that makes divisions, by which I act perversely and, taking that sorrow for joy, go about content. ॥10॥
lanka.111.cau11: You break the wicked and adorn the lovely earth; your lotus feet are served by Śambhu and Umā. Lord of kings, give me this boon: that I may always have a love for your lotus feet that brings every good. ॥11॥
lanka.111.do111: Brahmā, the four-faced, made his prayer, his body thrilling with love. Gazing on the ocean of beauty, his eyes could not have their fill. ॥111॥
lanka.112.cau1: At that moment Daśaratha came there; seeing his son, his eyes brimmed with tears. The Lord and his younger brother bowed to him, and then the father gave his blessing. ॥1॥
lanka.112.cau2: The Lord said: Father, it is all the power of your merit that I have conquered the invincible king of the demons. Hearing his son's words, his love grew greatly; his eyes filled and the hair on his body stood on end. ॥2॥
lanka.112.cau3: Śrī Rāma, mindful of his father's love of old, looked at him and gave him firm knowledge. Umā, that is why Daśaratha did not attain liberation: he had set his heart on devotion that keeps the Lord and the devotee distinct. ॥3॥
lanka.112.cau4: Those who worship the Lord with form do not take liberation; to them Śrī Rāma gives devotion to himself. Bowing to the Lord again and again, Daśaratha went gladly to the abode of the gods. ॥4॥
lanka.112.do112: The Lord of Kosala stood safe and well with his younger brother and Jānakī. Seeing their beauty, Indra, lord of the gods, rejoiced at heart and began to praise him: ॥112॥
lanka.113.cha1: Glory to you, Rāma, abode of beauty, giver of rest to those who bow before you. You bear a fine quiver, arrows and bow; your arms are mighty and glorious. ॥1॥
lanka.113.cha2: Glory to you, foe of Dūṣaṇa and Khara, crusher of the demon hosts. My Lord, you have slain this wicked one, and all the gods now have a protector. ॥2॥
lanka.113.cha3: Glory to you who lift the earth's burden; your greatness is noble and boundless. Glory to you, merciful foe of Rāvaṇa, who left the demons broken. ॥3॥
lanka.113.cha4: The lord of Laṅkā, swollen with pride in his strength, had brought gods and gandharvas under his sway. Sages, siddhas, men, birds and nāgas: he stubbornly dogged the steps of them all. ॥4॥
lanka.113.cha5: Given to malice towards others and utterly wicked, that great sinner has reaped his fruit. Now listen, you who are kind to the lowly, whose eyes are large as lotuses: ॥5॥
lanka.113.cha6: I was full of pride, thinking there was none my equal. Now that I have seen the Lord's lotus feet, the pride that brought heaps of sorrow is gone. ॥6॥
lanka.113.cha7: Some meditate on Brahman without attributes, whom the Vedas hymn as unmanifest. But the one I love is the king of Kosala, Śrī Rāma in his form with attributes. ॥7॥
lanka.113.cha8: With Sītā and your younger brother, make your home in my heart. Know me as your own servant, abode of Ramā, and give me devotion. ॥8॥
lanka.113.cha9: Give me devotion, abode of Ramā, remover of fear, giver of joy to those who seek refuge. Home of joy, Rāma, Lord of the Raghus, lovely as many Kāmadevas, I bow to you. Delight of the hosts of gods, destroyer of the pairs of opposites, wearing a human body, of matchless strength, Rāma, worshipped by Brahmā, Śaṅkara and the rest, tender with compassion, I bow to you. ॥9॥
lanka.113.do113: Now look on me with grace, merciful Lord, and give me your command: what shall I do? Hearing these pleasing words, the Lord, compassionate to the lowly, spoke: ॥113॥
lanka.114.cau1: Listen, Indra: the monkeys and bears of ours whom the demons killed are lying on the ground. For my sake they gave up their lives; wise lord of the gods, bring them all back to life. ॥1॥
lanka.114.cau2: Listen, Garuḍa: these words of the Lord are very deep, and only sages rich in knowledge understand them. The Lord could slay the three worlds and bring them to life again; here he simply gave the honour to Indra. ॥2॥
lanka.114.cau3: Showering nectar, Indra brought the monkeys and bears back to life, and they all rose up joyfully and came to the Lord. The rain of nectar fell on both armies, yet only the bears and monkeys revived, not the demons. ॥3॥
lanka.114.cau4: The minds of those demons had taken on the form of Śrī Rāma; they were set free, the bonds of worldly existence loosed. The monkeys and bears were all born of portions of the gods, and all of them revived by the will of Śrī Rāma. ॥4॥
lanka.114.cau5: Who is such a friend to the lowly as Śrī Rāma, who set free the demons, every one of them? Rāvaṇa, wicked, a home of impurity and given to lust, attained a state that the greatest sages do not attain. ॥5॥
lanka.114.do114क: Having showered flowers, the gods all mounted their beautiful aerial cars and departed. Seeing that the moment was right, the wise Śiva came to the Lord. ॥114 (क)॥
lanka.114.do114ख: With supreme love, joining both his hands, his lotus eyes filled with tears, his body thrilling and his voice choked, Śiva, the foe of Tripura, prays: ॥114 (ख)॥
lanka.115.cha1: Protect me, O Lord of Raghu's line, who hold the excellent bow and arrows in your beautiful hands. You are the wind that scatters the vast, dense veil of the clouds of delusion, the fire to the forest of doubt, the delight of the gods. ॥1॥
lanka.115.cau2: Without attributes and with attributes, abode of virtues and beautiful, you are the sun of mighty splendour to the darkness of error. Lion to the elephants of desire, anger and pride, dwell for ever in the forest of your devotee's mind. ॥2॥
lanka.115.cau3: To the lotus beds of the throngs of sensual cravings you are a hard frost; you are generous, and beyond the reach of the mind. Mount Mandara to the ocean of worldly existence, drive away my great fear and carry me across the round of births, so hard to cross. ॥3॥
lanka.115.cau4: Dark of body, lotus-eyed, friend of the lowly, deliverer of those who bow to you from their distress, O King Rāma, dwell for ever within my heart, with your younger brother and Sītā. ॥4॥
lanka.115.cau5: Joy of the sages, ornament of the circle of the earth, Tulasīdāsa's Lord who shatters fear. ॥5॥
lanka.115.do115: My Lord, when your coronation takes place in the city of Kosala, I will come, O ocean of mercy, to see your noble deeds. ॥115॥
lanka.116.cau1: When Śiva had made his prayer and departed, Vibhīṣaṇa came close to the Lord. Bowing his head at his feet, he said in gentle words: My Lord, wielder of the Śārṅga bow, hear my plea. ॥1॥
lanka.116.cau2: My Lord, you have slain Rāvaṇa with his family and his army, and spread your holy fame through the three worlds. On me, wretched and unclean, poor in understanding and low in birth, you have shown grace in many ways. ॥2॥
lanka.116.cau3: Now, my Lord, sanctify your servant's house; bathe there, and let the weariness of battle fall away. Look over the treasury, the palaces and the wealth, O compassionate one, and give gladly to the monkeys. ॥3॥
lanka.116.cau4: My Lord, accept me wholly as yours; then, when you go to Ayodhyā, take me along. As he heard these gentle words, both the large eyes of the Lord, kind to the lowly, filled with tears. ॥4॥
lanka.116.do116क: Śrī Rāma said: Listen, brother, this is the truth: your treasury and your house are all mine. But when I remember Bharata's state, each moment passes for me like an aeon. ॥116 (क)॥
lanka.116.do116ख: In the garb of an ascetic, his body worn thin, he repeats my name without ceasing. My friend, I beg you, find a way for me to see him soon. ॥116 (ख)॥
lanka.116.do116ग: If I go when the appointed time has passed, I shall not find my brother alive. As he remembered his younger brother's love, the Lord's body thrilled again and again. ॥116 (ग)॥
lanka.116.do116घ: The Lord went on: Rule for a whole aeon, and keep me in mind within your heart. Then you will reach my abode, where all the saints go. ॥116 (घ)॥
lanka.117.cau1: Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, Vibhīṣaṇa joyfully clasped the feet of the abode of grace. All the monkeys and bears rejoiced, and holding the Lord's feet they told of his spotless virtues. ॥1॥
lanka.117.cau2: Then Vibhīṣaṇa went to his palace and had the aerial car loaded with heaps of gems and with clothes. He brought the Puṣpaka and placed it in front of the Lord; then the ocean of mercy smiled and said: ॥2॥
lanka.117.cau3: Listen, my friend Vibhīṣaṇa: mount the aerial car, go up into the sky and rain down clothes and ornaments. Vibhīṣaṇa went up into the sky that very moment and rained down every gem and garment. ॥3॥
lanka.117.cau4: Each takes whatever pleases his fancy; the monkeys put the gems in their mouths and spit them out again. Śrī Rāma laughed, with Sītā and his younger brother, he who delights in play, the abode of grace. ॥4॥
lanka.117.do117क: He whom sages do not reach even in meditation, of whom the Vedas say neti neti, not this, not this, that same ocean of mercy is sporting in many ways with the monkeys. ॥117 (क)॥
lanka.117.do117ख: Umā, for yoga, japa, charity, austerity, many kinds of sacrifice, vows and rules of observance Śrī Rāma does not show such grace as he does for love, pure and unmixed. ॥117 (ख)॥
lanka.118.cau1: The bears and monkeys received clothes and ornaments, and decked out in them came to Śrī Rāma. Seeing all the monkeys in such variety, the Lord of Kosala laughs again and again. ॥1॥
lanka.118.cau2: Looking at them all, Śrī Rāma showed them kindness and spoke gentle words: By your strength I slew Rāvaṇa, and then crowned Vibhīṣaṇa. ॥2॥
lanka.118.cau3: Now go, all of you, each to your own home; remember me, and fear no one. Hearing these words, the monkeys were overcome with love, and all of them said with joined palms and respect: ॥3॥
lanka.118.cau4: My Lord, whatever you say becomes you; but hearing such words we are bewildered. You counted us monkeys poor and lowly and gave us a master in yourself; you, O Lord of the Raghus, rule the three worlds. ॥4॥
lanka.118.cau5: Hearing the Lord's words, we are dying of shame: do mosquitoes ever do Garuḍa a service? Seeing Śrī Rāma's countenance, the bears and monkeys were lost in love and had no wish to go home. ॥5॥
lanka.118.do118क: At the Lord's prompting, all the monkeys and bears, keeping Śrī Rāma's form in their hearts, set out with joy and sorrow mingled, after making their humble pleas in many ways. ॥118 (क)॥
lanka.118.do118ख: Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, Nīla, Jāmbavān, king of the bears, Aṅgada, Nala and Hanumān, together with Vibhīṣaṇa and the other mighty monkey troop leaders, ॥118 (ख)॥
lanka.118.do118ग: could say nothing, overcome by love, their eyes filling with tears again and again. Facing Śrī Rāma, they gazed at him, holding back even the blink of their eyes. ॥118 (ग)॥
lanka.119.cau1: Seeing their exceeding love, Śrī Rāma took them all up into the aerial car. Bowing his head in his heart at the feet of the brāhmaṇas, he set the car moving northward. ॥1॥
lanka.119.cau2: As the car moves off there is a great clamour, everyone crying: Glory to the hero of the Raghus. There is a throne, very high and lovely; on it the Lord took his seat with Sītā. ॥2॥
lanka.119.cau3: Śrī Rāma with his lady shines as though cloud and lightning rested on a summit of Mount Meru. The beautiful car sped on in great haste; the gods rejoiced and rained down flowers. ॥3॥
lanka.119.cau4: A most pleasant breeze blew, cool, gentle and fragrant; the waters of ocean, lake and river were pure. Fair omens appear all around; hearts are glad, and the sky and the quarters are clear. ॥4॥
lanka.119.cau5: Śrī Rāma said: Look at the battlefield, Sītā. Here Lakṣmaṇa slew Meghanāda, conqueror of Indra. Struck down by Hanumān and Aṅgada, mighty demons lie fallen on the field. ॥5॥
lanka.119.cau6: Kumbhakarṇa and Rāvaṇa, the two brothers who tormented gods and sages, were slain here. ॥6॥
lanka.119.do119क: Here I built the bridge and installed Śiva, the home of bliss. Then the compassionate Lord, with Sītā, bowed to Śiva. ॥119 (क)॥
lanka.119.do119ख: Every place in the forest where the ocean of mercy had stayed and rested he showed to Sītā, and told her the names of them all. ॥119 (ख)॥
lanka.120.cau1: Swiftly the car came to where the lovely Daṇḍaka forest lay. Śrī Rāma went to the dwellings of all the many great sages, Agastya and the rest. ॥1॥
lanka.120.cau2: Having received the blessings of all the seers, the Lord of the world came to Citrakūṭa. There he gladdened the sages, and the car flew swiftly on from there. ॥2॥
lanka.120.cau3: Next Śrī Rāma showed Sītā the lovely Yamunā, which takes away the taint of the Kali age. Then they saw the holy Gaṅgā, and Śrī Rāma said: Sītā, bow to her. ॥3॥
lanka.120.cau4: Now see Prayāga, king of holy places, at the sight of which the sins of ten million births take flight. Then see the most purifying Triveṇī, which takes away grief and is a ladder to the world of Śrī Hari. ॥4॥
lanka.120.cau5: And now see the city of Ayodhyā, most purifying, which destroys the threefold affliction and the disease of worldly existence. ॥5॥
lanka.120.do120क: With Sītā, the compassionate Lord bowed to Ayodhyā. His eyes filled with tears and his body thrilled; again and again Śrī Rāma was overjoyed. ॥120 (क)॥
lanka.120.do120ख: Then the Lord came to the Triveṇī and bathed there joyfully, and together with the monkeys he gave gifts of many kinds to the brāhmaṇas. ॥120 (ख)॥
lanka.121.cau1: The Lord explained to Hanumān: Take the form of a young brahmacārī and go to Ayodhyā. Give Bharata the news that we are well, and come back with news from there. ॥1॥
lanka.121.cau2: Hanumān, son of the Wind, set off at once. Then the Lord went to Bharadvāja. The sage worshipped him with many rites, sang his praises and then gave his blessing. ॥2॥
lanka.121.cau3: Bowing at the sage's feet with both palms joined, the Lord mounted the aerial car and went on again. Here the Niṣāda heard that the Lord had come, and called his people, crying: A boat! Where is a boat? ॥3॥
lanka.121.cau4: Then the aerial car came over the Gaṅgā and, at the Lord's command, came down on the bank. Then Sītā worshipped the Gaṅgā, and after that fell at her feet in many ways. ॥4॥
lanka.121.cau5: Gaṅgā, glad at heart, gave her blessing: Fair lady, may your married happiness never be broken. As soon as he heard, Guha ran, overcome with love, and came near, brimming with the highest joy. ॥5॥
lanka.121.cau6: Seeing the Lord with Vaidehī, he fell to the ground, aware of his body no longer. Seeing his great love, Śrī Rāma joyfully raised him up and pressed him to his heart. ॥6॥
lanka.121.cha1: The Lord of Ramā, treasury of mercy, king among the wise, pressed him to his heart, seated him very close and asked how he was. Then he made his entreaty: Now that I have seen your lotus feet, which Brahmā and Śaṅkara serve, all is well with me. O Rāma, abode of joy, whose every wish is fulfilled, I bow to you; Rāma, I bow to you. ॥1॥
lanka.121.cha2: Śrī Hari pressed the Niṣāda, lowly in every way, to his heart as he would Bharata. Dull-witted Tulasīdāsa, in the grip of delusion, has forgotten such a Lord. This holy story of Śrī Rāma, Rāvaṇa's foe, ever grants love for Śrī Rāma's feet. It takes away desire and the other passions and gives realised knowledge; gods, siddhas and sages sing it with joy. ॥2॥
lanka.121.do121क: To those of understanding who hear the deeds of Śrī Rāma's victory in battle, the Lord gives victory, discernment and prosperity, day after day. ॥121 (क)॥
lanka.121.do121ख: This age of Kali is a home of impurity: reflect in your mind and see. Apart from the name of Śrī Rāma, there is no other support. ॥121 (ख)॥

bal.17.so17: I bow to Hanumān, son of the Wind, a fire to the forest of the wicked, full of wisdom.
In the house of his heart Śrī Rāma dwells, holding his bow and arrows. ॥17॥
aranya.0.shloka1: The root of the tree of dharma, the full moon that gladdens the ocean of discernment,
the sun to the lotus of dispassion, who surely drives off the dense darkness of sin and takes away affliction,
the wind born of the sky in scattering the massed clouds of delusion, Śaṅkara,
sprung from Brahmā's line, remover of stain, dear to King Śrī Rāma: to him I bow. ॥1॥
aranya.0.shloka2: Whose body, full of dense bliss, has the beauty of a rain cloud, clad in yellow and lovely,
with bow and arrow in his hand and a quiver gleaming at his waist, the most excellent,
with long lotus eyes, graced by the matted locks he wears,
walking the road with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa: him, the delightful Rāma, I worship. ॥2॥
aranya.0.sou1: Umā, Śrī Rāma's virtues are deep; learned men and sages gain dispassion from them.
Those who are deluded, turned away from Śrī Hari and without love for dharma, are led by them into delusion.
aranya.1.cau1: I have sung, as far as my understanding allows, the love of the townspeople and of Bharata, matchless and lovely.
Now hear the Lord's most holy deeds, done in the forest, which delight gods, men and sages. ॥1॥
aranya.1.cau2: Once Śrī Rāma gathered lovely flowers and made ornaments with his own hands.
The Lord put them on Sītā with loving care and sat on a beautiful slab of crystal. ॥2॥
aranya.1.cau3: Indra's son, the wretch, disguised himself as a crow and wanted to see how strong Śrī Rāma was,
as though an ant, utterly slow of mind, wanted to reach the bottom of the ocean. ॥3॥
aranya.1.cau4: Pecking Sītā's foot with his beak, the foolish, dull-witted creature fled, a crow only for a purpose.
The blood flowed; Śrī Rāma knew of it and set a reed to his bow as an arrow. ॥4॥
aranya.1.do1: Śrī Rāma is supremely compassionate, ever loving towards the lowly.
With him that fool, a house of faults, came and played a trick. ॥1॥
aranya.2.cau1: Driven by a mantra, the Brahmā arrow sped after him; the crow took fright and fled.
Taking his own form he went to his father, but his father would not keep one turned against Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
aranya.2.cau2: He lost hope, and terror arose in his mind, as it did in the sage Durvāsā for fear of the discus.
Brahmā's realm, Śiva's city, every world he wandered, weary and frantic with fear and grief. ॥2॥
aranya.2.cau3: No one even asked him to sit. Who can shelter one who is hostile to Śrī Rāma?
Listen, Garuḍa: to such a one his mother becomes death, his father becomes like Yama, and nectar turns to poison. ॥3॥
aranya.2.cau4: A friend behaves to him like a hundred enemies, and the river of the gods becomes for him the Vaitaraṇī, the river of hell.
Listen, brother: to one who turns from Śrī Rāma the whole world grows hotter than fire. ॥4॥
aranya.2.cau5: Nārada saw Jayanta in distress, and pity touched him, for the hearts of saints are tender.
He sent him at once to Śrī Rāma, and Jayanta cried out: Friend of those who bow before you, save me. ॥5॥
aranya.2.cau6: Anxious and afraid, he went and clasped his feet: Save me, save me, compassionate Lord of the Raghus.
Your strength is beyond compare, and so is your sovereignty; I, slow of mind, could not grasp it. ॥6॥
aranya.2.cau7: I have reaped the fruit of my own deeds. Now protect me, Lord; I have come looking to you for refuge.
Hearing his most piteous words, Pārvatī, the compassionate Lord left him with one eye and let him go. ॥7॥
aranya.2.so2: Under delusion he had shown enmity, and though it was right that he be slain,
the Lord spared him out of tenderness. Who is as compassionate as Śrī Rāma? ॥2॥
aranya.3.cau1: Living at Citrakūṭa, Śrī Rāma did many deeds that are like nectar to the ear.
Then Śrī Rāma reflected: Everyone knows me now; crowds will gather here. ॥1॥
aranya.3.cau2: With leave taken of every sage, the two brothers went on their way, Sītā with them.
The Lord arrived at Atri's hermitage; hearing of it, the great sage rejoiced. ॥2॥
aranya.3.cau3: Atri, the hair on his body standing on end, rose and ran; when Śrī Rāma saw this he came on in haste.
The brothers were still lying prostrate when the sage pressed them to his heart, and he bathed them both in loving tears. ॥3॥
aranya.3.cau4: Seeing Śrī Rāma's beauty brought coolness to the sage's eyes; then he led them respectfully to his own hermitage.
After worship and gracious words he offered roots and fruit, which pleased the Lord. ॥4॥
aranya.3.so3: The Lord is seated; gazing at his beauty till his eyes are full,
the great sage, supremely wise, joins his palms and sings his praise: ॥3॥
aranya.4.cha1: I salute you, loving to your devotees, compassionate, gentle of nature.
I worship your lotus feet, which give your own abode to those who desire nothing. ॥1॥
aranya.4.cha2: Dark and surpassingly beautiful, you are Mount Mandara to churn the ocean of worldly existence.
Your eyes are like full-blown lotuses; you set us free from pride and the other faults. ॥2॥
aranya.4.cha3: Long of arm and mighty in valour, O Lord, your splendour is beyond measure.
You bear quiver, bow and arrows; you are the lord of the three worlds. ॥3॥
aranya.4.cha4: You are the jewel of the solar race and the breaker of Śiva's bow;
you delight the great sages and the saints and shatter the throngs of the gods' foes. ॥4॥
aranya.4.cha5: Śiva, the foe of Kāmadeva, bows to you; Brahmā and the other gods serve you;
your form is pure awareness, and you take away every fault. ॥5॥
aranya.4.cha6: I salute you, lord of Indirā (Lakṣmī), source of happiness, goal of the good.
I worship you with your Śakti (Sītā) and your younger brother, you who are the dear younger brother (Upendra) of Indra, Śacī's lord. ॥6॥
aranya.4.cha7: Those who, free of envy, worship at the soles of your feet
do not fall into the ocean of worldly existence, crowded with waves of doubt. ॥7॥
aranya.4.cha8: Those who dwell ever in solitude and joyfully worship you for liberation
draw back the senses and the rest, and reach their own true state. ॥8॥
aranya.4.cha9: Him, the one and wondrous Lord, desireless, the Master, all-pervading,
the teacher of the world, eternal, the Fourth (turīya, beyond waking, dream and sleep), the one alone, ॥9॥
aranya.4.cha10: him I worship, who loves true feeling and is very hard to reach for those of false practice;
a wish-fulfilling tree to his own devotees, impartial, easy to serve day after day. ॥10॥
aranya.4.cha11: King of peerless beauty, husband of the earth-born Sītā, I bow to you.
Look kindly on me; I salute you; give me devotion to your lotus feet. ॥11॥
aranya.4.cha12: Those who recite this hymn with reverence
go to your abode, filled with devotion to you; of this there is no doubt. ॥12॥
aranya.4.do4: Having made his prayer, the sage bowed his head, then joined his palms and said:
My Lord, may my mind never leave your lotus feet. ॥4॥
aranya.5.cau1: Clasping Anasūyā's feet, Sītā, gentle and humble, then greeted her.
Joy grew in the heart of the sage's wife; she blessed her and seated her close by. ॥1॥
aranya.5.cau2: She dressed her in heavenly clothes and ornaments that stay ever new, spotless and lovely.
The sage's wife spoke in sweet, tender words and, using Sītā as her pretext, described something of a woman's dharma: ॥2॥
aranya.5.cau3: Mother, father and brother are all your well-wishers, but listen, princess: what any of them gives has limits.
A husband, Vaidehī, is a giver beyond all measure, and a woman who does not serve him is base. ॥3॥
aranya.5.cau4: Patience, dharma, a friend and a wife: these four are tested in times of trouble.
A husband may be old, sickly, dull, poor, blind, deaf, quick to anger or utterly wretched; ॥4॥
aranya.5.cau5: yet a wife who slights even such a husband suffers many torments in Yama's city.
She has one dharma, one vow, one rule: to love her husband's feet in body, word and mind. ॥5॥
aranya.5.cau6: The Vedas, the Purāṇas and all the saints say that a faithful wife is of four kinds in this world.
In the mind of the highest kind it is settled that no other man exists in the world, even in a dream. ॥6॥
aranya.5.cau7: The middling one looks on another man as she would on her own brother, father or son.
She who holds back thinking of dharma and mindful of her family, the Veda calls the lower kind. ॥7॥
aranya.5.cau8: And she who stays faithful only for lack of opportunity or out of fear, count her as the lowest kind of woman in the world.
She who deceives her husband and loves another man falls into the Raurava hell for a hundred kalpas (ages). ॥8॥
aranya.5.cau9: For a moment's pleasure she does not see the sorrow of a hundred crore births: who is as wicked as she?
A woman who gives up deceit and holds to the dharma of a faithful wife reaches the supreme state without toil. ॥9॥
aranya.5.cau10: She who goes against her husband, wherever she is born, is widowed as she reaches youth. ॥10॥
aranya.5.so5क: Though a woman is impure by nature, by serving her husband she attains a blessed state.
The four Vedas sing the fame of Tulasī, who is dear to Śrī Hari even today. ॥5 (क)॥
aranya.5.so5ख: Listen, Sītā: by remembering your name women keep faith with their husbands.
Śrī Rāma is as dear to you as life; I have told this for the good of the world. ॥5 (ख)॥
aranya.6.cau1: Hearing this, Sītā was filled with joy and bowed her head with reverence at Anasūyā's feet.
Then Śrī Rāma, the treasury of mercy, said to the sage: If you permit, I shall now go to another forest. ॥1॥
aranya.6.cau2: Keep showing me your grace always, and knowing me for your servant, never withdraw your love.
At these words of the Lord, the mainstay of dharma, the wise sage answered with love: ॥2॥
aranya.6.cau3: Whose grace Brahmā, Śiva, Sanaka and his brothers and all who speak of the highest truth seek:
you are that very one, Rāma, dear to the desireless, friend of the lowly, who now speak such gentle words. ॥3॥
aranya.6.cau4: Now I see how clever Śrī (Lakṣmī) was, who passed over all the gods and gave herself to you.
How should he whom none can equal or surpass not have such goodness of nature? ॥4॥
aranya.6.cau5: How can I tell you, my master, to go now? Say it yourself, my Lord, for you know every heart.
With these words the steadfast sage gazed at the Lord, tears flowing from his eyes and his body thrilling. ॥5॥
aranya.6.cha1: The sage is thrilled all over and filled to the brim with love; he has fixed his eyes on the lotus of the Lord's face.
He thinks: What japa and austerity did I perform, that I have seen the Lord who is beyond mind, knowledge, the guṇas and the senses?
By japa, yoga and the many works of dharma a person comes to devotion beyond compare.
The servant Tulasīdāsa sings the holy deeds of Śrī Rāma night and day. ॥1॥
aranya.6.do6क: Śrī Rāma's fair fame wipes away the impurity of the Kali age, masters the mind and is the root of happiness.
Those who hear it with reverence have Śrī Rāma ever on their side. ॥6 (क)॥
aranya.6.so6ख: This hard age is a storehouse of impurity; in it there is no dharma, no knowledge, no yoga, no japa.
Those who give up all reliance on anything else and worship Śrī Rāma are wise. ॥6 (ख)॥
aranya.7.cau1: Śrī Rāma, Lord of gods, men and sages, laid his head at the sage's lotus feet and set off into the forest.
Śrī Rāma walks in front and his younger brother behind him, both splendid in the fine garb of hermits. ॥1॥
aranya.7.cau2: Between the two, how does Sītā look? Like māyā (the Lord's power of illusion) between Brahman and the individual soul.
Rivers, forests, mountains and rugged passes know their Lord and open a good way for him. ॥2॥
aranya.7.cau3: Wherever the divine Śrī Rāma goes, clouds spread shade across the sky.
As they went along the way, the demon Virādha met them; the moment he came near, Śrī Rāma struck him down. ॥3॥
aranya.7.cau4: At once he gained a beautiful form; seeing him in sorrow, the Lord sent him to his own abode.
Then, with his handsome younger brother and Sītā, he came to where the sage Śarabhaṅga lived. ॥4॥
aranya.7.do7: The great sage's eyes, like bees, gaze on Śrī Rāma's lotus face
and reverently drink in its nectar; most blessed is Śarabhaṅga's birth. ॥7॥
aranya.8.cau1: The sage said: Listen, compassionate hero of the Raghus, royal swan of the Mānasa lake of Śiva's mind.
I was on my way to Brahmā's realm when I heard that Śrī Rāma would come to the forest. ॥1॥
aranya.8.cau2: Day and night I kept watching the road; now, seeing my Lord, my heart is at peace.
My Lord, I am bare of every spiritual practice; knowing me for a lowly servant, you have shown me grace. ॥2॥
aranya.8.cau3: Yet this is no favour to me, my Lord; you have kept your own vow, you who steal your devotees' hearts.
Until I give up this body and come to you, stay here for the good of this humble one. ॥3॥
aranya.8.cau4: Yoga, sacrifice, japa, austerity and vows, all that he had practised, he offered up to the Lord, and from him took the boon of devotion.
Having thus built a pyre, the sage Śarabhaṅga sat on it, his heart free of every attachment. ॥4॥
aranya.8.do8: Lord, with Sītā and your younger brother, dark of body as a blue rain cloud,
Śrī Rāma in form with attributes, dwell in my heart for ever. ॥8॥
aranya.9.cau1: Saying this, he burnt his body in the fire of yoga and by Śrī Rāma's grace went to Vaikuṇṭha.
He did not merge into Śrī Hari, because he had already taken the boon of devotion that keeps the servant distinct from the Lord. ॥1॥
aranya.9.cau2: Seeing the state the great sage had reached, the assembled seers were especially glad at heart.
The whole company of sages sings his praise: Glory to the Lord who cares for those who bow to him, the root of compassion! ॥2॥
aranya.9.cau3: Then Śrī Rāma went on further into the forest, and many bands of great sages went along with him.
Seeing heaps of bones, Śrī Rāma was moved to great pity and asked the sages about them. ॥3॥
aranya.9.cau4: The sages said: Why do you ask, Lord, when you already know? You see all and dwell within every heart.
Hordes of demons have eaten all these sages. Hearing this, Śrī Rāma's eyes filled with tears. ॥4॥
aranya.9.do9: Raising his arm, Śrī Rāma vowed: I will rid the earth of demons.
and he visited the hermitage of every sage in turn, bringing each of them joy. ॥9॥
aranya.10.cau1: The sage Agastya had a wise disciple named Sutīkṣṇa, who loved the Lord.
In thought, deed and word he served Śrī Rāma's feet, and not even in a dream did he rely on any other god. ॥1॥
aranya.10.cau2: As soon as he heard of the Lord's coming, he ran off in eagerness, building hopes as he went.
O Creator, will Śrī Rāma, friend of the lowly, show mercy to a wretch like me? ॥2॥
aranya.10.cau3: Will Śrī Rāma, my master, with his younger brother, meet me as one of his own servants?
I have no firm confidence in my heart; there is no devotion, dispassion or knowledge in my mind. ॥3॥
aranya.10.cau4: I have had no company of the good, no yoga, japa or sacrifice, no firm love for the lotus feet.
But the treasury of compassion has one way: dear to him is the one who has no other refuge. ॥4॥
aranya.10.cau5: Today my eyes will be fulfilled, seeing the lotus face of him who frees from worldly existence.
The wise sage is wholly immersed in love; his state, Pārvatī, is beyond words. ॥5॥
aranya.10.cau6: He cannot tell the quarters or the points between them, nor the path; who he is and where he is going he does not know.
Now he turns back, then goes on again; now he sings the Lord's virtues and dances. ॥6॥
aranya.10.cau7: The sage has found unbroken, loving devotion; the Lord watches him, hidden behind a tree.
Seeing his boundless love, Śrī Rāma, who removes the fears of worldly existence, appeared in his heart. ॥7॥
aranya.10.cau8: The sage sat motionless in the middle of the path, his body bristling with thrill like a jackfruit.
Then Śrī Rāma came up close; seeing his devotee in that state, he was pleased at heart. ॥8॥
aranya.10.cau9: In many ways Śrī Rāma tried to wake the sage, but he did not stir, enjoying the bliss that meditation brought.
Then Śrī Rāma concealed his royal form, and within the sage's heart showed himself with four arms. ॥9॥
aranya.10.cau10: The sage then started up in distress, like a great serpent that has lost its jewel.
Before him he saw Śrī Rāma, dark of body, the home of joy, with Sītā and his younger brother. ॥10॥
aranya.10.cau11: Like a staff the fortunate sage fell at his feet, lost in love.
With his long arms the Lord lifted him up and held him to his breast with the deepest love. ॥11॥
aranya.10.cau12: As he embraces the sage, the compassionate Lord looks like a tamāla tree embracing a tree of gold.
The sage stands gazing at Śrī Rāma's face, as still as a figure drawn in a picture. ॥12॥
aranya.10.do10: Then the sage steadied his heart and clasped the Lord's feet again and again.
He brought the Lord to his hermitage and worshipped him in many ways. ॥10॥
aranya.11.cau1: The sage said: Lord, hear my prayer. How am I to praise you?
Your greatness is boundless, my understanding small, like a firefly's glow before the sun. ॥1॥
aranya.11.cau2: Dark of body like a garland of blue lotuses, wearing a crown of matted hair and a hermit's bark clothing,
bow and arrows in hand, quiver at the waist: to Śrī Rāma I bow without ceasing. ॥2॥
aranya.11.cau3: A fire to burn the dense forest of delusion, a sun to the lotus groves of the saints,
a lion to the herds of demon elephants, a hawk to the bird of worldly existence: may he ever protect us. ॥3॥
aranya.11.cau4: With eyes like red lotuses and fair attire, a moon to the cakora birds of Sītā's eyes,
a young swan in the Mānasa lake of Śiva's heart: to Rāma, broad of chest and long of arm, I bow. ॥4॥
aranya.11.cau5: A Garuḍa to swallow the serpent of doubt, the soother of grief born of harsh argument,
breaker of worldly existence, delight of the hosts of gods, a mass of grace: may he ever protect us. ॥5॥
aranya.11.cau6: Without attributes and with them, unequal and equal, beyond knowledge, speech and the senses, matchless,
pure, entire, faultless and boundless: to Rāma, remover of the earth's burden, I bow. ॥6॥
aranya.11.cau7: A garden of wish-granting trees for his devotees, who drives off anger, greed, pride and desire,
supremely skilful, a bridge over the ocean of worldly existence: may the banner of the Sun's race ever protect us. ॥7॥
aranya.11.cau8: Abode of matchless strength and might of arm, whose name shatters the vast stain of the Kali age,
armour of dharma, a store of joy-giving virtues: may my Rāma ever bring me blessing. ॥8॥
aranya.11.cau9: Though he is pure, all-pervading and imperishable, ever dwelling in every heart,
yet may Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara, who roams the forest, dwell in my mind with his younger brother and Sītā. ॥9॥
aranya.11.cau10: Let those who know, my Lord, know you as with and without attributes, the inner ruler of the heart;
but may Rāma, the lotus-eyed Lord of Kosala, make my heart his home. ॥10॥
aranya.11.cau11: May this pride never leave me, even by oversight: I am the servant, and Śrī Rāma is my master.
The sage's words delighted Śrī Rāma; joyfully he embraced the great sage once more. ॥11॥
aranya.11.cau12: Śrī Rāma said: Know that I am supremely pleased, sage; whatever boon you ask, I will give you.
The sage said: I have never asked for a boon; I cannot tell what is false and what is true. ॥12॥
aranya.11.cau13: Lord of the Raghus, giver of joy to your servants, give me whatever seems good to you.
Śrī Rāma said: May you have unbroken devotion, dispassion and realised knowledge, and become a treasury of every virtue and of wisdom. ॥13॥
aranya.11.cau14: The sage said: The boon my Lord gave, I have received; now give me what I long for. ॥14॥
aranya.11.do11: Lord Rāma, bearing bow and arrows, with your younger brother and Sītā,
dwell for ever in the sky of my heart like the moon, free of desire. ॥11॥
aranya.12.cau1: Saying so be it, Śrī Rāma, abode of Lakṣmī, joyfully set out for the pot-born sage Agastya.
Sutīkṣṇa said: It has been many days since I had sight of my guru and settled in this hermitage. ॥1॥
aranya.12.cau2: Now I will go with my Lord to my guru; in this, my Lord, I put you under no obligation.
Seeing the sage's cleverness, the treasury of mercy took him along, and both brothers laughed. ॥2॥
aranya.12.cau3: Speaking along the way of devotion to himself, beyond compare, Śrī Rāma, king of the gods, reached the sage's hermitage.
Sutīkṣṇa went at once to his guru, prostrated himself, and spoke thus: ॥3॥
aranya.12.cau4: My lord, the son of the king of Kosala, the support of the world, has come to meet you:
It is Śrī Rāma, the very one whose name you chant day and night, my master, and with him are his younger brother and Sītā. ॥4॥
aranya.12.cau5: Hearing this, Agastya sprang up and hurried out; tears welled in his eyes as he beheld Śrī Hari.
Both brothers threw themselves at the sage's lotus feet, and the seer, full of love, held them to his heart. ॥5॥
aranya.12.cau6: The wise sage asked after their welfare with respect, then brought them and seated them on fine seats.
Then, after worshipping the Lord in many ways, he said: There is no one as fortunate as I. ॥6॥
aranya.12.cau7: All the other companies of sages who were there rejoiced to see him, the root of joy. ॥7॥
aranya.12.do12: In the midst of the gathered sages the Lord sits facing every one of them.
They gaze at him as a flock of cakora birds gazes at the autumn moon. ॥12॥
aranya.13.cau1: Then Śrī Rāma said to the sage: My lord, nothing is hidden from you.
You know the reason for which I have come; that is why, revered sir, I have not spelt it out. ॥1॥
aranya.13.cau2: Now, my lord, give me the counsel by which I may slay the enemies of the sages.
Hearing the Lord's words the sage smiled and said: My Lord, what did you take me to be, that you asked me this? ॥2॥
aranya.13.cau3: O destroyer of sin, it is only by the power of worshipping you that I know a little of your glory.
Your māyā is a vast cluster-fig tree, and its fruits are the many hosts of universes. ॥3॥
aranya.13.cau4: Living beings, moving and unmoving, dwell within those fruits like tiny creatures and know of nothing else.
The eater of those fruits is harsh and dreadful Time, and even that Time is ever afraid of you. ॥4॥
aranya.13.cau5: And you, the master of all the guardians of the worlds, have questioned me as a man would.
This boon I ask, O abode of grace: dwell in my heart with Sītā and your younger brother. ॥5॥
aranya.13.cau6: Grant me unceasing devotion, dispassion, the company of the good, and unbroken love for your lotus feet.
Although you are Brahman, indivisible and endless, known only through experience and worshipped by the saints, ॥6॥
aranya.13.cau7: and though I know that form of yours and describe it, again and again it is Brahman with attributes that I love.
You always give honour to your servants; that is why, O Lord of the Raghus, you have asked me. ॥7॥
aranya.13.cau8: My Lord, there is a most charming place; its name is holy Pañcavaṭī.
Make the Daṇḍaka forest pure, my Lord, and lift the great sage's fierce curse. ॥8॥
aranya.13.cau9: Live there, O king of Raghu's race, and be kind to all the sages.
With the sage's leave Śrī Rāma went on his way and was soon near Pañcavaṭī. ॥9॥
aranya.13.do13: There he met Jaṭāyu, king of the vultures, and their love grew in many ways.
Near the Godāvarī the Lord thatched a hut of leaves and made his home there. ॥13॥
aranya.14.cau1: Ever since Śrī Rāma made his home there, the sages were happy and their fear was gone.
Hills, forests, rivers and lakes were filled with beauty, and grew lovelier with every passing day. ॥1॥
aranya.14.cau2: Flocks of birds and herds of deer lived in joy, and the bees, humming sweetly, made a lovely sight.
That forest, where Śrī Rāma dwelt in visible form, not even Śeṣa, king of serpents, could describe. ॥2॥
aranya.14.cau3: One day the Lord sat at ease, and Lakṣmaṇa spoke to him in words free of all deceit:
Master of gods, men and sages and of all that moves and does not move, I ask you as I would ask my own lord. ॥3॥
aranya.14.cau4: Explain to me, my Lord, that by which I may leave everything and serve the dust of your feet.
Tell me of knowledge, dispassion and māyā, and tell me of the devotion for whose sake you show mercy. ॥4॥
aranya.14.do14: My Lord, explain to me as well the whole difference between God and the individual soul.
Through that, may love for your feet arise, and grief, delusion and error depart. ॥14॥
aranya.15.cau1: Śrī Rāma said: I will explain it all in a few words, dear brother; listen with your understanding, mind and heart intent.
The sense of I and mine, of you and yours, is māyā, which holds all the hosts of beings in its sway. ॥1॥
aranya.15.cau2: The senses, their objects, and all that the mind can reach, brother: know all of it to be māyā.
Hear also its divisions; there are two, the one knowledge (vidyā), the other ignorance (avidyā). ॥2॥
aranya.15.cau3: One, ignorance, is wicked and full of sorrow beyond measure; in its power the soul has fallen into the well of worldly existence.
The other, knowledge, which holds the guṇas (the qualities of nature) under its sway, creates the world; it acts as the Lord impels it, with no strength of its own. ॥3॥
aranya.15.cau4: Knowledge is that in which not a trace of pride remains, and which sees Brahman equally in all.
Dear brother, that one should be called supremely dispassionate who has cast off the siddhis (powers) and the three guṇas as if they were straw. ॥4॥
aranya.15.do15: One who does not know māyā, God or his own self should be called the soul (jīva).
He who grants bondage and liberation, who is beyond all and sets māyā in motion, is the Lord, the auspicious one. ॥15॥
aranya.16.cau1: From dharma comes dispassion, from yoga knowledge, and knowledge grants liberation: so the Vedas declare.
But that by which I quickly melt, brother, is devotion to me, which gives joy to my devotees. ॥1॥
aranya.16.cau2: It is free and needs nothing else to lean on; knowledge and realised knowledge are under its control.
Dear brother, devotion has no equal and is the source of all happiness; it comes to one when the saints are pleased. ॥2॥
aranya.16.cau3: Now I shall set out in full what leads to devotion: it is an easy road, and by it living beings attain me.
First comes deep love for the feet of the brāhmaṇas, and each being devoted to his own duties in the way the Vedas teach. ॥3॥
aranya.16.cau4: Its fruit, in turn, is dispassion towards the objects of sense; then love springs up for my dharma.
The nine forms of devotion, hearing and the rest, grow firm, and the mind holds deep love for my divine play (līlā). ॥4॥
aranya.16.cau5: There should be deep love for the saints' lotus feet, and a firm rule of worship in mind, deed and word.
One should know me as guru, father, mother, brother, lord and god, all in one, and be steadfast in service. ॥5॥
aranya.16.cau6: As he sings my virtues, his body thrills, his voice is choked and tears flow from his eyes.
Dear brother, one in whom there is no desire and the like, no pride and no hypocrisy: I am ever under his sway. ॥6॥
aranya.16.do16: Those whose refuge I am in word, deed and mind, and who worship without desire,
in the lotus of their hearts I ever take my rest. ॥16॥
aranya.17.cau1: Hearing of the path of devotion, Lakṣmaṇa felt great joy and bowed his head at the Lord's feet.
In this way some days went by in talk of dispassion, knowledge, virtues and right conduct. ॥1॥
aranya.17.cau2: Śūrpaṇakhā, Rāvaṇa's sister, was wicked of heart and as cruel as a female serpent.
Once she went to Pañcavaṭī, and at the sight of the two princes she was overcome. ॥2॥
aranya.17.cau3: Garuḍa, a woman who sees a charming man, be he brother, father or son, is stirred.
She cannot hold back her mind, as the sunstone melts at the sight of the sun. ॥3॥
aranya.17.cau4: Taking on a lovely form, she went to the Lord and, smiling broadly, said:
No man is your equal, and no woman mine; the Creator has made this match after careful thought. ॥4॥
aranya.17.cau5: I have searched the three worlds and found no man anywhere to match me.
That is why I have stayed unmarried until now; seeing you, my heart is somewhat content. ॥5॥
aranya.17.cau6: Glancing at Sītā, the Lord said: My younger brother is unmarried.
She went to Lakṣmaṇa; knowing her to be the enemy's sister, he looked at the Lord and spoke gently: ॥6॥
aranya.17.cau7: Listen, fair one: I am his servant. I am not my own master; there would be no comfort for you with me.
My Lord is able to do anything; he is the king of Kosalapura, and whatever he does becomes him. ॥7॥
aranya.17.cau8: A servant who wants comfort, a beggar honour, one given to vice wealth, a profligate a blessed end,
a greedy man fame, a proud man the four ends of life: these creatures look for milk by milking the sky. ॥8॥
aranya.17.cau9: She turned back and came once more to Śrī Rāma; the Lord sent her again to Lakṣmaṇa.
Lakṣmaṇa said: He will wed you who has cut every tie with shame and cast it off. ॥9॥
aranya.17.cau10: Then, stung and angry, she went to Śrī Rāma and revealed her terrible form.
When he saw Sītā frightened, Śrī Rāma signalled to his brother and told him what to do. ॥10॥
aranya.17.do17: With great swiftness Lakṣmaṇa left her without nose and ears.
It was as though he had sent Rāvaṇa a challenge by her hand. ॥17॥
aranya.18.cau1: Robbed of nose and ears she was hideous to see, as if a mountain were pouring out streams of red ochre.
Weeping, she went to Khara and Dūṣaṇa and cried: Shame, shame on your manhood and your strength, brother! ॥1॥
aranya.18.cau2: When he asked, she told him everything plainly; hearing it, the demons made ready an army.
Hosts upon hosts of demons rushed out, like flocks of winged mountains of lampblack. ॥2॥
aranya.18.cau3: On mounts of many kinds, in many shapes, terrible and past counting, they carried weapons of every sort.
They put Śūrpaṇakhā at their head, ill-omened to look at, without ears or nose. ॥3॥
aranya.18.cau4: Countless fearful ill omens appeared, but all of them, in the grip of death, paid them no heed.
They roared, they threatened, they leapt into the sky; the warriors rejoiced greatly at the sight of the army. ॥4॥
aranya.18.cau5: Someone shouted: Take both brothers alive! Seize them, put them to death, and snatch the woman away.
The whole sky was filled with dust. Śrī Rāma called his younger brother and said: ॥5॥
aranya.18.cau6: Take Sītā and go to a mountain cave; a fearsome army of demons has come.
Stay on your guard. Hearing the Lord's words, Lakṣmaṇa went with Sītā, bow and arrows in hand. ॥6॥
aranya.18.cau7: Seeing the enemy host advancing, Śrī Rāma smiled and strung his mighty bow. ॥7॥
aranya.18.cha1: Having strung the mighty bow, as he binds his matted locks into a knot upon his head, how splendid he looks:
like a pair of serpents fighting with countless lightnings on a mountain of emerald.
Girding the quiver at his waist, taking the bow in his long arms and setting the arrows right,
the Lord gazes as a lion gazes when it sees a herd of mighty elephants. ॥1॥
aranya.18.so18: The warriors came charging in close array, crying out to seize him, seize him.
They closed round him as demons close round the young sun when they see it alone. ॥18॥
aranya.19.cau1: Seeing the Lord, they could not loose their arrows; the demon host stood spellbound.
Khara and Dūṣaṇa called their minister and said: This is some prince, a jewel among men. ॥1॥
aranya.19.cau2: Of nāgas, asuras, gods, men and sages, how many have we seen, conquered and slain!
Listen, brothers all: in our whole lives we have never seen such beauty. ॥2॥
aranya.19.cau3: Though he has disfigured our sister, so peerless a man does not deserve to be slain.
Hand over at once the woman you have hidden, and go home alive, the two of you. ॥3॥
aranya.19.cau4: Tell him what I have said, and when you have heard his reply, come back quickly.
The messengers went and told Śrī Rāma; on hearing it, Śrī Rāma smiled and said: ॥4॥
aranya.19.cau5: We are kṣatriyas who hunt in the forest, and it is beasts like you, wicked ones, that we roam in search of.
We do not fear a mighty foe when we see one; we would fight even Death, for once. ॥5॥
aranya.19.cau6: Men though we are, we destroy the race of demons; boys though we are, we guard the sages and torment the wicked.
If you lack the strength, turn back home; I strike down no one who turns away from battle. ॥6॥
aranya.19.cau7: Once in battle, to use guile and cunning, or to show mercy to an enemy, is the worst cowardice.
The messengers went and quickly told it all, and hearing it, Khara and Dūṣaṇa burned with rage at heart. ॥7॥
aranya.19.cha1: Their hearts ablaze, they cried: Seize him. The fearsome demon warriors charged.
They bore arrows, bows, javelins, spears, tridents, swords, iron clubs and axes.
First the Lord twanged his bow, with a harsh, terrible and fearful sound.
The demons were deafened and dismayed; at that moment they had no sense left. ॥1॥
aranya.19.do19क: Knowing the foe to be strong, they rushed on, now on their guard.
They began to rain missiles and weapons of many kinds upon Śrī Rāma. ॥19 (क)॥
aranya.19.do19ख: Śrī Rāma cut their weapons into pieces as small as sesame seeds.
Then, drawing his bow to his ear, he loosed his own arrows. ॥19 (ख)॥
aranya.20.cha1: Then the terrible arrows flew, like a host of hissing serpents.
Śrī Rāma grew wrathful in the battle, and his arrows, keen beyond measure, sped on. ॥1॥
aranya.20.cau2: Seeing those razor-sharp arrows, the demon warriors turned and fled.
The three brothers grew angry and said: Whoever runs away from the battle, ॥2॥
aranya.20.cau3: him we shall slay with our own hands. At this they turned back, resolved in their hearts to die.
Now they stood face to face and struck with weapons of many kinds. ॥3॥
aranya.20.cau4: Knowing the foe to be in a towering rage, the Lord set an arrow to his bow.
He loosed a great many iron shafts, and the dreadful fiends began to be cut down. ॥4॥
aranya.20.cau5: Chests, heads, arms, hands and feet began to fall on the ground on every side.
As the arrows struck, the demons shrieked, and their trunks came down like mountains. ॥5॥
aranya.20.cau6: Warriors are cut down, their bodies in a hundred pieces, and still they rise again through their tricks.
Arms and heads in great numbers fly through the air, and headless trunks run about. ॥6॥
aranya.20.cau7: Birds, the kaṅka and the crow, and jackals gnash their teeth, harsh and dreadful. ॥7॥
aranya.20.cha1_2: Jackals gnash their teeth; ghosts, spirits and fiends go about filling their skull-bowls.
Heroic vetālas beat time on skulls, and the yoginīs dance.
Śrī Rāma's fierce arrows sever the warriors' chests, arms and heads.
Their trunks drop here and there, then rise and fight on, raising a fearful cry: Seize him, seize him. ॥1॥
aranya.20.cha2: Vultures fly off clutching entrails, and fiends run holding the other end in their hands,
as though many children who dwell in the city of battle were flying kites.
Warriors in great numbers lie slain or dashed down, their chests torn open, groaning.
Seeing their army in distress, Triśirā and the other champions, with Khara and Dūṣaṇa, turned to fight. ॥2॥
aranya.20.cha3: Arrows, spears, javelins, axes, tridents and swords, all at a single moment,
countless demons hurl in their fury at Śrī Rāma.
Within a moment the Lord had stopped the foe's arrows; then he called out his challenge and shot his own.
Into the chest of every demon chief he drove ten arrows apiece. ॥3॥
aranya.20.cha4: No sooner do the warriors fall to earth than they rise and close again; they do not die, and they weave thick illusions.
The gods are afraid to see fourteen thousand fiends against the Lord of Avadh alone.
Seeing the gods and sages in fear, the Lord, master of māyā, worked a great marvel.
The foes began to see one another as Rāma, and the enemy host fought among itself and perished. ॥4॥
aranya.20.do20क: Crying Rāma, Rāma, they leave their bodies and reach the state of liberation.
By this device Śrī Rāma, the treasury of mercy, slew the enemy in an instant. ॥20 (क)॥
aranya.20.do20ख: The gods in their joy rain down flowers, and drums sound in the sky.
Singing his praises again and again, they all departed, resplendent in their many kinds of aerial cars. ॥20 (ख)॥
aranya.21.cau1: When Śrī Rāma had overcome the enemy in battle, the fear of gods, men and sages alike was at an end.
Then Lakṣmaṇa returned with Sītā; he fell at the Lord's feet, and in his joy the Lord drew him to his breast. ॥1॥
aranya.21.cau2: Sītā gazes on his dark and tender form, and in her deep love her eyes can never have enough.
Dwelling at Pañcavaṭī, Śrī Rāma does deeds that bring joy to gods and sages. ॥2॥
aranya.21.cau3: Seeing Khara and Dūṣaṇa brought to ruin, Śūrpaṇakhā went and stirred up Rāvaṇa.
In a towering rage she said: You have put your realm and your treasury clean out of mind. ॥3॥
aranya.21.cau4: You drink and you sleep, day and night, and do not know that the enemy stands over your head.
Kingship without right policy, wealth without dharma, good deeds not offered up to Śrī Hari, ॥4॥
aranya.21.cau5: and learning that gives birth to no discernment: to study, to do or to gain these brings nothing but toil for its fruit.
By attachment the ascetic, by ill counsel the king, by pride knowledge, by drink modesty, ॥5॥
aranya.21.cau6: love that lacks humility, and by vanity the man of gifts, are swiftly brought to nothing; this is the teaching of policy I have heard. ॥6॥
aranya.21.so21क: An enemy, a disease, fire, sin, a master and a snake should never be reckoned small.
Saying this, she broke into lament of every kind and began to weep. ॥21 (क)॥
aranya.21.do21ख: She fell distraught in the midst of the court and, weeping, cried out in many ways:
O ten-headed one, while you live, should such a fate befall me? ॥21 (ख)॥
aranya.22.cau1: At her words the courtiers started up in alarm; they soothed her, took her arm and helped her to her feet.
Rāvaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: Tell me your own story. Who cut off your nose and ears? ॥1॥
aranya.22.cau2: Śūrpaṇakhā said: The sons of Daśaratha, king of Avadh, lions among men, have come to the forest to hunt.
Their deeds have shown me that they will leave the earth without a single demon. ॥2॥
aranya.22.cau3: Ten-headed one, they are the ones whose strength of arm has made the sages fearless, so that they roam the forests freely.
To look at they are boys, but they are like Death itself: most steadfast, archers both, with many gifts. ॥3॥
aranya.22.cau4: Matchless in might and splendour are the two brothers, intent on killing the wicked and a joy to gods and sages.
The one who is a home of beauty is called Rāma, and with them is a young woman. ॥4॥
aranya.22.cau5: The Creator has fashioned that woman a treasure of beauty; a thousand million Ratis would be offered up for her.
His younger brother cut off my ears and nose; told that I am your sister, they mock me. ॥5॥
aranya.22.cau6: Hearing this, Khara and Dūṣaṇa answered my cry, but in a moment the two brothers slew the whole army.
When he heard of the slaying of Khara, Dūṣaṇa and Triśirā, Rāvaṇa burned in every limb. ॥6॥
aranya.22.do22: He calmed Śūrpaṇakhā and spoke of his own might in many ways.
Then he went to his palace, deep in worry, and that night sleep would not come. ॥22॥
aranya.23.cau1: Rāvaṇa thought: Among gods, men, asuras, nāgas and birds there is no one who can match even my followers.
Khara and Dūṣaṇa were as strong as I am; who but the Lord could have slain them? ॥1॥
aranya.23.cau2: If the Lord, who gladdens the gods and lifts the burden of the earth, has come down to earth in a body,
then I shall go and make him my enemy by force, and dying by the Lord's arrow, cross the ocean of worldly existence. ॥2॥
aranya.23.cau3: Worship will never come from this body of darkness; so in mind, deed and word this is my fixed resolve.
But if they are only princes of men, I shall seize the woman after I have beaten the two of them in battle. ॥3॥
aranya.23.cau4: Alone in his chariot he went off to the shore of the sea, where Mārīca had his dwelling.
Meanwhile, Umā, listen to the charming tale of how Śrī Rāma laid his plan here. ॥4॥
aranya.23.do23: When Lakṣmaṇa had gone into the forest to gather roots, fruit and tubers,
Śrī Rāma, all grace and joy, smiled and said to the daughter of Janaka: ॥23॥
aranya.24.cau1: Listen, my beloved, so fair in your vows and gentle in your ways: I am about to play a charming human part.
Until I have made an end of the demons, you must dwell within the fire. ॥1॥
aranya.24.cau2: The moment Śrī Rāma finished explaining it all, Sītā, holding the Lord's feet in her heart, vanished into the fire.
In her place Sītā left her own reflection, the same in nature and in form, and as modest as herself. ॥2॥
aranya.24.cau3: What the Lord had set in motion was a mystery hidden even from Lakṣmaṇa.
Rāvaṇa, base and bent on his own ends, went to where Mārīca was and bowed his head to him. ॥3॥
aranya.24.cau4: When the base bow low, great harm follows, as when a goad, a bow, a snake or a cat bends.
Pārvatī, the sweet words of the wicked are a thing to fear, like flowers that bloom out of season. ॥4॥
aranya.24.do24: Then Mārīca paid him honour and asked him respectfully:
Dear one, what troubles your mind so much that you have come alone? ॥24॥
aranya.25.cau1: The ill-fated Rāvaṇa told him the whole story with great pride, and said:
Take the shape of a false deer, full of guile, so that by this means I may carry off the king's wife. ॥1॥
aranya.25.cau2: Then Mārīca said: Listen, ten-headed one: he is the lord of all that moves and all that is still, in the form of a man.
Do not make him your enemy, dear one. If he slays, we die; if he grants life, we live. ॥2॥
aranya.25.cau3: When the prince went to protect the sage's sacrifice, Śrī Rāma struck me with an arrow that had no head,
and in a moment I was flung a hundred yojanas away. No good can come of making enemies of them. ॥3॥
aranya.25.cau4: I have become like the grub seized by the bhṛṅga wasp: wherever I look, I see the two brothers.
Say they are only men, dear one, still they are heroes of great valour; in opposing them you will not come through. ॥4॥
aranya.25.do25: He who killed Tāṛakā and Subāhu and broke Śiva's bow,
who slew Khara, Dūṣaṇa and Triśirā: can a mere man be so mighty? ॥25॥
aranya.26.cau1: Go back home, with the good of your family in mind. At these words Rāvaṇa burned with rage and poured out insults.
He said: Fool, do you set yourself up as my guru to instruct me? Name the warrior in all the world who is my equal. ॥1॥
aranya.26.cau2: Then Mārīca reasoned in his heart: To set oneself against these nine brings no good:
an armed man, one who knows one's secrets, a powerful master, a fool, a rich man, a physician, a bard, a poet and a skilled cook. ॥2॥
aranya.26.cau3: Seeing his death on either side, he looked to Śrī Rāma for refuge.
He thought: One word of answer and this ill-starred fellow will slay me, so let me rather fall to an arrow of Śrī Rāma. ॥3॥
aranya.26.cau4: With this settled in his heart he went along with Rāvaṇa; his love for Śrī Rāma's feet was never broken.
Great was the joy in his mind, that today he would see his dearest one, but he let Rāvaṇa see none of it. ॥4॥
aranya.26.cha1: I shall see my own most beloved Lord, and my eyes will have their reward, and I shall know joy.
On the feet of that abode of grace, with Sītā and his younger brother beside him, I shall fix my mind.
His very anger grants liberation, and devotion to him wins over even him who is subject to none;
that same Śrī Hari, ocean of bliss, will set an arrow to the string himself and strike me dead. ॥1॥
aranya.26.do26: Bow and arrows in hand, the Lord will run after me over the ground,
and I shall turn back again and again to look at him. No one is as blessed as I. ॥26॥
aranya.27.cau1: Rāvaṇa came near to that forest, and Mārīca then became the false deer.
So wondrous was it that it is past all describing; its body was made of gold, set with jewels. ॥1॥
aranya.27.cau2: Sītā saw the deer, lovely beyond compare, enchanting in every limb.
She said: Listen, my Lord, compassionate hero of the Raghus: the hide of this deer is very beautiful. ॥2॥
aranya.27.cau3: My Lord, ever true to your word, kill it and bring me its skin, says Sītā.
Śrī Rāma knew the whole cause of it; gladly he rose to bring the gods' purpose about. ॥3॥
aranya.27.cau4: Looking at the deer, he girded his waist, took his bow in hand and set a fine arrow to it.
The Lord gave Lakṣmaṇa careful instructions: Brother, many demons roam this forest. ॥4॥
aranya.27.cau5: Guard Sītā, taking thought of your wits, your discernment, your strength and the moment.
Seeing the Lord, the deer took flight, and Śrī Rāma ran after it with his bow made ready. ॥5॥
aranya.27.cau6: He of whom the Vedas say neti, not this, and whom Śiva cannot reach in meditation, is running after a deer of illusion.
Now it comes close, then flees far off; now it shows itself, now it hides. ॥6॥
aranya.27.cau7: Appearing and vanishing and playing many tricks, it drew the Lord far away in this manner.
Then Śrī Rāma took aim and loosed a deadly arrow, and it fell to the ground with a terrible cry. ॥7॥
aranya.27.cau8: First he called out Lakṣmaṇa's name, and afterwards in his heart he remembered Śrī Rāma.
As he gave up his life he showed his own true body, and remembered Śrī Rāma with love. ॥8॥
aranya.27.cau9: The all-wise Lord knew the love in his heart and bestowed on him a goal rare even for sages. ॥9॥
aranya.27.do27: The gods shower flowers in abundance and sing the story of the Lord's virtues.
Śrī Rāma, friend of the lowly, has given his own abode to a demon. ॥27॥
aranya.28.cau1: Having slain the wicked one, Śrī Rāma turned back at once, his bow shining in his hand, his quiver at his waist.
When that cry of distress reached Sītā, she spoke to Lakṣmaṇa in the utmost fear: ॥1॥
aranya.28.cau2: Go quickly; your brother is in grave danger. Lakṣmaṇa smiled and said: Listen, Mother.
He at the play of whose eyebrows creation dissolves — could he fall into danger even in a dream? ॥2॥
aranya.28.cau3: When Sītā spoke words that cut to the heart, Lakṣmaṇa's mind wavered, moved by Śrī Hari.
Entrusting her to all the gods of the forest and of the quarters, he went to where Śrī Rāma was, the Rāhu to the moon that is Rāvaṇa. ॥3॥
aranya.28.cau4: Finding her alone, Rāvaṇa came near in the guise of an ascetic.
He whose terror makes gods and demons afraid, so that they do not sleep at night or eat by day — ॥4॥
aranya.28.cau5: that same Rāvaṇa went on stealthily like a thief, glancing this way and that like a dog.
So it is, Garuḍa: when one sets foot on the wrong path, not a trace remains of bodily splendour, intellect or strength. ॥5॥
aranya.28.cau6: Telling pleasing tales of many kinds, he put before her statecraft, fear and love.
Sītā said: Listen, reverend ascetic: your words are those of a wicked man. ॥6॥
aranya.28.cau7: Then Rāvaṇa showed his own form, and when he told his name, Sītā was afraid.
Summoning all her courage, Sītā said: Stand there, wicked one; my Lord has come. ॥7॥
aranya.28.cau8: You have come under the sway of death, lord of the demons, like a petty hare that wants a lioness.
Hearing these words Rāvaṇa grew angry, yet in his mind he bowed to her feet and was glad. ॥8॥
aranya.28.do28: Then, full of rage, Rāvaṇa seated her in his chariot.
He set off along the path of the sky in haste, but he was so afraid that he could not drive the chariot. ॥28॥
aranya.29.cau1: Sītā cried out: Ah, Lord of the Raghus, the one hero of the world, for what fault have you forgotten your mercy?
You who take away distress and give happiness to those who seek refuge — ah, sun to the lotus of Raghu's line! ॥1॥
aranya.29.cau2: Ah, Lakṣmaṇa, the fault is not yours; I gave way to anger and have reaped its fruit.
Sītā lamented in many ways: the Lord, so full of grace and so loving, is far away. ॥2॥
aranya.29.cau3: Who will carry word of my plight to the Lord? A donkey wants to eat the sacrificial offering.
Hearing Sītā's bitter lament, all creatures, moving and unmoving, were filled with sorrow. ॥3॥
aranya.29.cau4: Hearing the cry of distress, Jaṭāyu, king of the vultures, knew her for the wife of Śrī Rāma, the ornament of Raghu's line.
The vile demon was carrying her off like a sacred tawny cow in the power of a barbarian. ॥4॥
aranya.29.cau5: Jaṭāyu said: Sītā, my daughter, have no fear; I will destroy this demon.
The bird flew at him in fury, like a thunderbolt loosed upon a mountain. ॥5॥
aranya.29.cau6: He cried: You there, wicked one, why do you not stand? You go on without fear; do you not know me?
Seeing him come on like Death itself, Rāvaṇa turned and reflected: ॥6॥
aranya.29.cau7: Is it Maināka, or Garuḍa, king of the birds? But he and his master both know my strength.
Then he knew him: This is old Jaṭāyu; he will leave his body at the holy place of my hands. ॥7॥
aranya.29.cau8: Hearing this, the vulture rushed at him, wild with rage, and said: Listen to my counsel, Rāvaṇa.
Let Sītā go and return home safe; otherwise, many-armed one, this is what will happen: ॥8॥
aranya.29.cau9: In the terrible fire of Śrī Rāma's anger your whole race will be as moths.
The warrior Rāvaṇa gave no answer; at once the vulture flew at him in anger. ॥9॥
aranya.29.cau10: Seizing him by the hair, he dragged Rāvaṇa from his chariot to the ground; setting Sītā aside, the vulture turned on him again.
Striking with his beak, he tore Rāvaṇa's body, and Rāvaṇa lay senseless for a daṇḍa (about twenty-four minutes). ॥10॥
aranya.29.cau11: Then, stung and furious, the demon drew a sword most terrible.
He cut off the bird's wings, and Jaṭāyu fell to the earth, remembering Śrī Rāma, having done a wondrous deed. ॥11॥
aranya.29.cau12: Seating Sītā in the chariot again, he hurried off, in no little fear.
Sītā went through the sky lamenting, like a frightened doe helpless in a hunter's grip. ॥12॥
aranya.29.cau13: Seeing monkeys sitting on a hill, she called the name of Śrī Hari and let a cloth fall.
In this way he carried Sītā off and kept her in the Aśoka grove. ॥13॥
aranya.29.do29क: The wicked one showed her fear and love in many ways and was beaten;
then he kept her beneath an Aśoka tree, having arrangements made for her keeping. ॥29 (क)॥
aranya.29.do29ख: The way Śrī Rāma ran off after the false deer —
that image Sītā keeps in her heart, ever repeating the name of Śrī Hari. ॥29 (ख)॥
aranya.30.cau1: Seeing his younger brother coming, Śrī Rāma showed great anxiety outwardly.
He said: Dear brother, setting my word aside, you have come away and left Janaka's daughter on her own? ॥1॥
aranya.30.cau2: Bands of demons roam the forest; my heart tells me Sītā is not at the hermitage.
His younger brother clasped his lotus feet and with joined hands said: My Lord, the fault is not at all mine. ॥2॥
aranya.30.cau3: With his younger brother the Lord went where the hermitage was, by the Godāvarī.
Finding the hermitage without Sītā, he was as distraught as any ordinary, helpless man. ॥3॥
aranya.30.cau4: Śrī Rāma lamented: Ah, Jānakī, mine of virtues! Ah, Sītā, pure in beauty, character, vows and observances!
Lakṣmaṇa reasoned with him in many ways, and he went on, asking the rows of creepers and trees: ॥4॥
aranya.30.cau5: O birds, O deer, O lines of bees, have you seen Sītā, the doe-eyed?
Wagtail and parrot, dove, deer and fish, the hosts of bees, the skilled cuckoo, ॥5॥
aranya.30.cau6: jasmine buds and pomegranate, lightning, lotus, autumn moon and she-serpent,
Varuṇa's noose, Kāmadeva's bow, swan, elephant and lion are all hearing their own praise. ॥6॥
aranya.30.cau7: The bael fruit, gold and the plantain rejoice, without the least fear or shyness in their minds.
Listen, Jānakī: with you gone, they are all rejoicing today as if each had come into a kingdom. ॥7॥
aranya.30.cau8: How can you bear this rivalry? My beloved, why do you not appear at once?
