So the Lord searched and lamented, as though he were a lover in deep separation, consumed by longing. ॥8॥
aranya.30.cau9: Śrī Rāma, whose every desire is fulfilled, the mass of joy, unborn and imperishable, was acting out a human part.
Ahead he saw the king of the vultures lying there, remembering Śrī Rāma's feet with their marks. ॥9॥
aranya.30.do30: Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, touched his head with his lotus hand.
Gazing on the face of Śrī Rāma, the home of beauty, he was freed of all his pain. ॥30॥
aranya.31.cau1: Then, steadying himself, the vulture said: Listen, O Rāma, who shatters the fear of worldly existence.
My Lord, it was Rāvaṇa who brought me to this state; that wicked one has carried off Janaka's daughter. ॥1॥
aranya.31.cau2: My master, he has gone south with her, and she was crying out bitterly like an osprey.
I held on to life, Lord, only to see you; now, treasury of mercy, it is about to depart. ॥2॥
aranya.31.cau3: Śrī Rāma said: Keep your body, dear father. Smiling, the vulture answered:
He whose name, if it comes to a dying man's lips, frees even the vilest, so the Vedas sing, ॥3॥
aranya.31.cau4: is here before me, visible to my eyes; for want of what, Lord, should I keep this body?
With eyes full of tears Śrī Rāma said: Dear father, you have won this state by your own deeds. ॥4॥
aranya.31.cau5: For those in whose hearts the good of others dwells, nothing in the world is hard to win.
Leave your body, dear father, and go to my abode. What can I give you? You have nothing left to desire. ॥5॥
aranya.31.do31: Dear father, do not go and tell my father of Sītā's abduction.
If I am Rāma, Rāvaṇa will come there with all his family and tell it himself. ॥31॥
aranya.32.cau1: Leaving the vulture's body, he took on the form of Śrī Hari, with many ornaments and peerless yellow garments.
Dark of body, with four mighty arms, his eyes brimming with tears, he sang the Lord's praise: ॥1॥
aranya.32.cha1: Glory to you, Śrī Rāma, of peerless form, without attributes and with them, truly the mover of the guṇas.
With fierce arrows you sever the mighty arms of the ten-headed one; you are the ornament of the earth.
Your body is the colour of a rain-cloud, your face a lotus, your eyes long like lotus petals.
I bow always to the compassionate Śrī Rāma, of mighty arms, who frees us from the fear of worldly existence. ॥1॥
aranya.32.cha2: You are might itself, immeasurable, without beginning, unborn, unmanifest, one, beyond perception;
Govinda, beyond the senses, remover of the pairs of opposites, realised knowledge in solid form, upholder of the earth.
You delight the minds of the countless saints and devotees who chant the Rāma mantra.
I bow always to Śrī Rāma, beloved of the desireless, who crushes the host of the wicked: desire and the rest. ॥2॥
aranya.32.cha3: He whom the Vedas hail as stainless, Brahman, all-pervading, free of passion and unborn;
whom many sages reach through meditation, knowledge, dispassion and yoga —
he, the root of compassion, the sum of all beauty, has appeared and enchants the moving and unmoving world.
In the lotus of my heart he hovers like a bee; the loveliness of many Kāmadevas shines in his limbs. ॥3॥
aranya.32.cha4: He who is hard to reach and easy, pure in nature, peerless yet even to all, ever cool and calm;
whom yogis see after great effort, keeping mind and senses always in check;
that Rāma, abode of Lakṣmī, master of the three worlds, is ever at the will of his servants.
May he dwell in my heart, he who ends the round of births, whose fame makes all pure. ॥4॥
aranya.32.do32: Asking for the boon of unbroken devotion, the vulture went to the abode of Śrī Hari.
With his own hands Śrī Rāma performed his last rites as was fitting. ॥32॥
aranya.33.cau1: Śrī Rāma is very tender of heart, kind to the lowly and merciful without cause.
To a vulture, a lowly bird that fed on flesh, he gave the state that yogis pray for. ॥1॥
aranya.33.cau2: Listen, Umā: unfortunate are those who leave Śrī Hari and give their love to the objects of the senses.
Then the two brothers went on searching for Sītā, seeing how thick the forest grew. ॥2॥
aranya.33.cau3: The dense forest was crowded with creepers and trees, and there were many birds and beasts, elephants and lions.
Śrī Rāma struck down Kabandha, who came at them on the way, and Kabandha told the whole story of his curse. ॥3॥
aranya.33.cau4: Kabandha said: The sage Durvāsā cursed me; at the sight of the Lord's feet that sin is gone.
Śrī Rāma said: Listen, Gandharva, I tell you this: one who is hostile to the race of brāhmaṇas does not please me. ॥4॥
aranya.33.do33: He who sets aside deceit in thought, deed and word and serves the brāhmaṇas, the gods on earth,
has all the gods, Brahmā and Śiva and me with them, under his sway. ॥33॥
aranya.34.cau1: A brāhmaṇa who curses, strikes or speaks harshly is still to be revered: so the saints sing.
A brāhmaṇa should be honoured even when lacking good conduct and virtue, but not a Śūdra, however rich in virtues and skilled in knowledge. ॥1॥
aranya.34.cau2: The Lord explained his own dharma to him, and seeing his love for his feet was pleased at heart.
Bowing his head at Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, Kabandha regained his own state and went up into the sky. ॥2॥
aranya.34.cau3: Having given him that state, the generous Śrī Rāma set foot in the hermitage of Śabarī.
Śabarī saw that Śrī Rāma had come to her home; the sage's words came back to her, and her heart rejoiced. ॥3॥
aranya.34.cau4: Eyes like lotuses, long arms, crowns of matted hair on their heads, garlands of wild flowers on their breasts:
at the feet of the two lovely brothers, one dark and one fair, Śabarī fell and clung to them. ॥4॥
aranya.34.cau5: Sunk in love, she could find no words; over and over she laid her head at their lotus feet.
Then she reverently took water and washed their feet, and seated them on beautiful seats. ॥5॥
aranya.34.do34: She brought tubers, roots and fruits, full of sweet juice, and gave them to Śrī Rāma.
The Lord ate them with love, praising them again and again. ॥34॥
aranya.35.cau1: She stood in front of him with palms joined, and at the sight of the Lord her love welled up all the more.
Śabarī said: In what way am I to praise you? I am of lowly birth and very slow of mind. ॥1॥
aranya.35.cau2: Among those counted lowest of the low, a woman is lower still, and among them, destroyer of sin, I am dull of mind.
Śrī Rāma said: Listen to what I say, good lady: the one bond I acknowledge is that of devotion. ॥2॥
aranya.35.cau3: Caste, community, lineage, dharma, standing, wealth, strength, kinsfolk, virtues and cleverness: with all of these,
how does a man without devotion appear? Like a cloud that is seen to hold no water. ॥3॥
aranya.35.cau4: I shall tell you of devotion in its nine forms; listen with care and keep it in your mind.
The first devotion is the company of saints; the second, love for the telling of my story. ॥4॥
aranya.35.do35: The third devotion is service, free of pride, at the lotus feet of one's guru.
The fourth is to sing the host of my virtues, leaving all deceit behind. ॥35॥
aranya.36.cau1: The fifth form of worship, which the Vedas make known, is repeating my mantra and holding firm trust in me.
The sixth is self-restraint, good conduct, dispassion towards a host of activities, and being ever engaged in the dharma of the good. ॥1॥
aranya.36.cau2: The seventh is to see the whole world alike as full of me, and to hold the saints higher than me.
The eighth is contentment with whatever comes, and not seeing others' faults even in a dream. ॥2॥
aranya.36.cau3: The ninth is simplicity, guilelessness with everyone, trust in me in the heart, and neither elation nor dejection.
Whoever has even one of these nine, be it a woman, a man or any being, moving or unmoving, ॥3॥
aranya.36.cau4: is exceedingly dear to me, good lady; and in you devotion of every kind is firm.
Today the state that is hard to reach even for hosts of yogis has become easy for you. ॥4॥
aranya.36.cau5: The fruit of seeing me is supreme and beyond compare: the soul attains its own natural form.
Good lady, if you know any news of Janaka's daughter, who walks with the grace of a noble elephant, tell me. ॥5॥
aranya.36.cau6: Śabarī said: O Lord of the Raghus, make your way to the Pampā lake; there Sugrīva will become your friend.
He will tell you all, my Lord, O hero of the Raghus. Steady of mind, you know it all and still you ask me. ॥6॥
aranya.36.cau7: Laying her head at the Lord's feet time after time, she told him the whole story with love. ॥7॥
aranya.36.cha1: Having told the whole story, she gazed on Śrī Hari's face and set his lotus feet within her heart.
Leaving her body in the fire of yoga, she was absorbed into Śrī Hari's state, from which none returns.
O people, your many kinds of rites, your wrongdoing and your many creeds all bring grief; leave every one of them.
The servant Tulasīdāsa says: hold to faith, and love the feet of Śrī Rāma. ॥1॥
aranya.36.do36: He set free even such a woman, of lowly caste and a very birthplace of sins;
utterly dull mind, do you seek happiness while forgetting such a Lord? ॥36॥
aranya.37.cau1: Śrī Rāma left that forest too and went on; matchless in strength, the two brothers were lions among men.
Grieving like one parted from his beloved, the Lord told many stories and talked of many things. ॥1॥
aranya.37.cau2: Śrī Rāma said: Lakṣmaṇa, see how beautiful the forest is. Who could look at it and keep his heart unshaken?
All the flocks of birds and herds of beasts are with their mates, as though they were reproaching me. ॥2॥
aranya.37.cau3: When the herds of deer see us they run away, and the does say to them: You have nothing to fear.
You were born of deer; be glad. These two have come looking for a golden deer. ॥3॥
aranya.37.cau4: The elephants keep their mates close beside them, as if giving me a lesson.
Even a well-pondered scripture is to be looked into again and again; even a well-served king is never to be thought of as under one's control. ॥4॥
aranya.37.cau5: A woman may be kept within the very heart, yet a young woman, a scripture and a king are never anyone's to command.
Look, brother, at this lovely spring; without my beloved it fills me with fear. ॥5॥
aranya.37.do37क: Knowing me to be distraught with separation, powerless and utterly alone,
Kāmadeva, with the forest, the bees and the birds, charged down on me in one line. ॥37 (क)॥
aranya.37.do37ख: But his envoy saw me with my brother, and hearing his report,
the mind-born god, it seems, held back his army and then pitched camp. ॥37 (ख)॥
aranya.38.cau1: Creepers are tangled over the great trees as though canopies of many kinds had been stretched out.
Plantains and palms are the fine flags and banners; only one whose mind is steadfast is not bewitched at the sight of them. ॥1॥
aranya.38.cau2: Trees of many sorts are in flower in many ways, like archers decked out in many uniforms.
Here and there handsome trees stand out, like warriors encamped apart from one another. ॥2॥
aranya.38.cau3: The calling cuckoos are, as it were, maddened elephants; the ḍheka and mahokha birds are camels and mules.
Peacocks, cakoras and parrots are fine horses; pigeons and swans are all Arab steeds. ॥3॥
aranya.38.cau4: Partridges and quails are the companies of foot soldiers; the host of Kāmadeva is beyond describing.
Mountain rocks are the chariots, waterfalls the drums, and the cātaka birds the heralds reciting his glories. ॥4॥
aranya.38.cau5: The humming bees are the kettledrums and pipes; the threefold breeze (cool, gentle and fragrant) has come as his envoy.
With his fourfold army about him, he roams everywhere, challenging all. ॥5॥
aranya.38.cau6: Lakṣmaṇa, those who stay steady at the sight of Kāmadeva's army are the ones whose name stands in the world.
His one supreme strength is woman; he who escapes her is a great warrior indeed. ॥6॥
aranya.38.do38क: Brother, three villains are exceedingly strong: desire, anger and greed.
Even the minds of sages who are homes of realised knowledge they unsettle in the blink of an eye. ॥38 (क)॥
aranya.38.do38ख: Greed draws its strength from craving and pretence; desire, from woman alone;
and anger, from harsh words: so the great sages say after reflection. ॥38 (ख)॥
aranya.39.cau1: Umā, Śrī Rāma is beyond the guṇas, master of all that moves and does not move, and the indweller of all.
He showed how helpless are those ruled by desire, and made dispassion firm in the minds of the steadfast. ॥1॥
aranya.39.cau2: Anger, desire, greed, pride and māyā all fall away by Śrī Rāma's mercy.
The man on whom that conjurer looks with favour is not led astray by his magic. ॥2॥
aranya.39.cau3: Umā, I tell you what I have known for myself: worship of Śrī Hari is true, and all the world a dream.
Then the Lord went to the shore of a lake named Pampā, lovely and deep. ॥3॥
aranya.39.cau4: Its water is clear as a saint's heart, and four charming ghāṭs have been built on it.
Here and there beasts of many kinds drink its water, like a crowd of petitioners at a generous man's door. ॥4॥
aranya.39.do39क: Screened by the dense lotus leaves, the water is not quickly found out,
just as the attributeless Brahman, veiled by māyā, is not seen. ॥39 (क)॥
aranya.39.do39ख: In the fathomless water all the fish live in unbroken happiness,
as the days of the righteous pass in joy. ॥39 (ख)॥
aranya.40.cau1: Lotuses of many colours have opened, and many bees hum sweetly.
Waterfowl and sweet-voiced swans call out, as if singing the praises of the Lord at the sight of him. ॥1॥
aranya.40.cau2: The flocks of cakravākas, herons and other birds must be seen; they cannot be described.
The sweet calls of the lovely birds seem to summon the travellers passing by. ॥2॥
aranya.40.cau3: Near the lake sages have roofed their huts, and all around are the lovely trees of the forest:
campaka, bakula, kadamba, tamāla, pāṭala, jackfruit, palāśa and mango. ॥3॥
aranya.40.cau4: Trees of many kinds are full of new leaves and flowers, and rows of bees sing on them.
A charming breeze blows without ceasing, cool, gentle and fragrant by nature. ॥4॥
aranya.40.cau5: The cuckoos call kuhū, kuhū; hearing their sweet voices, sages are drawn from their meditation. ॥5॥
aranya.40.do40: Bowed by the weight of their fruit, all the trees bend close to the ground,
as those who do good to others bow low when good fortune comes to them. ॥40॥
aranya.41.cau1: Seeing the exceedingly lovely pool, Śrī Rāma bathed in it and was supremely happy.
Finding the shade of a fine tree, Śrī Rāma sat down there with his younger brother. ॥1॥
aranya.41.cau2: Then all the gods and sages came there too, sang his praises and went back to their own abodes.
The compassionate Lord sat in great delight, telling his brother stories full of charm. ॥2॥
aranya.41.cau3: Seeing the Lord in the grief of separation, Nārada was deeply troubled at heart.
He thought: Accepting my curse, Śrī Rāma is bearing a heavy load of many sorrows. ॥3॥
aranya.41.cau4: I must go and see such a Lord; such a chance will not come again.
Thinking so, Nārada took up his vīṇā and made his way to where the Lord sat at his ease. ॥4॥
aranya.41.cau5: He was singing the story of Śrī Rāma in a gentle voice, lovingly dwelling on it in many ways.
The moment he prostrated, the Lord lifted him and kept him clasped to his heart a long while. ॥5॥
aranya.41.cau6: The Lord asked after his welfare and seated him close by, and Lakṣmaṇa reverently washed his feet. ॥6॥
aranya.41.do41: After entreating him in many ways, and knowing the Lord to be pleased at heart,
Nārada then folded his lotus hands and spoke: ॥41॥
aranya.42.cau1: Hear me, O Lord of the Raghus, bountiful by nature: fair boons, rare ones and easy ones alike, are yours to give.
My Lord, I have one boon to ask; grant it to me, though you know every heart and it is no secret to you. ॥1॥
aranya.42.cau2: Śrī Rāma said: Sage, you know my nature; do I ever hide anything from my devotee?
What thing is so dear to me, best of sages, that you could not ask for it? ॥2॥
aranya.42.cau3: In my mind there is nothing my devotee may not be given; never let go of this faith, even by mistake.
Then Nārada spoke joyfully: Making bold, I ask this boon: ॥3॥
aranya.42.cau4: Though the Lord has many names, and the Vedas say they surpass one another,
may the name Rāma, my Lord, be greater than all names, and be a hunter to the flocks of birds that are sins. ॥4॥
aranya.42.do42क: Let devotion to you be the full-moon night, and the name Rāma be its moon;
let the other names be the stars, and may they dwell in the clear sky of the devotees' hearts. ॥42 (क)॥
aranya.42.do42ख: Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, said to the sage: So be it.
Then Nārada's heart filled with great joy, and he bowed his head at the Lord's feet. ॥42 (ख)॥
aranya.43.cau1: Knowing Śrī Rāma to be very pleased, Nārada spoke again in a gentle voice:
Rāma, when you set your own māyā to work and it bewitched me — listen, O Lord of the Raghus — ॥1॥
aranya.43.cau2: I wished then to marry; for what reason, Lord, did you not let me?
Śrī Rāma said: Listen, sage, I tell you with emphasis: those who give up every other support and worship me, ॥2॥
aranya.43.cau3: I always keep watch over them, as a mother guards her child.
If a little child runs to grab fire or a snake, the mother pulls it away and keeps it safe. ॥3॥
aranya.43.cau4: When the son is grown, his mother still loves him, but it is not as it was before.
To me the wise man is like a grown son, and the servant without pride like an infant son. ॥4॥
aranya.43.cau5: My servant has my strength, while the wise man has his own; desire and anger are enemies to both.
Weighing this, the learned worship me, and even when they have gained knowledge they do not give up devotion. ॥5॥
aranya.43.do43: Desire, anger, greed and the rest, and pride, are the mighty army of delusion.
Among them the most dreadful and the most painful is woman, the very form of māyā. ॥43॥
aranya.44.cau1: Listen, sage: the Purāṇas, the Vedas and the saints say that to the forest of delusion woman is the spring.
Japa, austerity and religious observances are pools of water; woman turns into the summer and drains every one of them. ॥1॥
aranya.44.cau2: Desire, anger, pride and envy are frogs, and she alone is the rainy season that gladdens them.
Evil longings are a mass of night-lotuses, and to them she is the autumn, always bringing delight. ॥2॥
aranya.44.cau3: All forms of dharma are clusters of lotuses; woman, giver of a lowly pleasure, becomes the cold season and scorches them.
Then the dense growth of javāsā that is attachment springs green again when it finds woman as its late-winter season. ॥3॥
aranya.44.cau4: To the flocks of owls that are sins, woman is a night of thick darkness, much to their liking.
Intellect, strength, good conduct and truth are all fish, and the skilled say that woman is like a fishing hook to them. ॥4॥
aranya.44.do44: The young woman is the root of faults, a giver of pain and a mine of every sorrow.
Knowing this in my heart, sage, I held you back. ॥44॥
aranya.45.cau1: Hearing Śrī Rāma's lovely words, the sage thrilled all over and his eyes filled with tears.
His heart cried out: Tell me, what master ever had such a way, such tenderness and love for his servant? ॥1॥
aranya.45.cau2: Such is the Lord, and those who will not lay delusion aside to worship him are paupers in knowledge, foolish and ill-fated.
Then the sage Nārada spoke again with reverence: Listen, Rāma, master of realised knowledge. ॥2॥
aranya.45.cau3: O hero of the Raghus, my Lord who breaks the fear of worldly existence, tell me the marks of saints.
Śrī Rāma said: Listen, sage, I will tell you the virtues of saints, by which I remain in their power. ॥3॥
aranya.45.cau4: Saints have conquered the six vices; they are sinless, free of desire, unshaken, owning nothing, pure, and homes of happiness.
Their understanding is boundless; they want nothing, enjoy in measure, are true to the core, and are poets, learned men and yogis. ॥4॥
aranya.45.cau5: They are watchful, give honour to others, are free of pride and steadfast, and are supremely skilled in the way of dharma. ॥5॥
aranya.45.do45: Virtue makes its home in them; the world's sorrows do not touch them, and doubt has left them.
Apart from my lotus feet, neither their body nor their home is dear to them. ॥45॥
aranya.46.cau1: They shrink from hearing their own virtues and are all the more glad to hear of others'.
They are even and calm and never leave the right way; simple by nature, they have love for all. ॥1॥
aranya.46.cau2: They have japa, austerity, vows, restraint of the senses, self-control and observances, and love for the feet of the guru, of Govinda and of brāhmaṇas.
They have faith, forgiveness, friendliness, mercy, gladness at others' joy, and guileless love for my feet. ॥2॥
aranya.46.cau3: They have dispassion, discernment, humility, realised knowledge and a true understanding of the Vedas and Purāṇas.
They never practise hypocrisy, conceit or pride, and never set foot on a wrong path, even by mistake. ॥3॥
aranya.46.cau4: They always sing and hear of my divine play, and it is their nature to be given to the good of others without any motive.
Listen, sage: Sarasvatī and the Vedas cannot tell all the virtues that saints have. ॥4॥
aranya.46.cha1: Even Sarasvatī and Śeṣa cannot tell them all: the moment Nārada heard this, he took hold of the Lord's lotus feet.
So did the compassionate Lord, friend of the lowly, speak with his own mouth of his devotees' virtues.
Bowing his head again and again at the Lord's feet, Nārada went to the realm of Brahmā.
Tulasīdāsa says that those are blessed who have let go of every hope and taken on the colour of Śrī Hari. ॥1॥
aranya.46.do46क: People who sing and hear the purifying fame of Śrī Rāma, the foe of Rāvaṇa,
gain firm devotion to Śrī Rāma without dispassion, japa or yoga. ॥46 (क)॥
aranya.46.do46ख: A young woman's body is like a lamp's flame; my mind, do not be its moth.
Give up desire and pride, worship Śrī Rāma, and always keep the company of the good. ॥46 (ख)॥
kishkindha.0.shloka1: Beautiful as the jasmine and the blue lotus, mighty beyond measure, both abodes of realised knowledge,
rich in splendour, excellent archers, praised by the Vedas, dear to the hosts of cows and Brahmins,
taking human form by māyā (the Lord's power of illusion), the two best of the Raghus, the armour of true dharma, benevolent to all,
intent on the search for Sītā and travelling the road: may those two indeed grant us devotion. ॥1॥
kishkindha.0.shloka2: Born of the ocean of the Veda, utterly destroying the stains of the Kali age, and imperishable,
ever shining on the lovely, peerless moon of glorious Śiva's face,
the medicine for the sickness of worldly existence, the giver of joy, the very life of Śrī Jānakī:
blessed are the meritorious who drink without ceasing the nectar of Śrī Rāma's name. ॥2॥
kishkindha.0.sou1: Knowing Kāśī as the land where liberation is born, a mine of knowledge and the destroyer of sin,
and the place where Śiva and Bhavānī dwell, why should one not turn to Kāśī and live there?
kishkindha.0.sou2: He drank the deadly poison when the hosts of gods were burning:
dull mind, why do you not worship him? Who is as compassionate as Śaṅkara?
kishkindha.1.cau1: Then Śrī Rāma went on and drew near the mountain Ṛṣyamūka.
There Sugrīva lived with his ministers. Seeing the two coming, the very bounds of matchless strength, ॥1॥
kishkindha.1.cau2: Sugrīva, greatly alarmed, said: Listen, Hanumān: these two men are treasuries of strength and beauty.
Take the form of a young brahmacārī, go and see. Find out in your mind who they are, and let me know by a sign. ॥2॥
kishkindha.1.cau3: If they are sent by Vāli and mean harm, I must flee at once and leave this mountain.
Hanumān took the form of a Brahmin and went there, and bowing his head he asked: ॥3॥
kishkindha.1.cau4: Who are you, heroes, one dark and one fair, roaming the forest in the guise of Kṣatriyas?
Treading the hard ground on tender feet, my lords, for what reason do you wander in the forest? ॥4॥
kishkindha.1.cau5: Your limbs are soft, charming and beautiful, yet you bear the harsh sun and winds of the forest.
Are you one of the three gods, or are you the two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa? ॥5॥
kishkindha.1.do1: Or are you the cause of the world, who carries souls across worldly existence and lifts the burden of the earth,
the Lord of all the worlds, who has come down in human form? ॥1॥
kishkindha.2.cau1: Śrī Rāma said: We are sons of Daśaratha, king of Kosala, and we came to the forest at our father's bidding.
We are two brothers named Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. With us was a lovely woman of delicate frame. ॥1॥
kishkindha.2.cau2: Here a demon carried off Sītā, and we wander searching for her, Brahmin.
We have told you our own story; now, Brahmin, tell us yours plainly. ॥2॥
kishkindha.2.cau3: Recognising the Lord, Hanumān clasped his feet and fell at them. That joy, Umā, cannot be described.
His body thrilled; he could not utter a word, gazing at the beauty of the Lord's guise. ॥3॥
kishkindha.2.cau4: Then, steadying himself, he sang the Lord's praise, his heart glad at knowing his own master.
He said: My Lord, it was right for me to ask; but why do you ask, as if you were a man? ॥4॥
kishkindha.2.cau5: Under the sway of your māyā I wander astray; that is why I did not know my Lord. ॥5॥
kishkindha.2.do2: For one thing, I am dull, in the grip of delusion, crooked of heart and ignorant;
and then the Lord, the friend of the lowly, forgot me as well. ॥2॥
kishkindha.3.cau1: My Lord, though I have many faults, let the servant never slip from his master's mind.
My Lord, the soul is deluded by your māyā; it is set free only by your own grace. ॥1॥
kishkindha.3.cau2: Besides, O hero of the Raghus, I swear by you that I know no way at all of worship.
A servant relying on his master, and a son on his mother, stays free of care; it falls to the master to provide for him. ॥2॥
kishkindha.3.cau3: With these words, overwhelmed, he threw himself at the Lord's feet; he showed his own form, and love flooded his heart.
Then Śrī Rāma raised him and held him to his breast, and soothed him, bathing him with the tears of his own eyes. ॥3॥
kishkindha.3.cau4: The Lord said: Listen, Hanumān: let your heart not be downcast; I hold you twice as dear as Lakṣmaṇa.
All call me impartial; yet my servant is dear to me, since he has no other refuge. ॥4॥
kishkindha.3.do3: Hanumān, he alone is single-minded whose understanding never wavers from this:
I am the servant, and my master is the Lord, whose form is all that moves and all that does not move. ॥3॥
kishkindha.4.cau1: Seeing his master favourable, Hanumān, son of the Wind, rejoiced at heart, and all his pain was gone.
He said: My Lord, the king of the monkeys lives on this mountain; that Sugrīva is your servant. ॥1॥
kishkindha.4.cau2: My Lord, make friends with him, and knowing him to be helpless, free him from fear.
He will set the search for Sītā going; he will send out monkeys by the million, here and there. ॥2॥
kishkindha.4.cau3: Having explained the whole matter so, he took them both up on his back.
The sight of Śrī Rāma made Sugrīva feel that his birth had been supremely blessed. ॥3॥
kishkindha.4.cau4: He greeted them with reverence, bowing his head at their feet, and Śrī Rāma and his younger brother embraced him.
Sugrīva thought to himself: O Creator, will these two show me love? ॥4॥
kishkindha.4.do4: Then Hanumān told each side the other's whole story,
and, with fire as witness, joined them in a friendship firmly sealed. ॥4॥
kishkindha.5.cau1: They made friends and held nothing back between them, and Lakṣmaṇa told all of Śrī Rāma's story.
Sugrīva, his eyes filled with tears, said: My Lord, the princess of Mithilā will be found. ॥1॥
kishkindha.5.cau2: Once I was sitting here with my ministers, deep in thought,
when I saw her going by the path of the sky, helpless in another's power and weeping bitterly. ॥2॥
kishkindha.5.cau3: Crying, Rāma, Rāma, alas Rāma, she saw us and let fall a garment.
Śrī Rāma asked for it, and Sugrīva gave it at once. Pressing the cloth to his breast, he grieved deeply. ॥3॥
kishkindha.5.cau4: Sugrīva said: Listen, O hero of the Raghus: put away grief and take courage.
I will serve you in every way, so that Jānakī may come back to you. ॥4॥
kishkindha.5.do5: Hearing his friend's words, the ocean of mercy, the utmost in strength, was glad,
and said: Tell me, Sugrīva, why do you live in the forest? ॥5॥
kishkindha.6.cau1: Sugrīva said: My Lord, Vāli and I are brothers, and the love between us was beyond words.
My Lord, a son of Maya, Māyāvī by name, came to our town. ॥1॥
kishkindha.6.cau2: At midnight he shouted his challenge at the city gate, and Vāli could not bear the enemy's show of might.
Vāli ran at him, and seeing him the other fled; I too went, close behind my brother. ॥2॥
kishkindha.6.cau3: He went into a cave in a great mountain, and then Vāli told me plainly:
Wait for me a fortnight; if I do not come back by then, know that I have been killed. ॥3॥
kishkindha.6.cau4: I stayed there a month, O slayer of Khara, and then a great stream of blood gushed out.
He has killed Vāli, I thought, and will come and kill me; so I set a rock there and fled. ॥4॥
kishkindha.6.cau5: Seeing the city without its lord, the ministers made me king against my will.
Vāli killed him and came home, and seeing me he let ill feeling grow in his heart. ॥5॥
kishkindha.6.cau6: He beat me savagely, as one beats an enemy, and seized all I had, and my wife too.
For fear of him, O compassionate hero of the Raghus, I wandered all the worlds in distress. ॥6॥
kishkindha.6.cau7: Because of a curse he does not come here, and still I live in fear at heart.
As he heard his servant's sorrow, the Lord who is kind to the lowly felt both his mighty arms throb. ॥7॥
kishkindha.6.do6: Śrī Rāma said: Listen, Sugrīva: one arrow alone will slay Vāli.
Even if he runs to Brahmā and Rudra for refuge, his life will not be spared. ॥6॥
kishkindha.7.cau1: Those who are not pained by a friend's pain: even to look on them is a grave sin.
One should count one's own mountain of sorrow as a speck of dust, and a friend's speck of sorrow as Mount Meru. ॥1॥
kishkindha.7.cau2: Those in whom such a mind has not come naturally, why do the fools insist on making friends?
A friend turns one from the wrong path to the right one, makes one's virtues known and hides one's faults. ॥2॥
kishkindha.7.cau3: He gives and takes with no misgiving in his mind, and always does one good as far as his strength allows.
In times of trouble his love grows a hundredfold. The Vedas say these are the marks of a good friend. ॥3॥
kishkindha.7.cau4: One who speaks soft, studied words to your face, but behind your back works harm with crookedness in his heart,
whose mind, brother, moves crookedly like a snake: such a false friend is best given up. ॥4॥
kishkindha.7.cau5: A wicked servant, a miserly king, an ill-natured woman and a deceitful friend: these four are like a stabbing pain.
Friend, set your worry aside and rely on my strength; I will do your work in every way. ॥5॥
kishkindha.7.cau6: Sugrīva said: Listen, O hero of the Raghus: Vāli is mighty and unshaken in battle.
Sugrīva showed him the bones of Dundubhi and the palm trees, and Śrī Rāma brought them down without effort. ॥6॥
kishkindha.7.cau7: Seeing his boundless strength, Sugrīva loved him the more, and was sure that he would slay Vāli.
Again and again he bowed his head at the Lord's feet; knowing him for the Lord, the king of the monkeys rejoiced at heart. ॥7॥
kishkindha.7.cau8: Then knowledge dawned on him, and he said: My Lord, by your grace my mind has become still.
I will give up comfort, wealth, family and greatness, all of it, and serve you. ॥8॥
kishkindha.7.cau9: The saints who worship your feet say that all these stand in the way of devotion to Rāma.
Foe and friend, joy and sorrow in this world are the work of māyā, not the ultimate truth. ॥9॥
kishkindha.7.cau10: It is Vāli who has done me the greatest good, Rāma: thanks to him I have found you, who end all sorrow.
If one fights with someone in a dream, on waking one understands and feels abashed. ॥10॥
kishkindha.7.cau11: My Lord, now grant me this grace, that I may leave everything and worship you day and night.
Hearing Sugrīva's words full of dispassion, Śrī Rāma, bow in hand, smiled and said: ॥11॥
kishkindha.7.cau12: All that you have said is true; but, friend, my word cannot prove false.
As a showman makes a monkey dance, Garuḍa, so Śrī Rāma makes all dance: so the Vedas sing. ॥12॥
kishkindha.7.cau13: Taking Sugrīva with him, Śrī Rāma set out, bow and arrows in hand.
Then Śrī Rāma sent Sugrīva on; strengthened by him, Sugrīva went close and roared. ॥13॥
kishkindha.7.cau14: Hearing it, Vāli rushed out in a fury; his wife caught his feet in her hands and pleaded with him:
Listen, my husband: the two brothers Sugrīva has joined are the very bounds of splendour and strength. ॥14॥
kishkindha.7.cau15: They are Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma, sons of the king of Kosala, who could conquer even Death in battle. ॥15॥
kishkindha.7.do7: Vāli said: Listen, my timid dear: Śrī Rāma looks on all alike.
If perchance he kills me, then I shall have found my Lord. ॥7॥
kishkindha.8.cau1: With these words Vāli set out in his great pride, counting Sugrīva no more than a blade of grass.
The two clashed. Vāli taunted him fiercely, struck him with his fist and gave a mighty roar. ॥1॥
kishkindha.8.cau2: Then Sugrīva fled in distress, for the blow of that fist had struck him like a thunderbolt.
Sugrīva said: It is as I told you, O compassionate hero of the Raghus: he is not my brother; he is my death. ॥2॥
kishkindha.8.cau3: Śrī Rāma said: You two brothers look alike, and because of that confusion I did not kill him.
He laid his hand on Sugrīva, whose body turned hard as a thunderbolt, and every pain left him. ॥3॥
kishkindha.8.cau4: He placed a garland of flowers round Sugrīva's neck and sent him back, giving him great strength.
Again the two fought in many ways, while Śrī Rāma watched from behind a tree. ॥4॥
kishkindha.8.do8: Sugrīva tried many tricks and all his strength, then, seized by fear, lost heart.
Then Śrī Rāma drew an arrow and shot Vāli in the middle of his chest. ॥8॥
kishkindha.9.cau1: Struck by the arrow, Vāli fell to the ground in agony, but seeing the Lord before him he rose and sat up.
Dark was the Lord's body, his hair bound up in matted locks on his head, his eyes red, an arrow fitted to his bow. ॥1॥
kishkindha.9.cau2: Gazing again and again, he set his mind on the Lord's feet; he knew him for the Lord and held his birth fulfilled.
There was love in his heart but harsh words on his lips; looking at Śrī Rāma, he said: ॥2॥
kishkindha.9.cau3: My Lord, you came down to earth for the sake of dharma, yet you have killed me like a hunter.
Am I your enemy, and Sugrīva dear to you? For what fault, my Lord, have you killed me? ॥3॥
kishkindha.9.cau4: Śrī Rāma said: Listen, wicked one: a younger brother's wife, a sister, a son's wife and a daughter — these four are all alike.
Whoever looks on them with an evil eye may be slain, and there is no sin in it. ॥4॥
kishkindha.9.cau5: Fool, your pride is beyond measure; you would not listen to your wife's counsel.
You knew he leant on the strength of my arms, and still, base and arrogant as you are, you sought to kill him. ॥5॥
kishkindha.9.do9: Vāli said: Listen, Rāma: my cleverness is of no use before my master.
My Lord, now that at my last hour I have you for my refuge, am I a sinner still? ॥9॥
kishkindha.10.cau1: Hearing Vāli's very gentle words, Śrī Rāma laid his own hand on his head.
Śrī Rāma said: Let me make your body undying; keep your life. Vāli said: Listen, treasury of mercy: ॥1॥
kishkindha.10.cau2: Sages strive birth after birth, and yet at the end the name Rāma does not rise to their lips.
He by the power of whose name Śiva grants to all alike in Kāśī the state that never perishes ॥2॥
kishkindha.10.cau3: has come before my eyes. My Lord, will such a chance ever come about again? ॥3॥
kishkindha.10.cha1: He whose virtues the Vedas ever sing, saying “not this, not this”, stands before my eyes,
he whom sages, having mastered breath and mind and drained the senses of their relish, only now and then attain in meditation.
Taking me to be in the grip of great pride, the Lord told me to keep my body;
but who would be fool enough to insist on cutting down the wish-fulfilling tree to make a hedge for an acacia? ॥1॥
kishkindha.10.cha2: Now, my Lord, look on me with compassion and grant the boon I ask:
in whatever form of life my karma has me born, there may I love Śrī Rāma's feet.
This son of mine is my equal in humility and strength; take him to yourself, Lord, giver of all good.
Lord of gods and men, take Aṅgada by the arm and make him your own servant. ॥2॥
kishkindha.10.do10: Holding firm in love for Śrī Rāma's feet, Vāli gave up his body,
as an elephant does not even notice a garland of flowers slipping from its neck. ॥10॥
kishkindha.11.cau1: Śrī Rāma sent Vāli to his own abode. The townsfolk all came running in distress.
Tārā lamented in many ways, her hair loosened, heedless of her body. ॥1॥
kishkindha.11.cau2: Seeing Tārā distraught, Śrī Rāma gave her knowledge and lifted the māyā that held her.
He said: Earth, water, fire, sky and air — of these five is this body made, and it is utterly base. ॥2॥
kishkindha.11.cau3: That body lies plainly before you in sleep, and the soul is eternal: for whom, then, do you weep?
Knowledge dawned in her; she fell at the Lord's feet and asked for, and received, the boon of supreme devotion. ॥3॥
kishkindha.11.cau4: Umā, the Lord Śrī Rāma makes all dance like a wooden puppet.
Then he gave Sugrīva his command, and Sugrīva duly performed all the rites for the dead. ॥4॥
kishkindha.11.cau5: Śrī Rāma instructed his younger brother: Go and give the kingdom to Sugrīva.
Bowing their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet, all set out as he bade them. ॥5॥
kishkindha.11.do11: Lakṣmaṇa at once summoned the townspeople and an assembly of Brahmins,
and gave the kingdom to Sugrīva and to Aṅgada the rank of heir to the throne. ॥11॥
kishkindha.12.cau1: Umā, there is no friend in the world like Śrī Rāma: no guru, father, mother, brother or master.
Gods, men and sages all follow one way: they love for their own ends. ॥1॥
kishkindha.12.cau2: Sugrīva, harried day and night by dread of Vāli, his body covered with wounds and his breast burning with care —
that same Sugrīva the Lord made king of the monkeys. Such is the boundless compassion of Śrī Rāma's nature. ॥2॥
kishkindha.12.cau3: Why should those who forsake such a Lord, even knowing him, not fall into the net of misfortune?
Then he sent for Sugrīva and taught him the conduct of a king in many ways. ॥3॥
kishkindha.12.cau4: The Lord said: Listen, Sugrīva, king of the monkeys: for fourteen years I shall not enter a town.
The summer is over and the rains have come; I shall make my dwelling on a mountain close by. ॥4॥
kishkindha.12.cau5: Rule the kingdom with Aṅgada, and keep my work always in your heart.
When Sugrīva had gone back to his palace, Śrī Rāma made his dwelling on Mount Pravarṣaṇa. ॥5॥
kishkindha.12.do12: Long before, the gods had shaped a lovely cave in that mountain and kept it,
for Śrī Rāma, the treasury of mercy, would come and live there for some days. ॥12॥
kishkindha.13.cau1: The lovely forest, in full flower, was glorious, and swarms of bees hummed in their craving for honey.
From the time the Lord came, fine tubers, roots, fruits and leaves grew in plenty. ॥1॥
kishkindha.13.cau2: Seeing that charming, peerless mountain, Śrī Rāma, sovereign of the gods, stayed there with his younger brother.
Gods, siddhas and sages took the bodies of bees, birds and deer and served the Lord. ॥2॥
kishkindha.13.cau3: From the time the Lord of Ramā made his home there, the forest became full of blessing.
There was a slab of crystal, very white and fair, and on it the two brothers sat at ease. ॥3॥
kishkindha.13.cau4: He would tell his younger brother many discourses on devotion, dispassion, kingly conduct and discernment.
It was the season of rains; clouds covered the sky, and their thunder sounded most pleasing. ॥4॥
kishkindha.13.do13: Śrī Rāma said: Lakṣmaṇa, see the flocks of peacocks dancing at the sight of the clouds,
as a householder given to dispassion rejoices on seeing a devotee of Viṣṇu. ॥13॥
kishkindha.14.cau1: The massing clouds thunder dreadfully in the sky; without my beloved my heart is afraid.
The flash of lightning does not stay in the clouds, just as the love of the wicked does not last. ॥1॥
kishkindha.14.cau2: The clouds come down low to the earth to rain, as the wise bow down when they gain learning.
The mountains bear the beating of the drops as saints bear the words of the wicked. ॥2॥
kishkindha.14.cau3: The little rivers fill and rush on, breaking their banks, as the wicked swagger over even a little wealth.
Water falling on the ground turns muddy, as though māyā had wrapped itself round the soul. ॥3॥
kishkindha.14.cau4: Gathering little by little, the water fills the ponds, as good qualities come to a good man.
River water reaching the ocean grows still, as the soul becomes steadfast when it finds Śrī Hari. ॥4॥
kishkindha.14.do14: The earth is green and so thick with grass that no path can be made out,
as true scriptures are hidden by the wrangling of false doctrine. ॥14॥
kishkindha.15.cau1: The croaking of frogs on every side is pleasant, as though bands of young students were reciting the Vedas.
Many trees have put out new leaves, like the mind of a seeker who has found discernment. ॥1॥
kishkindha.15.cau2: The arka and javāsa plants have lost their leaves, as under good rule the schemes of the wicked come to nothing.
Search as you may, there is no dust to be found anywhere, as anger drives dharma far away. ॥2॥
kishkindha.15.cau3: How fair the earth looks, rich with crops, like the wealth of one who does good to others.
In the thick darkness of night the fireflies glitter, as if a band of hypocrites had gathered. ॥3॥
kishkindha.15.cau4: Heavy rain has burst the beds of the fields, as women go astray when they become independent.
Clever farmers weed their crops, as the wise cast off delusion, pride and vanity. ॥4॥
kishkindha.15.cau5: The cakravāka birds are nowhere to be seen, as virtues flee when the Kali age comes.
Rain falls on barren ground, but no grass springs up, as desire does not arise in the heart of Hari's devotee. ॥5॥
kishkindha.15.cau6: The earth teems and glows with creatures of every kind, as the people prosper under good rule.
Here and there many travellers have halted, weary, as the senses come to rest when knowledge arises. ॥6॥
kishkindha.15.do15क: At times a strong wind blows and the clouds melt away here and there,
as the good ways of a family perish when an unworthy son is born into it. ॥15 (क)॥
kishkindha.15.do15ख: At times there is deep darkness in the daytime, and at times the sun shines out,
as knowledge is lost in bad company and springs up again in good. ॥15 (ख)॥
kishkindha.16.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa, see: the rains are past and autumn has come, lovely beyond compare.
Flowering kāsa grass has spread over all the earth, as if the rainy season were showing its old age. ॥1॥
kishkindha.16.cau2: The star Agastya has risen, and the roads have lost their water, as greed is dried up by contentment.
The clear water of rivers and lakes is as lovely as a saint's heart freed from pride and delusion. ॥2॥
kishkindha.16.cau3: Little by little the water of rivers and lakes dries up, as the wise let go of the sense of “mine”.
Knowing autumn has come, the wagtails have arrived, as good deeds shine out when their time comes. ॥3॥
kishkindha.16.cau4: With neither mud nor dust, the earth looks as fine as the deeds of a king skilled in statecraft.
The fish are in distress as the water shrinks, like a foolish householder left without money. ॥4॥
kishkindha.16.cau5: The cloudless sky shines clear, like a devotee of Hari who has given up every hope.
Here and there falls a light autumn shower, as only a rare one gains devotion to me. ॥5॥
kishkindha.16.do16: Kings, ascetics, merchants and beggars have gladly left the cities and set out,
as people in all four stages of life lay down their toil once they gain devotion to Hari. ॥16॥
kishkindha.17.cau1: The fish in deep water are happy, as one who has taken refuge in Śrī Hari meets not a single obstacle.
With its lotuses in bloom the lake is as lovely as the attributeless Brahman when it takes on attributes. ॥1॥
kishkindha.17.cau2: The humming of the bees is wonderful to hear, and the birds raise lovely calls of many kinds.
The cakravāka is pained at heart to see the night fall, as a wicked man is pained to see another's wealth. ॥2॥
kishkindha.17.cau3: The cātaka keeps crying out, so great is its thirst, as one hostile to Śiva never finds happiness.
At night the moon takes away the heat of the autumn sun, as the sight of a saint drives sins away. ॥3॥
kishkindha.17.cau4: Flocks of cakoras gaze at the moon as devotees of Hari gaze on Hari when they have found him.
Mosquitoes and gadflies have died out for fear of the cold, as a family dies out when it turns against Brahmins. ॥4॥
kishkindha.17.do17: The creatures that had crowded the earth have gone now that autumn has come,
as hosts of doubts and delusions go when one meets a true guru. ॥17॥
kishkindha.18.cau1: Dear brother, the rains have passed and the clear season is here, yet no word of Sītā has reached us.
If once I can somehow learn where she is, I will conquer even Death and bring her back in the blink of an eye. ॥1॥
kishkindha.18.cau2: If she lives, dear brother, then wherever she is, I will make every effort and bring her home.
Even Sugrīva has let me slip from his mind: he has won a kingdom, a treasury, a city and a wife. ॥2॥
kishkindha.18.cau3: With the arrow that killed Vāli I will kill that fool tomorrow.
Umā, can he by whose grace pride and delusion fall away be angry even in a dream? ॥3॥
kishkindha.18.cau4: This play is understood only by wise sages who have given their love to the feet of Śrī Rāma.
Perceiving the Lord's anger, Lakṣmaṇa strung his bow and gripped arrows in his hand. ॥4॥
kishkindha.18.do18: Then Śrī Rāma, in whom compassion knows no bounds, counselled his younger brother:
Dear brother, only frighten my friend Sugrīva and bring him here. ॥18॥
kishkindha.19.cau1: Here Hanumān, son of the Wind, reflected that Sugrīva had forgotten Śrī Rāma's work.
He went to him, bowed his head at his feet, and reasoned with him in all four ways: conciliation, gifts, threat and division. ॥1॥
kishkindha.19.cau2: Hearing this, Sugrīva was seized with fear and said: The objects of the senses have stolen my wits.
Now, son of the Wind, send bands of messengers to wherever the troops of monkeys are, ॥2॥
kishkindha.19.cau3: and tell them that whoever does not come within a fortnight will die at my hands.
Then Hanumān summoned the messengers and showed them all great honour. ॥3॥
kishkindha.19.cau4: He set before them fear, affection and right counsel, and they all bowed at his feet and set off.
Just then Lakṣmaṇa came into the city; seeing his anger, the monkeys fled this way and that. ॥4॥
kishkindha.19.do19: Then, bow strung, he declared: I will reduce this city to ashes.
Seeing the city in distress, Vāli's son Aṅgada came forward. ॥19॥
kishkindha.20.cau1: Aṅgada bowed his head at his feet and pleaded, and Lakṣmaṇa held out his arm to him in assurance that he need not fear.
When the king of the monkeys heard with his own ears that Lakṣmaṇa was angry, he was overcome with fear and said: ॥1॥
kishkindha.20.cau2: Listen, Hanumān: go with Tārā, plead with the prince and bring him round.
Hanumān went with Tārā, bowed at Lakṣmaṇa's feet, and spoke of the Lord's fair fame. ॥2॥
kishkindha.20.cau3: Pleading with him, they led him into the palace, bathed his feet and gave him a seat on the couch.
Then Sugrīva, king of the monkeys, laid his head at his feet; Lakṣmaṇa clasped his arm and drew him to his breast. ॥3॥
kishkindha.20.cau4: Sugrīva said: My lord, nothing intoxicates like the objects of the senses; in a moment they cloud even the minds of sages.
Lakṣmaṇa was pleased to hear these humble words and counselled him in many ways. ॥4॥
kishkindha.20.cau5: Hanumān, son of the Wind, told the whole story of how the bands of messengers had gone out. ॥5॥
kishkindha.20.do20: Then Sugrīva set out joyfully, with Aṅgada and the other monkeys,
and with Śrī Rāma's younger brother leading the way they came to where Śrī Rāma was. ॥20॥
kishkindha.21.cau1: Sugrīva bowed his head at the Lord's feet and with joined palms said: My Lord, the fault is not mine at all.
Your māyā is overwhelmingly strong, O Lord; one is set free from it only if you show mercy, Rāma. ॥1॥
kishkindha.21.cau2: My Lord, gods, men and sages are all in the power of the senses, and I am a base beast, a monkey full of lust.
One whom the arrow of a woman's eyes has not struck, who has stayed awake through the dark night of fierce anger, ॥2॥
kishkindha.21.cau3: and who has never let the noose of greed close round his neck, is your equal, O Lord of the Raghus.
This virtue does not come by any practice; only a rare few gain it, by your grace. ॥3॥
kishkindha.21.cau4: Then Śrī Rāma smiled and said: You are as dear to me as my brother Bharata.
Now set your heart on the means by which news of Sītā may be had. ॥4॥
kishkindha.21.do21: While they were talking in this way, the troops of monkeys arrived.
Hosts of monkeys of many colours could be seen in every direction. ॥21॥
kishkindha.22.cau1: Umā, I saw that monkey army; anyone who would try to count it is a fool.
They come and bow their heads at Śrī Rāma's feet, and every one of them is blessed by gazing on his face. ॥1॥
kishkindha.22.cau2: There was not one monkey in the army whose welfare Śrī Rāma did not ask after.
This is nothing great for the Lord: Śrī Rāma has the universe for his form and pervades all. ॥2॥
kishkindha.22.cau3: At his command they took their places here and there, and Sugrīva instructed them all, saying:
This is Śrī Rāma's work and my request: go, you troops of monkeys, in every direction. ॥3॥
kishkindha.22.cau4: Go and search for Janaka's daughter, and come back within a month, brothers.
Whoever lets the time run out and returns without news will end up being put to death by me. ॥4॥
kishkindha.22.do22: As soon as they heard his words, all the monkeys set off at once in every direction.
Then Sugrīva called Aṅgada, Nala and Hanumān. ॥22॥
kishkindha.23.cau1: Sugrīva said: Listen, Nīla, Aṅgada, Hanumān, and wise Jāmbavān of steady mind:
all of you, fine warriors, go south together and ask everyone for news of Sītā. ॥1॥
kishkindha.23.cau2: In thought, deed and word, think out the means by which Śrī Rāma's work may be accomplished.
One should take the sun on one's back and a fire on one's breast, but serve one's master with one's whole being, free of deceit. ॥2॥
kishkindha.23.cau3: Leaving māyā aside, one should look to the world beyond; then every sorrow born of worldly existence is wiped away.
Brothers, this is the fruit of having a body: to give up every desire and worship Śrī Rāma. ॥3॥
kishkindha.23.cau4: He alone knows true worth, he alone is fortunate, who loves the feet of Śrī Rāma.
Asking leave and bowing their heads at his feet, they set off joyfully, remembering Śrī Rāma. ॥4॥
kishkindha.23.cau5: Last of all Hanumān, son of the Wind, bowed his head, and the Lord, knowing the work would be done by him, called him close.
Laying his lotus hand on Hanumān's head, he gave him his signet ring, for he knew him as his own. ॥5॥
kishkindha.23.cau6: The Lord said: Comfort Sītā in every way, tell her of my strength and my longing, and come back quickly.
Hanumān counted his birth fulfilled and set off holding the treasury of mercy in his heart. ॥6॥
kishkindha.23.cau7: Though the Lord, protector of the gods, knows everything, he keeps to the ways of statecraft. ॥7॥
kishkindha.23.do23: They all went on, searching forests, rivers, lakes, mountains and caves,
their minds wholly absorbed in Śrī Rāma's work, forgetting all care for their own bodies. ॥23॥
kishkindha.24.cau1: Any demon they ran into anywhere lost his life to a single slap.
They searched the mountains and forests in many ways, and if they met a sage, they all crowded round him. ॥1॥
kishkindha.24.cau2: Thirst came upon them and they grew desperate; there was no water anywhere, and the thick forest left them lost.
Hanumān judged in his mind that without water to drink they would all soon die. ॥2॥
kishkindha.24.cau3: Climbing a mountain peak, he looked all around and saw a marvel at a cave in the ground:
cakravākas, herons and swans were flying up, and many birds were going inside. ॥3॥
kishkindha.24.cau4: Hanumān, son of the Wind, climbed down and led the whole band to the cave to show it to them.
Putting Hanumān in front, they went into the cave without delay. ॥4॥
kishkindha.24.do24: Once inside, they came upon a splendid garden and a lake bright with many open lotuses.
A lovely abode was there, where a woman was seated, a very mass of austerity. ॥24॥
kishkindha.25.cau1: Keeping their distance, they bowed their heads to her; she questioned them, and they told her all that had befallen them.
Then she said: Drink water, and eat the many kinds of fine, juicy fruit. ॥1॥
kishkindha.25.cau2: They bathed and ate the sweet fruit, then all came back to her.
She told them her whole story and said: Now I shall go to where Śrī Rāma is. ॥2॥
kishkindha.25.cau3: Close your eyes and leave the cave; you will find Sītā, so do not despair.
The heroes closed their eyes, and when they looked again they were all standing on the shore of the ocean. ॥3॥
kishkindha.25.cau4: She then went to where Śrī Rāma was, and bowed her head at his lotus feet.
Many were the prayers she offered, and the Lord blessed her with unfailing devotion. ॥4॥
kishkindha.25.do25: Taking the Lord's command upon her head, she went to the forest of Badarī,
holding in her heart the two feet of Śrī Rāma to which Brahmā and Śiva bow. ॥25॥
kishkindha.26.cau1: Here the monkeys were thinking to themselves that the time allowed was over and nothing had been done.
Gathering together, they said to one another: Brothers, what are we to do without news? ॥1॥
kishkindha.26.cau2: Aṅgada said, his eyes brimming with tears: Either way, death is upon us.
No news of Sītā has been found here, and back there the king of the monkeys will put us to death. ॥2॥
kishkindha.26.cau3: When my father was slain, he would have killed me; it was Śrī Rāma who saved me, no kindness of his.
Again and again Aṅgada said to them all: Death has come; there is no doubt of it. ॥3॥
kishkindha.26.cau4: Hearing Aṅgada's words, the monkey heroes could not speak; tears streamed from their eyes.
They were lost in anxious thought for a moment, and then all of them spoke up: ॥4॥
kishkindha.26.cau5: Wise prince, we will not go back without news of Sītā.
With these words the monkeys all went to the shore of the salt sea, spread darbha grass and sat down on it. ॥5॥
kishkindha.26.cau6: Seeing Aṅgada's grief, Jāmbavān told stories full of special counsel:
Dear one, do not take Śrī Rāma for a man; know him as the attributeless Brahman, unconquered and unborn. ॥6॥
kishkindha.26.cau7: All of us, his servants, are most fortunate, for we ever love Brahman with attributes. ॥7॥
kishkindha.26.do26: Of his own will the Lord comes down to earth for the sake of the gods, the earth, cows and Brahmins.
There those who worship him with form stay by his side, giving up every kind of liberation. ॥26॥
kishkindha.27.cau1: In this way the tale was told in many ways, and in his cave on the mountain Sampāti heard it.
Coming out, he saw a great many monkeys and thought: The Lord of the world has given me food. ॥1॥
kishkindha.27.cau2: Today I will eat them all. Many days have gone by, and I am dying for want of food.
I never get food enough to fill my belly; today the Creator has given it all at once. ॥2॥
kishkindha.27.cau3: When their ears caught the vulture's words, they were afraid: Now we know that death has truly come.
Seeing the vulture, all the monkeys stood up, and Jāmbavān was deeply troubled in mind. ॥3॥
kishkindha.27.cau4: Aṅgada thought it over in his mind and said: Blessed is Jaṭāyu; there is none like him.
That most fortunate one gave up his body for Śrī Rāma's work and went to Śrī Hari's abode. ॥4॥
kishkindha.27.cau5: Hearing words that held both joy and grief, the bird came near, and the monkeys were afraid.
He went up, assured them they had nothing to fear and asked them, and they told him the whole story. ॥5॥
kishkindha.27.cau6: Hearing what his brother had done, Sampāti spoke of Śrī Rāma's greatness in many ways. ॥6॥
kishkindha.27.do27: Sampāti said: Take me to the seashore, so that I may offer him water and sesame.
I will help you with words; you will find the one you are searching for. ॥27॥
kishkindha.28.cau1: After performing the rites for his younger brother on the seashore, Sampāti told his own story: Listen, brave monkeys.
In our early youth we two brothers flew up into the sky, close to the sun. ॥1॥
kishkindha.28.cau2: The blaze was too much for him and he came back; I was proud, and flew on until I was near the sun.
The boundless blaze burned my wings, and with a terrible shriek I fell to the earth. ॥2॥
kishkindha.28.cau3: There was a sage there called Candramā; when he saw me, pity stirred in him.
He taught me wisdom in many ways and freed me from the pride that comes of the body. ॥3॥
kishkindha.28.cau4: The sage said: In the Tretā age Brahman will take a human body, and the king of the demons will carry off his wife.
The Lord will send messengers to search for her; meeting them, you will be made pure. ॥4॥
kishkindha.28.cau5: Your wings will grow again, so do not worry; you are to show them Sītā.
Today the sage's words have come true. Now listen to what I say and do the Lord's work. ॥5॥
kishkindha.28.cau6: Laṅkā stands on Mount Trikūṭa, and there lives Rāvaṇa, fearless by nature.
There is the Aśoka grove where Sītā stays; she sits there, lost in grief. ॥6॥
kishkindha.28.do28: I can see her; you cannot, for a vulture's sight has no bounds.
I have grown old, or I too would have given you some help. ॥28॥
kishkindha.29.cau1: Śrī Rāma's work will be done by one rich in wisdom who can leap across the ocean, a hundred yojanas wide.
Look at me and take heart: see what Śrī Rāma's grace has made of my body. ॥1॥
kishkindha.29.cau2: His name, remembered, carries even sinners across the utterly boundless ocean of worldly existence;
you are his messengers. Cast off faint-heartedness, keep Śrī Rāma in your hearts and find a way. ॥2॥
kishkindha.29.cau3: Garuḍa, when the vulture had said this and gone, the monkeys were filled with wonder.
Each told of his own strength, but each had doubts about getting across. ॥3॥
kishkindha.29.cau4: Jāmbavān, king of the bears, said: I am old now; there is not a trace left in my body of the strength I once had.
At the time Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara, became Trivikrama, I was young and of great strength. ॥4॥
kishkindha.29.do29: When the Lord grew as he bound Bali, his body became too vast to describe.
Within two ghaṛīs (under an hour) I ran round it seven times. ॥29॥
kishkindha.30.cau1: Aṅgada said: I could get across, but I have some doubt in my mind about coming back.
Jāmbavān said: You are fit for everything, but you are the leader of all of us; how can we send you? ॥1॥
kishkindha.30.cau2: Jāmbavān, king of the bears, said: Listen, Hanumān. Why have you fallen silent, mighty one?
You are the son of the Wind and as strong as the Wind; you are a treasury of intelligence, discernment and realised knowledge. ॥2॥
kishkindha.30.cau3: What task in the world is so hard that you cannot do it, dear one?
You were born for Śrī Rāma's work. As soon as he heard this, Hanumān became as huge as a mountain. ॥3॥
kishkindha.30.cau4: His body, the colour of gold, blazed with splendour, as though he were a second king of mountains.
Roaring like a lion again and again, he said: I could leap across the salt ocean in play. ॥4॥
kishkindha.30.cau5: I could kill Rāvaṇa along with his helpers, then uproot Trikūṭa and bring it here.
Jāmbavān, I ask you: give me fitting counsel. ॥5॥
kishkindha.30.cau6: Jāmbavān said: Dear one, go and do just this much: see Sītā, come back, and tell us how she is.
Then the lotus-eyed Lord will act by the might of his own arms; the monkey army will go with him only for the sport of it. ॥6॥
kishkindha.30.cha1: With the monkey army Śrī Rāma will destroy the demons and bring Sītā back.
Gods, sages, Nārada and others will tell of his fair fame, which makes the three worlds pure.
A person who hears it, sings it, tells it and understands it reaches the supreme state.
Tulasīdāsa, a bee hovering at Śrī Rāma's lotus feet, sings it. ॥1॥
kishkindha.30.do30क: The fame of Śrī Rāma is the remedy for worldly existence.
Men and women who listen to it have all their wishes fulfilled by Śrī Rāma, slayer of Triśirā. ॥30 (क)॥
kishkindha.30.so30ख: Dark of body as a blue lotus, more beautiful than ten million Kāmadevas:
listen to the host of virtues of him whose name is a hunter to the birds of sin. ॥30 (ख)॥
sundar.0.shloka1: I bow to him who is serene, eternal, immeasurable and sinless, the giver of the peace of liberation,
ceaselessly served by Brahmā, Śiva and Śeṣa, king of serpents, known through the Vedānta and pervading all;
who is called Rāma, the Lord of the world, teacher of the gods, Hari who through māyā (his power of illusion) appears as a man;
the mine of compassion, the best of the Raghus, the crest-jewel of kings. ॥1॥
sundar.0.shloka2: O Lord of the Raghus, there is no other longing in my heart.
This is the truth, and you dwell in all as their inner Self.
O best of the Raghus, grant me devotion in its fullness.
Make my mind free of desire and the other faults. ॥2॥
sundar.0.shloka3: I salute the son of the Wind: the home of matchless strength, his body shining like a mountain of gold,
a fire to the forest of the demons, foremost among the wise,
the treasury of every virtue, lord of the monkeys,
dear devotee of the Lord of the Raghus. ॥3॥
sundar.1.cau1: Jāmbavān's words were pleasing, and Hanumān was delighted at heart to hear them.
He said: Brothers, wait for me till then, bearing hardship and living on tubers, roots and fruit, ॥1॥
sundar.1.cau2: until I return from seeing Sītā. The work will be done; a special joy fills me.
With these words he bowed his head to everyone and, holding Śrī Rāma in his heart, set off in joy. ॥2॥
sundar.1.cau3: On the shore of the ocean stood a fine mountain. Hanumān leapt onto it for sport.
Remembering Śrī Rāma again and again, the mighty son of the Wind sprang up with tremendous force. ॥3॥
sundar.1.cau4: The mountain on which Hanumān planted his feet as he set off sank at once into the netherworld.
As Śrī Rāma's unfailing arrow flies, so Hanumān sped on. ॥4॥
sundar.1.cau5: The Ocean, considering that he was the messenger of Śrī Rāma, said: Maināka, be the one to relieve his weariness. ॥5॥
sundar.1.do1: Hanumān touched Maināka with his hand, bowed to him, and said:
Until Śrī Rāma's work is done, how can I rest? ॥1॥
sundar.2.cau1: The gods watched the son of the Wind on his way, and to find out how great his strength and wisdom were,
they sent Surasā, the mother of serpents. She came and spoke these words. ॥1॥
sundar.2.cau2: Today the gods have given me my food. On hearing her words, Hanumān said:
When I have done Śrī Rāma's work and come back and told the Lord the news of Sītā, ॥2॥
sundar.2.cau3: After that I will come and enter your mouth; this is the truth, mother, so let me go.
But on no account would she let him pass. Hanumān said: Then why do you not swallow me? ॥3॥
sundar.2.cau4: She opened her mouth a yojana wide (a yojana is some eight miles), and Hanumān made his body twice that size.
She stretched her mouth to sixteen yojanas; at once the son of the Wind grew to thirty-two. ॥4॥
sundar.2.cau5: However wide Surasā made her mouth, Hanumān showed a form twice as large.
When her mouth reached a hundred yojanas, the son of the Wind took on a very tiny form. ॥5॥
sundar.2.cau6: Going into her mouth, he came back out, then bowed his head to her and asked leave to go.
She said: The gods sent me to learn the secret of your wisdom and strength, and I have learnt it. ॥6॥
sundar.2.do2: You will accomplish all of Śrī Rāma's work, treasury of strength and wisdom that you are.
Blessing him, she went away, and Hanumān went on his way rejoicing. ॥2॥
sundar.3.cau1: A demoness lived in the ocean who caught the birds of the air by sorcery.
When creatures flew through the sky, she would see their shadows in the water ॥1॥
sundar.3.cau2: and seize the shadow, so that they could not fly away; in this way she always fed on those that travel the sky.
She tried the same trick on Hanumān, and he saw through her deceit at once. ॥2॥
sundar.3.cau3: Having killed her, the brave and steady-minded son of the Wind reached the far shore of the ocean.
Arriving there, he saw the beauty of the forest, where bees hummed, greedy for honey. ॥3॥
sundar.3.cau4: Trees of many kinds were lovely with fruit and flowers, and the flocks of birds and herds of animals delighted his heart.
Ahead of him he saw a huge mountain, and casting off fear he ran and climbed it. ॥4॥
sundar.3.cau5: Umā, in this there is no greatness of Hanumān's own; it is the glory of the Lord, which devours even Death.
Climbing the mountain, he saw Laṅkā, a fortress so extraordinary that words cannot describe it. ॥5॥
sundar.3.cau6: It is very lofty, with the ocean on all four sides, and its rampart of gold blazes with light. ॥6॥
sundar.3.cha1: Laṅkā's wall is of gold, set with gems of every colour, and within it stand many fine mansions.
With its crossroads, markets, good roads and lanes, the city is beautifully laid out in every way.
Who could count its herds of elephants, horses and mules, its foot soldiers and its many chariots?
The bands of demons who take many forms, and their army of immense strength, are beyond describing. ॥1॥
sundar.3.cha2: Woods, gardens, groves, flower gardens, lakes, wells and stepwells adorn it.
Maidens of men, nāgas, gods and gandharvas charm the minds of sages with their beauty.
In places, wrestlers of immense strength, with huge bodies like mountains, are roaring.
In many arenas they grapple and challenge one another in many ways. ॥2॥
sundar.3.cha3: Millions of warriors of fearsome build guard the city with care on all four sides.
In places the wicked demons are devouring buffaloes, humans, cows, donkeys and goats.
For this reason Tulasīdāsa has told a little of their story:
With Śrī Rāma's arrows as their place of pilgrimage they will give up their bodies and surely attain salvation. ॥3॥
sundar.3.do3: Seeing the city's many guards, Hanumān reflected:
I will take a very small form and make my way into the city by night. ॥3॥
sundar.4.cau1: Taking a form the size of a mosquito, Hanumān set out for Laṅkā, remembering the Lord in human form.
A demoness named Laṅkinī said: Are you going in without a thought for me? ॥1॥
sundar.4.cau2: You fool, do you not know my secret? Thieves, as many as there are, are all my food.
The great Hanumān struck her a single blow with his fist, and she tumbled to the ground, vomiting blood. ॥2॥
sundar.4.cau3: Then Laṅkinī recovered and rose, and with joined palms she pleaded in fear:
When Brahmā granted Rāvaṇa his boon, he told me a sign as he was leaving: ॥3॥
sundar.4.cau4: When a monkey's blow leaves you reeling, know then that the demons are destroyed.
My merit is very great, dear one, for I have seen Śrī Rāma's messenger with my own eyes. ॥4॥
sundar.4.do4: Dear one, put the joys of heaven and of liberation together on one side of a scale.
All of them together do not weigh as much as the joy of a moment in the company of the good. ॥4॥
sundar.5.cau1: Enter the city and do all your work, keeping the king of Kosala in your heart.
Poison turns to nectar, enemies act as friends, the ocean shrinks to a cow's hoofprint and fire grows cool, ॥1॥
sundar.5.cau2: and Mount Sumeru becomes like a speck of dust, Garuḍa, for one on whom Śrī Rāma has looked with grace.
Hanumān took a very small form and entered the city, remembering the Lord. ॥2॥
sundar.5.cau3: He searched palace after palace and saw countless warriors everywhere.
Then he went into the palace of Rāvaṇa, so wondrous that it cannot be described. ॥3॥
sundar.5.cau4: Hanumān saw Rāvaṇa lying asleep, but Sītā was not to be seen in that palace.
Then he saw a lovely house with a separate temple of Śrī Hari built in it. ॥4॥
sundar.5.do5: The house was marked with emblems of Śrī Rāma's weapons, and its beauty was beyond words.
Seeing clumps of fresh tulasī there, Hanumān, the best of monkeys, was overjoyed. ॥5॥
sundar.6.cau1: Laṅkā is the home of hosts of demons; how could a good person live here?
So Hanumān began to reason in his mind, and at that very moment Vibhīṣaṇa awoke. ॥1॥
sundar.6.cau2: He called the Lord to mind, saying Rāma, Rāma, and Hanumān was glad at heart, knowing him for a good man.
I will make a point of making myself known to him; a good man brings no harm to one's work. ॥2॥
sundar.6.cau3: Taking the form of a brāhmaṇa, Hanumān spoke to him, and on hearing him Vibhīṣaṇa rose and came there.
He bowed, asked after his welfare and said: Brāhmaṇa, tell me your story and make it clear. ॥3॥
sundar.6.cau4: Are you one of the servants of Śrī Hari? A great love is rising in my heart.
Or else, are you Śrī Rāma himself, who loves the humble, come to make me blessed? ॥4॥
sundar.6.do6: Then Hanumān told him all of Śrī Rāma's story, and his own name.
At this, both of them thrilled from head to foot, and remembering the Lord's many virtues their minds were lost in them. ॥6॥
sundar.7.cau1: Listen, son of the Wind, to how I live here: like the poor tongue among the teeth.
Dear one, will the Lord of the Sun's line ever know me to be without a protector and be gracious to me? ॥1॥
sundar.7.cau2: My body is tāmasic, of the nature of darkness; I have no spiritual practice, and my mind has no love for the lotus feet of the Lord.
Yet now, Hanumān, I have taken heart, for without the grace of Śrī Hari one does not meet saints. ॥2॥
sundar.7.cau3: It is because Śrī Rāma has been gracious to me that you have sought me out and shown yourself to me.
Listen, Vibhīṣaṇa, to the Lord's way: he always loves his servants. ॥3॥
sundar.7.cau4: Tell me, what high and noble birth is mine? I am a restless monkey, lowly in every way.
Whoever takes our name in the morning goes without food that day. ॥4॥
sundar.7.do7: Listen, my friend: lowly as I am, even on me Śrī Rāma has shown his grace.
As he remembered the Lord's virtues, Hanumān's eyes filled with tears. ॥7॥
sundar.8.cau1: Those who know such a master and still forget him and wander about, how should they not be miserable?
Telling thus of Śrī Rāma's many virtues, he found a peace beyond words. ॥1॥
sundar.8.cau2: Then Vibhīṣaṇa told him everything: how Janaka's daughter was living there.
Then Hanumān said: Listen, brother, I wish to see Mother Jānakī. ॥2॥
sundar.8.cau3: Vibhīṣaṇa explained every means to him, and Hanumān, son of the Wind, took leave of him and set out.
Taking the same form again, he went to the place in the Aśoka grove where Sītā was living. ॥3॥
sundar.8.cau4: Seeing her, he bowed to her in his heart. She sits on as the watches of the night go by.
Her body is wasted, her hair is a single matted braid, and in her heart she repeats Śrī Rāma's virtues one after another. ॥4॥
sundar.8.do8: Her eyes rest on her own feet, her mind is lost in Śrī Rāma's lotus feet.
Seeing Jānakī in such distress, the son of the Wind was filled with grief. ॥8॥
sundar.9.cau1: He stayed hidden among the leaves of the tree, thinking: Well, what am I to do now?
Just then Rāvaṇa came there, dressed in finery, with many women. ॥1॥
sundar.9.cau2: In many ways the wicked one tried to win Sītā over, using conciliation, gifts, intimidation and sowing discord.
Rāvaṇa said: Listen, fair-faced and clever one: Mandodarī and all my other queens ॥2॥
sundar.9.cau3: I shall make your maidservants; this is my vow. Only look my way once.
Holding up a blade of grass as a screen, and remembering her most loving lord, the king of Avadh, Sītā spoke: ॥3॥
sundar.9.cau4: Listen, Rāvaṇa: does a lotus ever open in the light of a firefly?
Sītā went on: Understand this in your mind. Wretch, you have no thought of Śrī Rāma's arrows. ॥4॥
sundar.9.cau5: Fool, you carried me off when I was left alone. Vile, shameless creature, have you no shame? ॥5॥
sundar.9.do9: Hearing himself likened to a firefly and Śrī Rāma to the sun,
and hearing such harsh words, Rāvaṇa drew his sword and, stung with fury, said: ॥9॥
sundar.10.cau1: Sītā, you have insulted me. I will cut off your head with this cruel sword.
Otherwise, do as I say at once, fair one, or you will lose your life. ॥1॥
sundar.10.cau2: Rāvaṇa, the Lord's arm is as lovely as a garland of dark lotuses, and like an elephant's trunk.
Either that arm will be around my neck or your dreadful sword. Listen, fool: this vow of mine is true. ॥2॥
sundar.10.cau3: Candrahāsa (Rāvaṇa's sword), take away my anguish, born of the fire of separation from Śrī Rāma.
Your edge is cool, keen and fine. Sītā said: Take away the weight of my sorrow. ॥3॥
sundar.10.cau4: Hearing her words, he then rushed at her to kill her, but Mandodarī, Maya's daughter, reasoned with him and gave him wise counsel.
He summoned all the demonesses and said: Go and terrify Sītā in every way you can. ॥4॥
sundar.10.cau5: If within a month she has not done as I say, then I will take my sword out and kill her. ॥5॥
sundar.10.do10: Rāvaṇa went back to his palace.
Here a band of demonesses take on many hideous forms and terrify Sītā. ॥10॥
sundar.11.cau1: One demoness, named Trijaṭā, loved Śrī Rāma's feet and was wise in discernment.
She called them all together, told them her dream and said: Serve Sītā and so do yourselves good. ॥1॥
sundar.11.cau2: In my dream a monkey burned Laṅkā and slew the whole demon army.
Rāvaṇa is riding a donkey, naked, his ten heads shaven and his twenty arms cut off. ॥2॥
sundar.11.cau3: In this state he is going towards the south, and it seems that Vibhīṣaṇa has gained Laṅkā.
Śrī Rāma's sovereignty has been proclaimed through the city, and then the Lord has sent for Sītā. ॥3॥
sundar.11.cau4: I tell you this dream aloud: within a few days it will come true.
Hearing what she said, they all grew afraid and threw themselves at the feet of the daughter of Janaka. ॥4॥
sundar.11.do11: Then they all went off this way and that, and Sītā thought anxiously:
When the month is over, the vile demon will kill me. ॥11॥
sundar.12.cau1: Sītā said to Trijaṭā, her hands folded: Mother, in my misfortune you are my companion.
Quickly find me some way to give up this body; this unbearable separation can be borne no longer. ॥1॥
sundar.12.cau2: Bring wood and build a pyre, and then, mother, set it alight.
Wise one, prove my love true. Who could bear to hear words that pierce the ears like a spike? ॥2॥
sundar.12.cau3: Hearing her words, Trijaṭā clasped her feet and comforted her, telling her of the Lord's glory, strength and fair fame.
Listen, gentle lady: at night no fire can be found. With these words she went back to her own home. ॥3॥
sundar.12.cau4: Sītā said: Fate has turned against me. I shall find no fire, and my pain will not end.
Embers are plainly to be seen in the sky, yet not a single star comes down to earth. ॥4॥
sundar.12.cau5: The moon is made of fire, yet it does not shower fire on me, as though it knew me for an unlucky one.
Hear my plea, Aśoka tree: be true to your name (Aśoka, without sorrow) and take my sorrow away. ॥5॥
sundar.12.cau6: Your new leaves are like fire: give me fire, and do not drive my suffering to its last extreme.
Seeing Sītā so overwhelmed by separation, Hanumān felt that moment pass like an aeon. ॥6॥
sundar.12.so12: Then Hanumān, having thought it over in his heart, dropped the ring down to her.
It was as if the Aśoka had given her an ember: she rose joyfully and caught it up in her hand. ॥12॥
sundar.13.cau1: Then she saw the lovely ring, engraved with Śrī Rāma's name and exceedingly beautiful.
Recognising it, she gazed at it in wonder, her heart stirred by joy and sorrow together. ॥1॥
sundar.13.cau2: Who could defeat Śrī Rāma, the unconquerable? And no magic illusion could make a ring like this.
While Sītā turned many thoughts over in her mind, Hanumān spoke in a sweet voice. ॥2॥
sundar.13.cau3: He began to describe Śrī Rāma's virtues, and as soon as she heard them Sītā's sorrow fled.
She listened with ears and mind intent, and he told her the whole story, starting from the very beginning. ॥3॥
sundar.13.cau4: The one who has told this lovely story, nectar to the ears, why does he not show himself, brother?
Then Hanumān came close to her. She turned her face away and sat, wondering in her mind. ॥4॥
sundar.13.cau5: Mother Jānakī, I am the messenger of Śrī Rāma; I swear it truly by the Lord, the treasury of compassion.
Mother, I brought this ring: Śrī Rāma gave it so that you would know me by it. ॥5॥
sundar.13.cau6: Tell me, how did man and monkey come together? And he told her the story of how that companionship had come about. ॥6॥
sundar.13.do13: Hearing Hanumān's loving words, Sītā felt trust rise in her heart.
She knew that he was a servant, in thought, deed and word, of the ocean of mercy. ॥13॥
sundar.14.cau1: Recognising him as a devotee of Hari, Sītā felt a deep and intense love; tears came to her eyes, and the hair on her body stood on end.
Hanumān, dear one, I was drowning in the ocean of separation, and you have become a ship for me. ॥1॥
sundar.14.cau2: Now tell me, and may I be a sacrifice for you, how Śrī Rāma, slayer of Khara and home of joy, fares with his younger brother.
Śrī Rāma is tender-hearted and compassionate; why, Hanumān, has he put on such hardness? ॥2॥
sundar.14.cau3: Does Śrī Rāma, whose very nature it is to give joy to his servants, ever think of me?
Dear one, will my eyes ever be cooled by gazing on his dark and tender form? ॥3॥
sundar.14.cau4: No words would come, and her eyes filled with tears: Alas, my Lord, you have forgotten me utterly!
Seeing Sītā so overwhelmed by the pain of separation, Hanumān spoke to her gently and humbly. ॥4॥
sundar.14.cau5: Mother, the Lord is well, and his younger brother with him; but he, the abode of grace, grieves at your grief.
Mother, do not be downcast at heart: Śrī Rāma's love is twice as great as yours. ॥5॥
sundar.14.do14: Mother, take heart now and listen to Śrī Rāma's message.
Saying this, Hanumān was overcome, his voice faltering and his eyes brimming with tears. ॥14॥
sundar.15.cau1: This is what Śrī Rāma said: Sītā, in separation from you, all things have turned contrary for me.
The trees' new leaves seem like fire, night is like the night of doom, and the moon like the sun. ॥1॥
sundar.15.cau2: Beds of blue lotuses seem a forest of spears, and the clouds seem to rain boiling oil.
Things that once did me good now give me pain, and the breeze, cool, gentle and fragrant, is like a serpent's breath. ॥2॥
sundar.15.cau3: Grief grows a little lighter even by being told, but whom shall I tell? No one understands it.
Beloved, the truth of the love between you and me is known to my mind alone. ॥3॥
sundar.15.cau4: And that mind stays always with you; from this much alone, know the essence of my love.
Hearing the Lord's message, Sītā was so immersed in love that she was no longer aware of her body. ॥4॥
sundar.15.cau5: Hanumān said: Mother, take heart, and remember Śrī Rāma, who gives joy to his servants.
Call to mind the majesty of Śrī Rāma, and hearing my words, give up your faint-heartedness. ॥5॥
sundar.15.do15: The demon hordes are like moths, and Śrī Rāma's arrows like fire.
